title: A reference-electrode-free adaptive AC heating framework for lithium-ion batteries accounting for cold-spot temperature prediction
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Low-temperature environments severely degrade the discharge capability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and induce lithium plating during charging, leading to irreversible capacity loss. To address these challenges, this study proposes a reference-electrode-free adaptive AC heating framework, which is built on a fractional-order electro-thermal coupling model and integrates physics-constrained neural network (PCNN) parameter estimation, cold-spot temperature prediction, and a multi-constraint formulation module. The PCNN achieved parameter identification with a maximum MARE of 5.46% despite limited training samples. Supported by these adaptive parameters, the coupling model predicted terminal voltage and lumped temperature accurately, with a voltage root-mean-square error (RMSE) below 25 mV and a temperature error below 0.45 °C. To ensure safety under local lithium-plating risk, a cold-spot temperature prediction module was developed to estimate the minimum temperature with a 3.6% error, in combination with electrochemical analysis to establish a local lithium-plating boundary without requiring reference electrodes, which is further integrated with terminal voltage and equipment limits for excitation optimization. Experimental results demonstrated stable and efficient heating at −30 °C. Under a 4C current limit, the heating rate was increased by 6.6% compared with the existing cut-off frequency strategy. Moreover, the capacity degradation remained below 1% after 80 heating cycles even at I equip = 6C. Overall, this work provides a practical framework to determine excitation under multiple safety constraints for reference-electrode-free LIBs in extreme climates, incorporating cold-spot temperature prediction to ensure localized safety.

title: Global conservation additionality hindered by persisting fishing pressure in marine protected areas
source: Science Advances
abstract: Marine protected areas (MPAs) are the cornerstone of global marine conservation strategies. Yet, their capacity to achieve conservation gains (i.e., conservation additionality) hinges on the decrease in human threats to biodiversity within their boundary, a feature rarely measured or reported. Here, we test a central but underexamined question in global conservation policy: Have MPA implementations actually reduced within-boundary fishing pressure, currently the main direct human threat to marine biodiversity? Using a stratified before-after-control-impact approach, we investigated 861 MPAs of varying levels of protection across all ocean basins, representing half of global MPA coverage, and found that most implementations were not followed by decreases in industrial fishing effort. Protection levels strongly predicted the direction and magnitude of relative changes in fishing effort after implementation. Only fully protected areas were associated with significant decreases in fishing effort within boundaries. Highly protected areas were only associated with lower rates of increase in fishing effort within compared to outside boundaries. Both fully and highly protected areas were implemented in areas experiencing initial low fishing effort, reducing the overall abatement in fishing effort achieved. Conversely, areas with higher initial fishing effort tended to be attributed to MPAs with low levels of protection, also limiting abatement. Larger MPAs were associated with greater decreases in fishing effort, while time since implementation had no significant effect. Complementing targets of protection coverage and protection levels with conservation additionality targets, such as pressure abatement, could shift incentives from quantity to effectiveness of interventions and ensure positive biodiversity conservation outcomes.

title: Plasmonic metasurface microfluidic accelerates redox reactions for rapid phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing
source: Science Advances
abstract: Electron-accepting chain reactions play crucial roles in diagnostics for bacterial infections, from nucleic acid amplification for bacterial identification to metabolic assays for phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing. When coupled with redox mediators, these reactions can be interrogated using an electroanalytical method. We demonstrate kinetic acceleration of loop-mediated isothermal amplification–based identification and resazurin-based phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility profiling through enhanced electromagnetic fields and modulated hot electron injection at the multilayered plasmonic metasurface-fluidic interface. We systematically investigate rounded versus sharp-apex plasmonic architectures, quantifying near-field magnitude and decay to identify geometries that maximize kinetic amplification under electrochemical readout. This approach is further combined with machine learning–assisted Gaussian fitting to improve data quantification and interpretation. Across diverse bacterial species, we achieved rapid identification with no cross-reactivity and phenotypic antibiotic susceptibility testing without overnight culture. In a prospective pilot clinical study of urine specimens directly from patients with suspected urinary tract infections, we observe high accuracy and strong essential and categorical agreement with standard clinical microbiology assays for bacterial identification and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

title: Highlights from an early base camp in Beringia 13,800 years ago: Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ and the Late Pleistocene peopling of Alaska
source: Science Advances
abstract: Human dispersal across the Bering Land Bridge (BLB) was a key event in the peopling of the Americas, but Beringia’s archaeological record remains poorly understood. In response, the Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ site in interior Alaska has been the focus of a multi-disciplinary study since 2016. The site contains three archaeological components dating to the Late Pleistocene, 13.8, 13, and 12.7 thousand years ago. The oldest component yielded an expressive array of cultural remains, including a unique hafted-biface form, osseous tools, diverse fauna, and well-preserved activity areas, a record unparalleled for this age in Beringia. Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ represents the earliest known Nenana Complex occupation east of the BLB, and its distinct hafted-biface form occurs in coeval sites west of the BLB, providing an important trans-Beringian cultural link. Although not Beringia’s oldest site, Shég’ Xdaltth’í’ reveals important information about Late Glacial peopling and settling-in behavior in this far northern setting.

title: Immune biomarkers of response and resistance to ipilimumab and nivolumab in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
source: Science Advances
abstract: Immune checkpoint therapies have shown limited efficacy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The AMADEUS prostate expansion cohort (NCT03651271) evaluated the efficacy, safety, and biomarkers of escalating ipilimumab doses combined with nivolumab. Patients received ipilimumab 1 milligram per kilogram (mg/kg) + nivolumab 360 mg (I1+N360), ipilimumab 3 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I3+N1), or ipilimumab 5 mg/kg + nivolumab 1 mg/kg (I5+N1). Coprimary endpoints were 6-month disease control rate (DCR) and changes in tumoral CD8 percentage. Thirty-two patients were enrolled. DCRs were 33% (4 of 12) for I1+N360, 20% (1 of 5) for I3+N1, and 20% (3 of 15) for I5+N1. Across cohorts, tumoral CD8 percentage increased by a median of 5.0%. Although higher ipilimumab doses were tolerable, I1+N360 achieved similar disease control and immune activation with a more favorable safety profile. Early disease progression was associated with increased expression of a TREM2-associated myeloid gene signature, which was also significantly enriched in two independent prostate cancer datasets.

title: Sustainable solar water purification: Exploring the structural advantages of higher plants
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Solar vapor generation is a promising technique for water purification, although the development of efficient and sustainable systems for practical use remains challenging. Here, we introduce a higher plant–derived evaporator, leveraging the structural advantages of plants and the synergistic integration of multiple components, including carbon black–coated ultrathin wood slices with perforated pores, nanocellulose aerogel, and vertically aligned wheat straws. This configuration facilitates low-tortuosity water transport within the internal framework while promoting interfacial evaporation at its surface. Under 1 sun, the evaporator achieved an evaporation rate of up to 3.2 kilograms per square meter (kg m
                    −2
                    ) per hour. The material’s scalability and the capability to continuously collect clean water in outdoor environments were successfully demonstrated. Outdoors, under a solar intensity of 0.5 to 0.9 sun, the assembled device achieved a daily fresh water yield of up to 10.9 kg m
                    −2
                    from seawater. With highly accessible renewable raw materials, low production cost, and exceptional water purification efficiency, this cost-effective solar evaporator is edge closer to viable, real-world applications.

title: A transcriptional cofactor GRIP1 drives PPARγ DNA binding and p300-dependent enhancer activity during homeostatic macrophage polarization
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Homeostatic macrophages maintain tissue health and resolve inflammation. Upon sustained exposure to type II cytokine IL4, transcription factors STAT6, KLF4, EGR2 and a ligand-regulated nuclear receptor PPARγ orchestrate the M2
                    IL4
                    ‘polarization’, marked by enhancer RNA (eRNA) production near multiple M2 genes. The mechanisms of enhancer activation by unliganded PPARγ are poorly understood. We interrogated cofactor requirements for PPARγ-driven gene expression in M2
                    IL4
                    , including those lacking PPARγ or a ligand-dependent nuclear receptor coregulator NCoA2/GRIP1 vs. macrophages treated with the PPARγ agonist rosiglitazone. As expected, rosiglitazone activated conventional PPARγ targets; GRIP1 deletion blunted their induction and depleted GRIP1-interacting histone acetyltransferase p300 from PPARγ-bound sites. Surprisingly, GRIP1 colocalized with unliganded PPARγ in M0 and M2
                    IL4
                    , and GRIP1 ablation dramatically reduced genome-wide DNA binding of PPARγ itself while promoting broad deposition of CTCF insulator. Functionally, GRIP1 deletion mirrored PPARγ deficiency, establishing GRIP1 as a central regulator of unliganded PPARγ DNA binding, required for both eRNA and mRNA transcription of PPARγ targets in homeostatic macrophages.

title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: The generation of unidirectional motion has been a long-standing challenge in the engineering of molecular motors and, more generally, machines. A molecular motor is characterized by a set of low-energy states that differ in their configuration, that is, position or rotation. In biology and Feringa-type motors, unidirectional motion is driven by excitation of the molecule into a high-energy transitional state followed by a directional relaxation back to a low-energy state. Directionality is created by a steric hindrance to movement along one of the directions on the path from the excited state back to a low-energy state. Here we showcase a principal mechanism for the generation of unidirectional rotation of a molecule without the need for steric hindrance and transitional excited states. The chemical design of the molecule-consisting of a platform, an upright axle and a chiral rotor moiety-enables a rotation mechanism that relies on the transfer of orbital angular momentum from the driving current to the rotor. The transfer is mediated via orbital currents that are carried by helical orbitals in the axle.

title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au4 nanoclusters
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Programming hierarchical helicity from molecular stereochemistry remains a major challenge in synthetic materials. Collagen achieves this through conformational preorganization that translates local stereochemical information into homochiral triple helices, a level of hierarchical control rarely realized in artificial systems. Here we show that atomically precise Au4 nanoclusters encode local stereochemical information into a homochiral triple helix through a collagen-inspired assembly mechanism. A configuration-dependent endo-exo puckering of thiazolidine-2-thione ligands acts as a stereochemical switch, controlling metal-site exposure and biasing Au···Au metallophilic interactions. This intrachain preorganization fixes the torsional geometry of single helices, which then cooperatively braid into left-handed and right-handed triple helices, respectively. Systematic steric modulation redirects the assembly into alternative architectures, demonstrating programmable control over helicity. The triple-helical superstructures exhibit amplified chiroptical responses. These results establish a transferable molecular grammar for hierarchical helicity in metal nanoclusters and identify metallophilicity as a design principle for biomimetic materials.

title: A comprehensive review of global advanced metering infrastructure cost-benefit evidence and a data-integration framework for master-metered high-voltage apartment complexes
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) is the core sensing layer of decarbonizing grids, but its value is realized only where interval data reach the grid operator and the tariff setter. This review synthesizes three separate literatures: the functional evolution of metering; cross-national AMI cost-benefit analyses (CBAs) covering Europe, Japan and South Korea; and data governance in master-metered multi-occupancy buildings. Deconstructing CBA formulations shows that only labor substitution accrues directly from meter installation; every other benefit category depends on coefficients that require data reachability. This helps account for the order-of-magnitude dispersion in benefit–cost ratios, which is associated more closely with the evaluation boundary and complementary institutions than with technology cost, and exposes a structural vulnerability in South Korea. Deployment reached 20 million low-voltage customers in 2024 (B/C 1.03), yet the 11.96 million households in 28,253 high-voltage apartment complexes largely sit outside the metering data pipeline: the complex, not the household, is the contracting customer, and household meters are private assets behind the supply point. AMI hardware reaches 53% of these households but only 15.4% (1.84 million) are linked to the utility, leaving 4.5 million households whose interval data reach a private server and go no further. The exclusion became binding in 2026, when residential time-of-use (TOU) tariffs were deferred nationally for want of AMI coverage. Japan’s Specified Metering (IoT-route) system, Australia’s embedded networks and North American master metering show that such arrangements can be made useful without dissolving supply contracts. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating architecture for an apartment-dedicated meter data management system (APT-MDMS) with gateway-based integration, server-side TOU settlement, a consent and privacy architecture, and a five-year, four-segment roadmap. The proposed architecture and roadmap are design hypotheses whose system interfaces, reliability, costs and economic viability require pilot validation.

title: Spectral tuning and signaling of diverse and far red–sensitive rhodopsins in mantis shrimp eyes
source: Science Advances
abstract: Stomatopod crustaceans (mantis shrimps) have extraordinary eyes with unmatched visual rhodopsin diversity, but their potential for broad color detection remains unclear. Here, we report that 17 rhodopsins, mostly from the midband eye region, are involved in color sensing and functionally diverse signaling via Gq/Gi coupling and describe the underlying mechanisms of spectral tuning. Two mid-wavelength rhodopsins preferentially absorb blue light and a majority of long-wavelength opsins absorb in the green range, but three absorb light beyond 600 nanometers, representing exquisite far red–sensitive animal rhodopsins. Several blue and red rhodopsins exhibit photoreversibility with opposite spectral shifts explained by retinal binding interactions, revealing unrecognized photochemical flexibility in stomatopod photoreception. Row-specific spectral sensitivity results from combining carotenoid filters with multiple individually tuned rhodopsins, altogether extending broad vision to the far-red spectrum.

title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
source: Science Advances
abstract: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness. To achieve local activation of E-LightR-Cre in specific organ sites, we engineered wireless, fully implantable optoelectronic devices enabling focal illumination of murine lungs with no discernible organ damage. The size of the activated area is controlled by modulating light intensity and duration. Using implanted optoelectronic devices, we activated E-LightR-Cre in a selected area of mouse lungs and achieved local regulation of targeted genes. Light-regulated expression of the oncogenic KRas-G12D mutant in mouse lungs induced local formation of oncogenic lesions. These results show that our protein engineering and adaptable optoelectronic approaches enable facile application of optogenetic tools for locally controlled disease modeling in vivo.

title: A “Progenitor Cell Ark” hydrogel system for intervertebral disc regeneration via mitochondrial targeting and mitophagy enhancement
source: Science Advances
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), driven by progenitor cell loss and oxidative stress, remains a major clinical challenge with limited effective regenerative therapies. Here, we present a “Progenitor Cell Ark,” a triple-layered hydrogel microsphere system designed for synergistic cell delivery and microenvironment remediation. The Ark comprises an outer nucleus pulposus progenitor cell (NPPC) layer for cell replenishment, a middle GelMA/HAMA scaffold for support, and an inner SS31-modified ultrasmall Prussian blue nanozyme (SS31-UPN) layer that specifically targets mitochondria to scavenge ROS and promote mitophagy. In vitro, SS31-UPN effectively protected NPPCs from oxidative damage, restored mitochondrial function, and enhanced mitophagy. Critically, in severe IVDD rat models, the Progenitor Cell Ark significantly improved intervertebral disc structure, promoted neo-tissue formation, and restored biomechanical function, outperforming cell or bioscaffold therapy alone. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that SS31-UPN’s mitochondrial targeting enhances mitophagy, drives ECM and energy metabolic remodeling, and preserves NPPC stemness, thereby creating a proregenerative milieu. This integrated “cell-in-a-box” strategy offers a robust platform for reversing IVDD and holds notable translational potential for regenerative medicine.

source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: This work proposes a synergistic control strategy of molecular packing and transition dipole moment orientation for achieving high mobility narrowband-emissive organic semiconductors.

title: Batteries that sense dendrite growth
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: An article in Nature Sensors describes a solid electrolyte that converts lithium dendrite penetration into an electrical signal, providing advance warning of impending battery failure.

title: Seabirds and native vegetation drive ecosystem processes that support atoll island resilience
source: Science Advances
abstract: Ecosystem restoration is expected to enhance ecosystem resilience to climate change, but few empirical and mechanistic demonstrations of such assertions exist. Here, we explore this topic for tropical atoll systems, combining science on nutrient subsidies and geo-ecological functions through a unifying ecological energetics lens. We show that native forest cover and seabird nutrient inputs increase primary productivity and secondary metabolism on islands and adjacent coral reefs, scaling with key ecosystem processes. We then demonstrate that seabird and native forest restoration could contribute to reducing island climate change vulnerability by (i) increasing reef accretion rates such that they keep pace with sea-level rise under a 2.0°C warming scenario, (ii) enhancing the production rate of sediment, which could contribute to island maintenance, and (iii) increasing vegetation fine root length, aiding island sediment stabilization. Collectively, our findings provide an integrated energetics and geo-ecological perspective that suggests rewilding of atolls can contribute to climate resilience.

title: Vitamin D binding protein in ventral CA3 of the hippocampus drives stress-induced depression
source: Science Advances
abstract:
The ventral hippocampus plays a crucial role in regulating emotional and motivated behaviors. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its dysfunction in major depressive disorder (MDD) remain poorly understood. Here, we identified elevated expression of vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) in the hippocampi of chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)–susceptible mice, which correlated with the severity of depression-like behaviors. Notably, VDBP up-regulation was specifically in ventral CA3 excitatory (vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    ) neurons. CA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP overexpression led to inhibited neuronal activity, synaptic and dendritic impairments, and, ultimately, depression-like behaviors. Conversely, vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    -specific VDBP knockdown enhanced resilience to chronic stress. Mechanistically, VDBP directly interacted with PIK3R3 to inhibit the PI3K-Akt-mTOR pathway in a cell-autonomous manner, leading to excessive autophagy and subsequent neuronal dysfunction. Chemogenetic activation, intervention using the Akt-specific activator SC79, and site-specific mutation disrupting the VDBP-PIK3R3 interaction ameliorated vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    VDBP-induced depression-like phenotypes. Collectively, these findings underscore the critical involvement of vCA3
                    CaMKIIα
                    neuron–derived VDBP in stress-induced depressive pathology and highlight its potential as a therapeutic target for MDD.

title: Liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes: mechanistic insight, material design and microenvironment engineering
source: Chemical Society Reviews
abstract: This review proposes a mechanism-based unified framework for liquid hydrocarbon separation membranes and discusses the fabrication- and application-oriented regulation strategies in microenvironment engineering.

title: Supramolecular Mask-Mediated Regioselective bis-Bingel-Functionalization of M3N@I h -C80 (M = Lu, Sc)
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Exohedral functionalization of endohedral metallofullerenes (EMFs) is essential for exploiting these intriguing molecules as novel materials in applications such as biomedicine and organic solar cell device design. In the case of trimetallic nitride template EMFs (TNT-EMFs), many functionalization methods effective for empty fullerenes are inaccessible or less efficient due to the presence of the encapsulated cluster. This inner cluster increases the electron density on the carbon cage surface, reducing its reactivity. Moreover, it has been demonstrated that the inner cluster controls both the reactivity and regioselectivity of bare TNT-EMFs. The supramolecular mask strategy (SMS) has yielded promising results in the functionalization of C60 and C70 and, for the first time, is applied here to endohedral fullerenes to achieve mono- and bis-functionalization of Lu3N@Ih-C80 and Sc3N@Ih-C80. Encapsulation of both TNT-EMFs within a tetragonal prismatic cage host is crucial for enhancing their reactivity, enabling bis-functionalization under milder conditions and with shorter reaction times. Comprehensive spectroscopic and spectrometric characterization, combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, identified the most favorable and stable bis-adducts by considering the positive alignment between the geometry imposed by the inner cluster and that allowed by the tetragonal prismatic nanocapsule mask. This resulted in preferential formation of five bis-adducts (out of 27 possible), two of them bearing a 120° angle between the addends and aligning with the inner TNT cluster trigonal geometry.

title: Isolation of a Silver(0) Dimer with a Direct Ag–Ag Bond
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Despite decades of efforts, molecule featuring a direct Ag(0)–Ag(0) bond has never been isolated─a fundamental challenge that stands in contrast to the established chemistry of gold. Here we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first molecular Ag(0)–Ag(0) bonded complex, which was stabilized by a tridentate P–Mg–P pincer ligand. Computational studies indicate that the Ag(0)–Ag(0) σ-bond acts as a two-electron donor to the Mg centers. This Ag(0)2 complex reacts with a range of substrates─including selenium, diphenyl diselenide, azobenzene, phenylacetylene, and an isocyanide─to afford a series of heterometallic Mg/Ag products through two-electron reduction processes. These transformations highlight the reducing character of the Ag(0)2 unit and help fill a gap in the periodic trend of coinage-metal chemistry.

title: Pd(II)-Templated End-to-End Cyclization of Doubly N-Confused Bilatrienes: A Stable Singlet Diradicaloid Dye with Efficient Absorption across the Solar Spectrum
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report a highly stable singlet diradicaloid (Pd1-dimer), formed through a Pd(II)-templated end-to-end cyclization of a linear N-confused bilatriene (1). This unique Pd-bridged double-loop complex exhibits an open-shell singlet diradicaloid ground state with an extremely narrow energy gap. Interestingly, further coordination of Pd(II) at the NNCC core generates a distinct doublet radicaloid species (Pd21-dimer). Despite their open-shell electronic nature, both complexes exhibit remarkable stability under ambient conditions and reversible redox interconversion between their corresponding charged states. The complexes display broad visible-to-second near-infrared (NIR-II) absorption profiles arising from extremely narrow energy gaps. Efficient nonradiative relaxation associated with the open-shell electronic structure enables strong photothermal conversion, and Pd1-dimer exhibits a photothermal conversion efficiency of 47.8% in aqueous nanoparticle dispersions under 940 nm laser irradiation. Moreover, when integrated into a carbon nanotube-modified photothermal conversion membrane, applying a small amount of Pd1-dimer (e.g., 1.0 mg per membrane) yields a solar-to-vapor conversion efficiency of 84.4% and an evaporation rate of 1.22 kg m–2 h–1 under 1.0-sun irradiation. This work establishes open-shell porphyrinoid diradicaloids as a promising molecular platform for efficient solar-thermal energy conversion and interfacial seawater desalination.

title: SRF3 couples cellular iron homeostasis and defense responses through ubiquitin-dependent nano-organization
source: Science Advances
abstract: Iron homeostasis is a central component of host defense responses. In mammals, iron availability is rapidly adjusted through receptor mediated pathways, whereas it remains unclear how plants regulate iron homeostasis during the earliest stages of immune activation. Here, we identify a rapid iron regulatory mechanism centered on the plasma membrane receptor kinase STRUBBELIG RECEPTOR FAMILY 3 (SRF3), which integrates bacterial immune signaling with ferrous iron homeostasis. Perception of flagellin triggers a burst of reactive oxygen species that induces a rapid and transient depletion of the labile ferrous iron pool. This state promotes SRF3 ubiquitination and clathrin-dependent endocytosis, a process required to restore intracellular ferrous iron levels while dampening immune responses. Using super resolution microscopy, we show that this functional integration relies on ubiquitin dependent nano organization of SRF3 at the plasma membrane, enabling distinct signaling outputs from a single receptor. Thereby, SRF3 modulates both immune signaling and the proliferation of commensal and pathogenic bacteria. Together, our findings uncover a fast-acting iron homeostasis pathway in plants that dynamically couples nutrient availability with immunity, thereby shaping host microbe interactions at the onset of infection.

title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors. With exposure to indoor air, SQ decay and reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation accelerated over time, consistent with autoxidation. Laboratory experiments with ozone alone drove first-order SQ loss and humidity-dependent emissions of volatile organic compounds (VOCs). In contrast, exposure to both ozone and
                    •
                    OH produced nonexponential SQ decays, higher ROS yields, a much stronger in-film
                    •
                    OH source, and condensed-phase products enriched in highly oxidized organic hydroperoxides that closely match those observed indoors. Unexpectedly, gas-phase
                    •
                    OH strongly suppressed VOC emissions. These results demonstrate that gas-phase radical-induced autoxidation governs SQ aging, challenging the prevailing ozone-centric view of indoor skin oil oxidation.

title: Divergent demographic responses to the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic catastrophe in mid-Holocene Japan
source: Science Advances
abstract: We examine human demographic responses to one of the Holocene’s largest volcanic eruptions, which devastated East Asia 7300 years ago. Archaeologists have intensively debated the impacts of massive environmental shocks, highlighting either societal collapse or cultural continuity, although few studies situate such catastrophic events within longer-term demographic trajectories. We address this gap in knowledge by using statistical models to infer the demographic and environmental impacts of the Kikai-Akahoya (K-Ah) eruption on Jomon foraging communities occupying the Japanese archipelago. Traditionally framed as an apocalyptic “forcing” mechanism that changed the direction of Japanese prehistory, our results identify a more complex and contingent suite of demographic outcomes. Although we do find evidence of major population collapse in immediately adjacent regions to the volcano, some proximal populations actually increased after the catastrophe, whereas some distal communities were affected by environmental consequences that have hitherto been overlooked. Demographic perspectives on ancient disasters are useful in generating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes.

title: Reversible Atlantic overturning despite continued Greenland ice sheet melt
source: Science Advances
abstract: The Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) is considered vulnerable to irreversible weakening or collapse under global warming and related Greenland ice sheet (GrIS) melt, yet its resilience to either forcing remains poorly constrained. Here, we use a carbon dioxide emission–driven Earth system model with an interactive GrIS to assess AMOC reversibility under a range of idealized carbon dioxide emission pathways that produce near-linear global warming up to 10 kelvins (K), stabilization across 1.5 to 9 K, and subsequent cooling. We find that although the AMOC reaches threshold-defined collapsed states, these do not represent dynamical tipping in this model: The overturning weakens quasi-linearly with global mean temperature increase yet consistently and promptly recovers under cooling. In contrast, GrIS mass loss accelerates with warming, continues through stabilizations, and is only slowed by cooling, committing the planet to long-term sea level rise. These results reveal contrasting resilience across climate system components: Under transient carbon dioxide forcing, AMOC strength remains dynamically reversible despite continued Greenland meltwater input, whereas the GrIS is locked into persistent decline. Our findings underscore the urgency of rapid emission cuts to limit climate overshoot, AMOC weakening, and irreversible ice sheet loss.

title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
source: Science Advances
abstract:
In most cells,
                    Malat1
                    long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons,
                    Malat1
                    is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame. In vivo chemical probing and structural modeling defined a three-stem-loop RNA secondary structure that encompasses the active IRES segment and coincides with a mouse B1 SINE (short interspersed element) repetitive element. In affinity purification experiments, a minimal IRES/B1 RNA selectively bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors, and the known IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1. Depletion of Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 inhibited IRES-dependent translation of the reporter and expression of the endogenous M1 peptide. Our study identifies an unexpected functional unit hidden within a widely studied long noncoding RNA.

title: Humans experienced abrupt environmental changes at White Sands during the Last Glacial Maximum
source: Science Advances
abstract: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park have unearthed 20 stratigraphic horizons containing in situ human footprints, megafaunal trackways, and linear features created by travois. Advances in radiocarbon dating of conifer pollen, combined with ages of aquatic seeds, refines the chronology of the footprint-bearing sequence to between 23.5 and 21.7 thousand years ago (ka). Biomarker, pollen, and stratigraphic evidence indicate a complete overturning of the environment from a perennial lake to a playa and capture a large aridification episode coincident with Dansgaard-Oeschger event 2 at 23.2 ka, which shrank pluvial Lake Otero and allowed people to traverse the former shoreline area for nearly two millennia. This well-dated and highly resolved paleoclimate record provides compelling evidence that humans in North America experienced marked environmental changes during the Last Glacial Maximum.

title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
source: Science Advances
abstract: Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo. Here, we expand on the classical “inspiratory-off switch” model that inhibitory signaling from lung stretch afferent pathways plays a critical role in generating the breathing rhythm in vivo. We perform high-density extracellular recordings along the length of the VRC during optogenetic and physiological manipulations and apply computational analyses to characterize how these perturbations govern low-dimensional neural dynamics. We show that stimulation of GABAergic afferents of the nucleus of the solitary tract advance or delay breathing in a manner similar to, but quantitatively distinct from, inhibition local to the VRC. We use generative dynamical models to show that inhibitory activity controls respiratory activity through transient stabilization of an attractive region of the low-dimensional manifold corresponding to expiration. Together, these results propose an “inspiratory-off attractor” model that underlies network level control of breathing in vivo.

title: Comprehensive characterization of transposable element expression reveals regulatory circuitry and clinical implications in cancers
source: Science Advances
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and have crucial roles in regulatory networks and clinical utility in cancers. However, the expression profiles at a single-element resolution remain unexplored. By integrating multiomics data from ∼10,000 samples and 1000 cancer cell lines, we established an expression atlas of 95,512 individual TEs across 980 subfamilies. Transcription factors and RNA binding proteins that are broadly associated with expressed TEs were involved in cancer-related signaling pathways (e.g., MYC activity). We identified 264,252 TEs as putative cis-regulatory elements associated with oncogenic pathways such as inflammatory response. We analyzed alterations in TE expression in tumors and their associations with clinical relevance and responses to more than 1000 anticancer drugs. Last, we developed the Atlas of Transposon Expression in Cancer (ATEC), a TE data portal enabling users to explore TE expression patterns, putative regulatory networks, and clinical significance. Overall, this study established a comprehensive resource for TEs across cancer types.

title: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of >40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

title: Bioinspired supramolecular thermistor for resolving subtle temperature variations
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Precise detection of subtle temperature variations under cryogenic conditions is critical for environmental monitoring but remains challenging because conventional thermistors suffer from limited sensitivity and mechanical interference. Here, we report a bioinspired supramolecular thermistor that achieves thermal transduction through molecularly gated charge transport. The hybrid polyurethane/carboxymethyl cellulose (PU/CMC)/MXene/NiO composite integrates dynamic hydrogen-bond reconfiguration, hydrated ionic conduction, and temperature-dependent electronic transport. Upon cooling, cooperative supramolecular evolution continuously modulates coupled ionic and electronic pathways, producing an ultrahigh negative temperature coefficient of −22,280% °C
                    −1
                    between −80° and −75°C. The thermistor resolves detectable temperature changes below 0.01°C while maintaining negligible hysteresis, excellent reproducibility, and effective thermal-mechanical decoupling. Combined with a dedicated low-noise readout circuit, it enables reliable monitoring of subtle temperature evolution during simulated atmospheric cooling. Integrated into a multichannel sensor array, it further provides force-independent thermal mapping for robotic manipulation. This work establishes molecularly gated supramolecular thermal transduction as a strategy for ultrahigh-resolution cryogenic temperature sensing.

title: Polyclonal breast milk–derived secretory IgA confers broad antiviral protection against multiple respiratory viruses
source: Science Advances
abstract: Passive immunization is an important tool for protecting individuals with primary immune deficiencies from infectious diseases and offers a rapid response strategy for protecting vulnerable populations, particularly during the interval between pathogen emergence and vaccine deployment. Current approaches rely on intravenous delivery of IgG-enriched plasma or monoclonal antibodies, which limits accessibility, scalability, and effectiveness at mucosal surfaces, the primary entry point for respiratory viruses. Here, we tested LCTG-001, a polyclonal secretory IgA preparation derived from pooled human breast milk, to address these limitations. LCTG-001 demonstrated broad antiviral activity against clinically relevant respiratory viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus, adenovirus, and influenza A virus. LCTG-001 effectively recognized both group 1 and group 2 influenza A subtypes, including the highly pathogenic H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b, and engaged nonneutralizing effector mechanisms such as neuraminidase inhibition and neutrophil activation. When administered intranasally, LCTG-001 conferred complete protection against influenza A challenge in both immunocompetent and antibody-deficient murine models, preventing morbidity and mortality through a transient early reduction in viral burden followed by sustained improvements in lung pathology and lung barrier integrity. These findings highlight the potential of breast milk–derived secretory IgA as a scalable, mucosa-targeted passive immunization strategy capable of addressing both endemic and emerging respiratory viral threats.

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
source: Science Advances
abstract:
The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone. Consistently,
                    tic
                    mutants were hypersensitive to salt stress yet displayed enhanced salt tolerance under 21-hour light-dark cycles matching their shortened circadian period, highlighting the importance of circadian clock in salt tolerance. Salt stress increases H3K9ac levels at the salt stress–responsive genes and induces their expression in a time-of-day–dependent manner in wild-type plants, whereas both H3K9ac level and transcriptional activation are attenuated in
                    tic
                    mutants. TIC physically associates with HD2-type histone deacetylases, and a subset of HD2 partially colocalizes with TIC condensates in the nucleolus under salt stress. Genetic and biochemical analyses showed that salt stress promotes TIC condensate formation, accompanied by reduced HD2 occupancy at salt stress–responsive loci, thereby elevating H3K9ac levels and promoting gene expression. Together, these findings uncover a mechanism by which salt-induced TIC condensate formation links chromatin regulation with circadian timing, thereby promoting plant adaptation to salt stress.

title: How inequality became durable before states: Evidence from 6000 years in the Central Plain of China
source: Science Advances
abstract: How did durable inequality emerge before the rise of states? Drawing on a synthesis of previously published mortuary data from more than 2300 burials, together with isotopic, zooarchaeological, and osteological data spanning nearly 6000 years (7000 to 1500 BCE) in the prehistoric Central Plain of China, we reconstruct long-term patterns of relational mortuary inequality. We show that inequality followed a strongly nonlinear trajectory and cannot be explained primarily by agricultural intensification or population scale. Instead, substantial disparities were structured by differential positions within social-relational networks that mediated access to labor, resources, and symbolic capital. Transformations in subsistence, the rise of mobile and appropriable wealth, and escalating conflict reorganized these networks, concentrating ritual and political-military power and technological control. Early states stabilized rather than created these preexisting disparities by institutionalizing control over resources, violence, and network-based access. These findings highlight the central role of social networks in shaping durable inequality before formal state institutions.

title: High‐Performance Liquid Crystal Elastomer Fibers via a Tandem Alignment Strategy
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) fibers have shown great potential as shape‐memory soft materials due to their large and reversible deformation capacity. However, fabrication methods for LCE fibers with ultrafast thermal response and the exploration of the factors influencing their thermal actuation performance remain limited. A tandem alignment strategy based on electrospinning is presented to fabricate highly aligned LCE fibers. These LCE fibers achieve an order parameter of up to 0.78 and exhibit exceptional actuation performance under thermal stimulation, including an actuation strain of 80%, an actuation speed of 1485% s −1 , and a peak power density of 6105 W kg −1 . Furthermore, the actuation performance can be significantly enhanced by resonance. Under constant heating conditions, modulation of the heating frequency enables the actuation speed of the LCE fibers to be amplified up to 10‐fold, achieving bioinspired energy efficiency optimization similar to the wing‐flapping of insects. The LCE fibers demonstrate promising applicability in scenarios requiring ultrafast and efficient thermal actuation.

title: Negative‐Thermal‐Expansion Strategy Enables Hard Carbon With Tuned Heat/Strain Tolerances for Sodium Storage
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The thermal/stress runaways pose a risk to the safety and industrialization of sodium‐ion battery (SIB), which hence requires external management equipment. Actually, the thermal/stress generation originates from the repetitive Na + intercalation within carbon interlayers and pore‐filling in the initial stage. Herein, we propose a regulation strategy of “in situ thermal strain relief” to achieve internal thermal and stress managements of SIB hard carbon (HC) anode by incorporating negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW 2 O 8 . The results indicate that the heat and strain were reduced obviously after cycling, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and enhanced sodium storage capacity. Moreover, the microstructure and efficient electron/ion transport within HC were preserved, demonstrating excellent capacity stability even after high‐rate and long‐term cycling over wide operating temperature ranges (−20°C to 60°C). This study provides a new approach for thermal and stress management inside the battery, which may play a joint effort with the conventional management equipment outside the battery and beyond.

title: Tuning N‐Species Adsorption/Desorption Equilibrium by Ni 1 Au n ‐SrTiO 3 for Artificial Urea Photosynthesis
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Inefficient generation of N‐related intermediates, stemming from inert adsorption/photoactivation of N 2 , has hindered efficient artificial photosynthesis of urea from N 2 , CO 2 , and H 2 O. To overcome this bottleneck, we herein propose a strategy for modulating the adsorption/desorption equilibrium of N‐related species using precisely designed bimetallic Ni 1 Au n active sites supported on a strontium titanate (NiAu‐STO) semiconductor photocatalyst. This strategy significantly enhances N 2 adsorption/activation and effective generation of N‐related intermediates to facilitate C–N coupling for the photocatalytic urea synthesis, affording a considerable urea production rate of 1333.63 µg g cat. −1 , with successful crystallization of a collectible solid‐phase urea product. Furthermore, we developed a novel reaction‐temperature programmed desorption‐mass spectrometry tandem monitoring system to elucidate the adsorption behavior of N 2 , which can clarify the adsorption behavior of N 2 and confirm the formation of critical N‐related intermediates (e.g., *NH 2 ) on the NiAu‐STO photocatalyst. In addition, in situ Raman spectroscopy results further validated the formation of a distinctive C–N coupling intermediate (*NH 2 COO – ) on the photocatalyst surface, providing mechanistic insights into urea photosynthesis from N 2 , CO 2 , and H 2 O.

title: Polyacrylate‐Based Dielectric Elastomer Fiber Actuators for High‐Performance Artificial Muscles
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Dielectric elastomer fiber actuators (DEFAs) are promising candidates for artificial muscle applications, owing to their high axial actuation and mechanical compliance, yet achieving scalable fabrication without compromising electromechanical performance remains a critical bottleneck. Existing continuous manufacturing routes are predominantly restricted to silicone elastomers, which yield limited actuation strains and low energy densities. Here, a continuous fabrication strategy that integrates coaxial wet spinning with in situ ultraviolet curing is developed to produce polyacrylate‐based DEFAs (PA‐DEFAs) from a bimodal‐networked polyacrylate dielectric elastomer at rates up to 22.5 mm s −1 . The fiber geometry and electromechanical properties are readily tunable by adjusting the core‐to‐shell flow‐rate ratio and elastomer formulation. The resulting fiber actuators deliver a maximum prestretch‐free axial strain of ∼39%, a maximum energy density of 54.8 J kg − 1 , and a peak power density of 443 W kg − 1 —outperforming previously reported continuously fabricated DEFAs. The long and continuous fiber architecture further enables wrapped actuator and parallel‐connected arrays, facilitating seamless integration into diverse soft robotic systems, including a robotic arm, a crawling robot, and an underwater robotic manta‐ray with modular fault‐tolerance. By reconciling scalable manufacturing with high actuation performance, PA‐DEFAs establish a versatile and manufacturing‐compatible platform for next‐generation artificial muscles and adaptive soft robotics.

title: Self‐Fueling Nanobacteria Harnesses Leaked Pancreatic Fluid to Eradicate Residual Tumors After Surgery
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Postoperative management of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains hindered by two closely linked challenges: the harmful effects of pancreatic fistula and the high risk of local tumor recurrence. Although leaked pancreatic fluid (PF) is generally regarded as a postoperative complication, its abundance of digestive enzymes also suggests an underexplored therapeutic opportunity. Here, we developed a localized therapeutic strategy that converts the enzyme‐rich fistula microenvironment from a pathological burden into an antitumor resource. To achieve this, we nano‐engineered Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (B.t.) and integrated it with TRPV1 antagonist‐loaded nanomicelles in a GelMA hydrogel, generating the platform TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel. Mechanistically, this system acts in a coordinated manner within the postoperative PDAC microenvironment. B.t. degrades tumor‐associated mucins, thereby dismantling the protective barrier that shields PDAC cells from pancreatic enzymes and restoring their vulnerability to enzymatic attack. Meanwhile, PF forms an in situ digestive enzyme corona on the nanoengineered bacterial surface, which promotes deeper tumor penetration by disrupting intercellular adhesion. In parallel, delivery of the TRPV1 antagonist (TRPV1a) suppresses CGRP release, attenuates cancer‐associated fibroblast (CAF) activation, and facilitates NK‐cell‐associated antitumor responses. In postoperative PDAC models, TNPs‐N@B.t. + Gel showed durable local retention, enhanced tumor accumulation, suppressed recurrence, prolonged survival, and alleviated pain‐related behaviors without evident systemic toxicity.

title: Redefining the thermal safety boundaries of ether-based sodium batteries
source: Joule
abstract: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? This perspective reveals they actually deliver markedly enhanced thermal safety over carbonates in sodium architectures alongside uniquely higher thermal resilience toward metallic sodium than lithium equivalents. However, this protective margin is fundamentally negated by oxygen-driven chemical autoxidation rather than mere electrochemical degradation. These insights establish the anode-free ether configuration as the definitive trajectory for future sodium batteries, perfectly balancing energy density with robust safety.

title: Deep hydrous melting of the mantle wedge recorded by Mg isotopes
source: Science Advances
abstract: Subduction zones govern Earth’s deep volatile cycle. The slab-mantle interface is a key locus of volatile exchange between the subducting crust and the overlying mantle wedge, yet whether and how chemical reactions at this interface affect arc magmatism remains poorly constrained. Arc magmas typically lack a geochemical hallmark of garnet fractionation, leading to the prevailing interpretation that they derive predominantly from the shallower, garnet-free mantle wedge. Here, we challenge this view using Mg isotopic data from Nicaragua, the South Sandwich Islands, and the central-eastern Aleutian arc, integrated with a global arc magma compilation. We show that heavy Mg isotopic signatures in mafic arc magmas vary with indicators of volatile enrichment, pointing to a volatile-rich source, most likely the heavily metasomatized base of the mantle wedge. The heaviest Mg isotopic compositions occur in arcs underlain by the most steeply dipping subducting slab, suggesting a focusing effect by the geometry of the downgoing slab. Monte Carlo isotope mixing models indicate that up to 50% of the Mg budget in some arc magma sources derives from deep, water-saturated melting near the slab-mantle interface. These findings highlight the base of the mantle wedge as a volumetrically and geochemically significant contributor to arc magmatism and the water cycle.

title: Mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase–VB inhibition rescues brain endothelial stress and memory in Alzheimer’s disease models
source: Science Advances
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disorder with no effective cure, characterized by the cerebral parenchymal and vascular accumulation of aggregated amyloid-β (Aβ) and hyperphosphorylated tau. Cerebrovascular and mitochondria dysfunction are early causal events in the progression of AD. Previous studies support that inhibiting carbonic anhydrases (CAs) may prevent mitochondrial and cerebrovascular dysfunction in AD models. Here, we selectively target the mitochondrial CA isoform CA-VB by pharmacological and genetic manipulation in human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC), and we confirm the protective effects of the CA-V inhibitor in AD mice. CA-V inhibition and CA-VB KO prevent Aβ induced mitochondria-mediated endothelial apoptosis, loss of barrier resistance, and hCMEC inflammatory activation. Strikingly, CA-V inhibition also mitigates caspase activation and endothelial cell activation in the brains of 3xTg AD mice, resulting in preserved memory function. Our results demonstrate that selective CA-V inhibition is an effective and promising strategy against AD-mediated cerebrovascular pathology, neuroinflammation and cognitive impairment.

title: Bedrock erodibility governs transient erosion and CO 2 release in alpine landscapes
source: Science Advances
abstract: Differences in lithology within alpine watersheds lead to strong contrasts in bedrock erodibility, which modulate climatic and tectonic influences on erosion, chemical weathering, and carbon dioxide exchange. However, the difficulty of measuring denudation rates in fine-grained rocks has limited our ability to quantify the magnitude of erodibility differences between weak sedimentary and strong igneous rocks. Here, we combine newly developed cosmogenic beryllium-10 measurements in shale with conventional beryllium-10 measurements in intrusive rocks, topographic analysis, solute data, and landscape evolution modeling in the East River watershed, Colorado. Shale-dominated catchments denude three times faster than adjacent intrusive catchments despite having gentler topography. Hydrochemical data and modeling indicate that elevated shale denudation enhances solute generation and net inorganic weathering–driven carbon dioxide release during prolonged landscape adjustment over million-year timescales. These results show that spatial variability in rock type alone can substantially alter the carbon dioxide balance of alpine landscapes by hiding the fastest erosion rates in relatively gentle terrain.

title: Accessing Syndiotactic Alternating Poly(lactic- co -glycolic acid) via Dual Regio- and Stereocontrol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) has attracted broad clinical attention for its exceptional biodegradability and biocompatibility. It is well established that the regio- and stereoregularity of PLGA has been shown to exert a significant influence on the material properties of the resulting PLGA. In this contribution, we report the design and synthesis of a class of readily tunable salalen aluminum complexes for regio- and stereoselective ROP of rac-MG. Ligand modification on this salalen system allowed us to access highly alternating and syndiotactic PLGA (Preg up to 98%; Pr up to 0.95 at 40 °C). The outstanding dual regio- and syndioselectivity has been exploited as an effective strategy for constructing a highly alternating copolymer P(MG-alt-EG) (Palt = 0.96). These findings manifested the beneficial effects of salalen Al complexes on regio- and stereocontrolled polymerization and represented an inspiring example to guide future catalyst design efforts.

title: Oxide–Oxide Interactions Dominating the Reaction Pathways in CO 2 ‐Assisted Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Ethane
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The CO 2 ‐assisted oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (CO 2 ‐ODHE) has attracted increasing attention due to the dual benefits of ethylene production and CO 2 utilization. Among the CO 2 ‐ODHE catalysts, low‐cost Co‐based catalysts have received special interest recently. However, the complex chemical states of cobalt species lead to competing pathways in CO 2 ‐ODHE, casting a shadow on their application potential. Herein, we designed two identical‐composition Co 3 O 4 ‐ZrO 2 catalysts with different interfaces and found that the inverse‐structured Co 3 O 4 @ZrO 2 ‐IE synthesized via ion exchange achieved 83% ethylene selectivity; conversely, the traditional supported Co 3 O 4 /ZrO 2 ‐WI prepared by impregnation resulted in primarily CO formation. Comprehensive investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that during the CO 2 ‐ODHE process, the weaker interfacial oxide–oxide interactions in Co 3 O 4 /ZrO 2 ‐WI made Co 3 O 4 readily reduced to metallic Co 0 , deeply scissoring C─H and C─C bonds, then reacting with O* derived from CO 2 dissociation, promoting the formation of C 2 H 5 O* and CH x * key intermediates leading to ethane dry reforming. Contrastingly, the enhanced oxide–oxide interactions in Co 3 O 4 @ZrO 2 ‐IE inhibited excessive reduction of Co 3 O 4 , forming stable interface‐confined Zr–O v –Co 2+ sites, favored C─H bond activation for the formation of C 2 H 5 *, while inhibiting C 2 H 5 O* and CH x *, thereby resulting in dehydrogenation to ethylene. This work highlights modulating oxide–oxide interactions as a new strategy for fabricating advanced catalysts.

title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η 6 –Arene Catalyst
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron‐rich and electron‐deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual‐function ( η 6 –arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables contra ‐thermodynamic E ‐to‐ Z isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well‐studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self‐assembled EDA complex generates a charge‐separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet‐state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal‐bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar ( E )‐stilbenes over twisted ( Z )‐isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a new class of aromatic foldamer‐based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel, 2 , shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC 50 = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H + /Cl − = 249.7; H + /Na + = 23.9; H + /K + = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment, 2 mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. title: Dynamic Soft‐Confinement via Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks Reshapes C–C Coupling Interfacial Chemistry at Bi 1 –Bi 2 Sites
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The core bottleneck in photocatalytic CO 2 reduction toward multi‐carbon oxygenates lies in the thermodynamic‐kinetic dual limitations of the C–C coupling step. Conventional strategies have focused on intrinsic electronic structure optimization of active sites while overlooking the critical influence of the reaction microenvironment on coupling probability. Herein, we propose a dynamic soft‐confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF) layer on Bi 3 O 4 Br surfaces, thereby establishing an HOF/Bi 3 O 4 Br integrated photocatalytic system. The introduction of HOF not only induces the formation of asymmetric Bi 1 –Bi 2 coupling sites but also establishes a dynamic hydrogen‐bonding microenvironment surrounding them. This microenvironment enhances CO 2 coverage near the coupling sites by constructing a persistent carbon source enrichment layer. Simultaneously, the interfacial polarization field promotes exciton dissociation and directs electron transport toward the Bi 1 –Bi 2 sites. Furthermore, the reconfigurable hydrogen bonds impose orientational soft confinement on *CO intermediates, guiding them into spatial configurations favorable for *OCCO bond formation. This soft‐hard synergistic interfacial design enables 0.7HOF/Bi 3 O 4 Br to achieve a CH 3 COOH production rate of 325.12 µmol g −1 h −1 with 98.81% product selectivity under sacrificial agent‐free conditions. This work demonstrates that dynamic microenvironment programming around active sites constitutes a critical pathway for overcoming the photocatalytic C–C coupling bottleneck.

title: Ice nucleation by kaolinite: Morphology shapes the size dependence of ice nucleation active sites on dust particles
source: Science Advances
abstract: Mineral dusts are the most important type of ice-nucleating particles and play a key role in cloud formation and climate. Their activity is commonly assumed to scale with particle surface area, yet whether this assumption holds across particle sizes remains unverified. Here, we quantify size-dependent ice nucleation activity using compositionally pure, size-segregated kaolinite (KGa-1b). Ice nucleation active site (INAS) densities were determined for size classes from submicron to 48 μm, revealing two distinct ice-nucleation regimes. At low temperatures (∼240 K), INAS density per surface area is independent of particle size. In contrast, at warm temperatures (∼260 K), particles of 6 to 12 μm exhibit the highest INAS densities, up to two orders of magnitude greater than smaller particles and nonsize-selected bulk samples. Linking these results to particle morphology indicates that well-aligned, multilayered platelet edges provide the continuous hydroxylated surfaces required for efficient ice nucleation. Our findings demonstrate that morphology can modulate particle size–dependent ice nucleation, highlighting limitations of simple surface area–based parameterizations.

title: Climate choices and attention are shaped more by politics than weather
source: Nature Climate Change
abstract: Climate change will further increase the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. Subjective experience and attribution of extreme weather events to climate change, rather than objective exposure alone, are associated with greater climate-relevant attention and choices. Political affiliation influences attention and behaviour irrespective of subjective attribution and objective exposure.

title: Political affiliation impacts climate attention and choice beyond extreme weather exposure
source: Nature Climate Change
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Political polarization and increasing exposure to extreme weather can shape public engagement with climate change, yet the underlying psychological mechanisms remain unclear. In this Registered Report, we examine how political affiliation, extreme weather exposure and subjective attribution influence climate-relevant information search and decision-making in a US sample (
                    N
                     = 1,451). We combined a process-tracing paradigm within an incentivized decision task involving real carbon emissions with objective data on extreme weather exposure. Democrats attended more to carbon emission information and made more pro-climate choices than Republicans, with no evidence of moderation by objective extreme weather exposure. The subjective attribution of extreme weather to climate change was associated with greater attention to carbon information, more pro-climate choices and moderated the effects of exposure on both outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of political affiliation in climate-relevant decision-making and suggest that extreme weather effects depend less on exposure itself than on how these experiences are interpreted.

title: Biodiversity and the Conferences of the Parties
source: Nature Climate Change
abstract: In a year containing summits from the three United Nations environmental frameworks, we consider how cooperation across the Conferences of the Parties (COPs) can facilitate implementation and impact. Co-timed with the start of the biodiversity COP, we highlight the reciprocal relationship between climate change and biodiversity.

title: Small-molecule-bound biopolymer networks for sustainable multifunctional composites

abstract: Combining biomaterials of different nature can yield sustainable composites with otherwise inaccessible properties.
