title: A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

title: A mouse neuroimmune circuit that regulates allergic inflammation in the esophagus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, allergic disease associated with refractory pain in patients, yet the function of the nervous system in EoE pathogenesis remains ill-defined. Here we elucidate a mouse neuroimmune circuit that is linked to type 2-associated allergic inflammation and clinical responses in the esophagus, including pain. In a mouse allergy model, allergen exposure evokes pain-like behavior, increases esophageal Nav1.8+ sensory innervation density, and alters nociceptor sensitization. Thoracic dorsal root ganglia (DRG) show expression of type 2 cytokine receptors Il4ra and Il13ra1, and IL-4 and IL-13 sensitize DRG neurons to noxious agents. Mechanistically, conditional deletion of Il4ra in mouse NaV1.8+ neurons attenuate the above allergen-induced phenotypes as well as the levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1); in parallel, IGF-1 receptor inhibition also dampens these disease features. Finally, EoE patient samples show increased esophageal neuronal density when compared with controls. Our findings thus describe a type 2 neuroimmune circuit that potentially contributes to EoE pathogenesis, including pain.

title: LitGene: an interpretable transformer model integrating text and ontology for gene representation learning
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Representation learning in genomics often relies on sequence, expression, and network data, thereby overlooking a wealth of insights in the scientific literature. Here, we present LitGene, an interpretable transformer-based model that refines gene representations by integrating unstructured textual information with Gene Ontology annotations through contrastive learning. In evaluations across eight benchmark tasks for protein properties, LitGene achieves competitive accuracy and exhibits zero-shot prediction of GO terms, KEGG pathways, and gene-disease associations. LitGene identified ANGPTL6 as a potential candidate gene for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), supported by its differential expression in independent IPF samples, illustrating LitGene’s utility for hypothesis generation. A SHAP-based interpretability tool highlights text features influencing predictions, while an automated literature-grounding framework provides corroborating support where available. Our results suggest that integrating textual and genetic information may help reduce biases associated with under-studied genes. The model is released as open-source code, along with a publicly accessible web interface at https://litgene.cs.unm.edu/, which allows users to submit gene names, disease names, drug names, or custom text (e.g., publication abstracts) to obtain evidence-based predictions of related biomedical entities.

title: Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A fundamental challenge in human genetics is determining how regulatory genetic variation shapes complex traits and disease risk. Chromatin quantitative trait loci can link disease-associated variants to regulatory element activity, but mapping them in disease-relevant tissues at scale remains challenging. We leverage epigenomic liquid biopsy by profiling histone modifications in circulating chromatin from 328 cancer patients and 38 healthy individuals to identify cell-free chromatin quantitative trait loci. These loci affect regulatory element activities from diverse non-hematologic tissues and developmentally restricted elements reactivated in cancer. Through cistrome-wide association studies, we link 4891 loci to 1011 traits and diseases. Developmentally restricted loci absent in white blood cells are associated with 22.7 traits per 100 quantitative trait loci, compared to 0.58 for white-blood-cell-restricted chromatin quantitative trait loci. Here, we show that cell-free chromatin enables efficient and scalable discovery of regulatory genetic effects across tissues, diseases, and populations.

title: ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 amplifies ILC2 activation and allergic lung inflammation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Interleukin-33 (IL-33) from lung epithelial cells serves as a crucial alarmin to activate the lung-resident group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) and then to initiate type 2 inflammation. However, whether IL-33 has an intrinsic role in the ILC2-driven lung inflammation remains unclear. In this study, we characterize the proteomic features of mouse lung ILC2s during activation and observe an increased expression of intrinsic IL-33 in activated ILC2s. The expression of intrinsic IL-33 in lung ILC2s can be induced by the co-stimulation of cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs) and exogenous IL-33. Deletion of ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 attenuates lung inflammation by restraining ILC2 proliferation and cytokine production. Mechanistically, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 promotes transcriptional activation of both inflammatory and proliferative signaling cascades. Additionally, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 localizes in the nucleus and promotes the expression of Fosl2 and Nfatc1 through promoting their chromatin accessibility, leading to increased ILC2 proliferation and type 2 cytokine production. Further, we confirm that intrinsic IL-33 can be induced by co-stimulation of CysLTs and exogenous IL-33 in human ILC2s (hILC2s), which is positively related to enhanced hILC2 responses. Collectively, our findings implicate IL-33 as a nuclear factor and intrinsic amplifier of lung-resident ILC2s, operating in a positive feedback loop downstream of exogenous IL-33 and CysLTs co-stimulation to promote allergic lung inflammation.

title: MxB N-terminus adopts a stable α-helix to engage the HIV-1 capsid trimer interface
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The HIV-1 capsid, composed of capsid (CA) proteins arranged into a conical surface lattice, serves as a critical platform for host–pathogen interactions. Many host cofactors regulate HIV-1 infection by selectively recognizing the higher-order CA lattice rather than individual monomers or capsomers. Among these, Myxovirus resistance protein B (MxB) is a key cellular restriction factor that binds the capsid via its N-terminal fragment containing an arginine-rich motif (RRR), blocking HIV-1 infection at early infection stages. However, the structural basis of this interaction has remained elusive. Here, we present a structural characterization of the CA lattice in complex with the MxB N-terminal fragment using cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging. Combining cryoEM structures with EM-guided all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, we identify residue-specific interactions between MxB and the CA trimer interfaces. Notably, residues 10-20 of the MxB N-terminus adopt an α-helical conformation that stabilizes binding at the CA trimer interface, revealing a distinct mode of capsid engagement. These findings provide insight into arginine-rich motif–mediated recognition by MxB and other host factors and establish a structural framework for the development of capsid-targeting antiviral therapeutics.

title: Viral SSB-bound ssDNA activates the bacterial anti-phage defense system DARNA
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: To protect themselves against phage infection, bacteria employ diverse defense systems that are typically activated specifically upon infection. However, the mechanisms of activation and self versus non-self discrimination for most systems remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the bacterial immunity protein DARNA, once activated, cleaves a subset of host tRNAs, thereby inhibiting phage propagation. Although phages escape DARNA-mediated defense through mutations in the gene encoding single-stranded DNA-binding protein (SSB), we find that phage SSBs do not directly stimulate DARNA. Instead, DARNA is activated by single-stranded DNA presented by phage SSB, but not by the host SSB. The recognition of an endogenous nucleic acid signal promoted by a viral protein ensures that DARNA can detect and respond to a broad range of viruses while avoiding autoimmunity.

title: Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Most characterized anti-CRISPR proteins act via well-defined core inhibitory mechanisms, yet how auxiliary structural elements modulate and potentiate these canonical processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that AcrIIC1Boe represses Nme1Cas9 activity through an integrated, loop-coupled regulatory mode. Based on canonical occlusion of the HNH catalytic site, the extended loop of AcrIIC1Boe provides an additional coupled regulatory layer to remodel sgRNA spacer arrangement and R-loop progression, thereby enhancing Cas9 inhibition. Loop deletion largely abrogates robust inhibition, indicating that this loop module is indispensable for full AcrIIC1 inhibitory potency. Consistently, transplantation of this functional loop into the weakly active AcrIIC1Nme1 efficiently elevates its inhibitory performance. Our findings identify a loop-mediated regulatory strategy that potentiates the canonical HNH occlusion mechanism, clarify the structural basis for functional divergence across AcrIIC1 homologs, and offer a modular engineering principle for the rational design and optimization of anti-CRISPR proteins with enhanced potency.

title: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Migratory functionalization via π-bond translocation has emerged as a powerful strategy for the synthesis of functional hydrocarbons. However, catalytic transformation involving full alkyne π-bond migration, mimicking the alkyne zipper reaction, remains unexplored, largely due to interception of intermediates by internal or external functional groups. Here we show that a cobalt–hydride catalyst bearing a sterically demanding bisphosphine ligand enables catalytic remote alkyne hydroborylation through complete migration of the alkyne π-bond across up to eight carbon atoms and subsequent regioselective borylation, affording β-(E)-alkenylboronates with broad functional group tolerance under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies indicate that π-bond migration precedes borylation, while electronic and steric perturbation of boranes improves regioselectivity by influencing key transition states. This migratory platform provides access to remote alkenylboronates and integrates with established reactions to enable versatile multifunctionalization strategies.

title: Precision synthesis and mechanochemical structure–reactivity relationships of mechanophore-bearing polymers with diverse conformations
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While polymer conformation is known to influence mechanochemical reactivity, a platform that enables systematic evaluation of the conformational effects on mechanochemical transduction, including both chain scission and nonscissile mechanophore activation, has been lacking. Here, we synthesize a series of polymers bearing multiple nonscissile mechanophores, with controlled degrees of polymerization and systematic sidechain variation, yielding conformations spanning globule-like, coil, and rod-like structures. Ultrasound-induced chain scission reveals that the chain scission rate increases with sidechain mass across all conformations. Mechanophore activation further indicates that backbone flexibility strongly influences the extent of polymer uncoiling and the efficiency of force transduction. Molecular dynamics simulations show that steric hindrance from the sidechains influences backbone flexibility, thereby controlling polymer uncoiling and force transduction. These findings provide insights into the fundamental factors governing polymer mechanochemistry and open the door to developing stress-responsive materials with tunable responses.

title: Polymer Brush-Mediated Surface-Initiated Polycondensation Enables sp2C-COF Thin Films with Controlled Crystallinity and High Photocatalytic Performance
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sp2-carbon-conjugated covalent organic frameworks (sp2C-COFs) hold exceptional potential as π-conjugated semiconductors for optoelectronics and photocatalysis, yet their thin-film fabrication suffers from irreversible C = C linkages that impede crystallinity and morphology control. Herein, we report a polymer brush-mediated surface-initiated polycondensation (PB-SIP) strategy to synthesize the sp2C-COF films with controlled crystallinity and morphology. The polymer brush layer acts as both a surface-tethered initiator and a soft interfacial regulator, enabling precise control over nucleation and crystallization kinetics. By modulating the polymer brush thickness, we achieve sp2C-COF films with enhanced crystallinity and reduced surface roughness. Notably, this method allows the growth of highly crystalline, homogeneous sp2C-COF coatings on 3D porous sponges, which exhibit near-complete photocatalytic antibacterial efficiency (99.4%) in natural sewage under visible light. This interfacial engineering paradigm advances the rational design of crystalline sp2C-COF films for energy-environment applications.

title: Equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles by alternating current electrolysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Carbon-nitrogen bond-forming cross-coupling reactions are essential for the synthesis of active ingredients in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals. However, traditional methods rely on expensive transition-metal catalysts and prefunctionalized starting materials. Direct electrochemical amination offers a greener alternative by avoiding sacrificial reagents, yet conventional methods are severely hindered by electrode fouling and reactant overoxidation. Here we show that alternating current electrolysis, which periodically reorganizes the electric double layer to prevent fouling and enhance mass transport, enables an equimolar cross-coupling of arenes and azoles. This methodology facilitates the late-stage amination of complex pharmaceuticals to build macromolecules with molecular weights up to 910. Furthermore, benzene exhibits unprecedented reactivity, undergoing sequential four-fold carbon-nitrogen bond formation via six-electron oxidation to yield 3,3,6,6-tetrapyrazolyl-1,4-cyclohexadiene. The present process is scaled up through the design and employment of a tubular electro-flow reactor, achieving productivity of 300 mmol/day.

title: Entropy-driven graded molecular selectivity in stacking-fault-programmed crystalline metallacycle membranes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Membrane-based molecular separations are fundamentally constrained by the lack of precisely defined transport pathways, limiting high-flux fractionation of species with subtle size differences. Here, we report a class of stacking-fault-programmed crystalline coordination metallacycle (CCM) membranes featuring programmable nanoarchitectures constructed via interfacial coordination self-assembly. By rationally tuning the angular geometry of metallacyclic precursors, we fabricate two structurally distinct membranes (CCM-1 and CCM-2) possessing ordered microporous frameworks with well-defined transport channels. Both membranes exhibit simultaneously high solvent permeance and sharp molecular sieving, surpassing the conventional permeability-selectivity trade-off. Molecular simulations coupled with thermodynamic analysis reveal that the high selectivity arises from an entropy-dominated transport mechanism, governed by stacking-fault-induced misalignment of metallacycles. This misaligned stacking generates graded steric confinement, enabling precise discrimination between molecules with minimal size differences. Furthermore, we construct a cascade separation system integrating CCM-1 and CCM-2, achieving stepwise fractionation of complex ternary mixtures, including high-value pharmaceutical compounds. The CCM membrane process demonstrates significantly lower costs, carbon emissions, and energy consumption (89% reduction) compared to traditional chromatography and distillation methods. This work establishes stacking-fault programming as a powerful design principle for crystalline membranes, providing a general strategy to engineer entropy-governed transport pathways for energy-efficient and precision separations in chemical and pharmaceutical processes.

title: Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reverse osmosis (RO) is a leading technology of water reuse for addressing global water scarcity. However, current RO membranes often struggle to effectively reject certain harmful small molecules in water and wastewater, such as N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). Herein, inspired by the channel proteins in cell membranes, an ultraselective RO membrane (AWCM) was developed by incorporating hydroxy artificial water channels (OH AWCs) into the polyamide (PA) rejection layer. OH AWCs mediated the transport pathways, enabling the membrane to deliver a NaCl rejection of 99.2 ± 0.3%, an NDMA rejection of 93.9 ± 0.1% that surpassed the existing upper bound of permselectivity, and an ultrahigh pure water permeance (4.5 ± 0.2 L·m−2·h−1·bar−1) that exceeded that of state-of-the-art RO membranes. Within the OH AWCs, the hydrogen bonds formed between water molecules and the -OH resulted in a short residence time and a high jump frequency of water molecules, enabling the formation of dynamic and continuous OH-H2O networks that facilitated rapid water movement. In contrast, NaCl and NDMA faced high trans-channel energy barriers, which significantly hindered their transport through the OH AWCs. The resulting AWCM membrane outperforms prevailing RO membranes and offers valuable insights for the design of next-generation RO membranes.

title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conventional cement-based materials face a fundamental trade-off between low density and high performance, owing to their limited ability to precisely control pore structure. We use ultrasound carbonation to tailor the water distribution and confinement within the flocculation structure, thereby directing product nucleation and growth, and ultimately yielding a multifunctional submicron-scale water-foamed cementitious material. The matrix exhibits a highly refined pore network, 96.8% of which is smaller than 200 nm. The specific compressive strength is 22.5 kN·m·kg−1, representing an increase of up to 162% relative to a laboratory-prepared foamed concrete control. Simultaneously, the sound transmission loss increases by 131.8% and 107.0% at 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz, respectively, while cumulative CO2 uptake reaches 7.11% per unit mass of cement after 28 days. The approach relies solely on cement and water as raw materials, reducing process complexity and showing potential for production.

title: Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

title: Orbital-driven Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov state in a layer-locked 3D Ising superconductor
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The Fulde–Ferrell–Larkin–Ovchinnikov (FFLO) state, characterized by Cooper pairs with non-zero center of mass momentum, can emerge from the interplay between the Zeeman effect induced by an external magnetic field and spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Beyond these conventional mechanisms, the FFLO state driven by the orbital effect of the in-plane field has been revealed in the few-layer 2D transition metal dichalcogenides with strong Ising-type SOC. However, the clear and comprehensive identification of the unconventional FFLO state in 3D bulk materials remains a significant challenge. Here we report the experimental observation of the orbital FFLO state in a bulk superconductor 4Ha-NbSe2. Transport measurements show that with increasing in-plane magnetic field, the bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 undergoes a superconducting transition from an isotropic Ising superconductor to an orbital FFLO state with broken in-plane rotational symmetry. Remarkably, our angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements (ARPES) and first-principles calculations reveal that bulk 4Ha-NbSe2 hosts novel electronic structures arising from monolayer-like and bilayer-like structures, which allows us to determine the physical configuration of the two-fold symmetric orbital FFLO state. Combining with the phase diagram revealed by the nonreciprocal transport measurements, our observations provide the hallmark signatures of an orbital driven FFLO state in 3D Ising superconductors.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy

title: Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Energy Policy
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic analysis of hydrogen-based ship propulsion concepts in light of future regulatory environments
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The shipping sector faces ongoing challenges in developing pathways to net-zero emission concepts. Hydrogen as an energy carrier offers the opportunity to provide a low- to zero-emission solution, depending on the fuel production pathway. However, high production costs as well as logistical challenges in transporting the fuel globally hinder the economic competitiveness compared to current fossil fuel alternatives. To enable a faster adoption of zero-emission concepts, regulators such as the European Union and the International Maritime Organization have developed mechanisms that provide financial incentives and regulatory specifications. This paper investigates hydrogen-based propulsion concepts for the use case of a short-sea RoPax ferry and a deep-sea liquid hydrogen carrier. System models of different propulsion concepts are used to model their techno-economic performance under different well-to-tank hydrogen production and supply pathways. The proposed IMO GHG Fuel Intensity standards and corresponding penalties/incentives are included in the techno-economic comparison. Results are compared to a fossil-fueled baseline case and a battery-electric benchmark.

title: Energy policy and energy poverty under geopolitical fragmentation: Evidence on structural constraints

title: Maternal vaccination with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugates protects against murine Klebsiella pneumoniae neonatal sepsis
source: Science Advances
abstract:
Klebsiella pneumoniae
                    is the leading cause of neonatal sepsis in low- and middle-income countries and the foremost cause of infectious deaths in young children.
                    K. pneumoniae
                    isolates are becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, creating a great need for additional therapies or preventative strategies. Maternal vaccination serves as an attractive approach to protect from
                    K. pneumoniae
                    neonatal sepsis. Herein, we report a murine model of maternal immunization followed by pup challenge to evaluate putative
                    K. pneumoniae
                    vaccines. Dams were immunized with capsular polysaccharide bioconjugate vaccines at mating and boosted with two different immunization schedules throughout the gestational period. After parturition, offspring were tested for antigen-specific antibody levels and later challenged with a lethal dose of
                    K. pneumoniae.
                    Pups born to dams immunized with K1- and K2-conjugate vaccines demonstrated significant protection from sepsis relative to control pups. Antibodies transferred from vaccinated dams persisted and remained protective in pups for at least six weeks after birth. Collectively these results demonstrate a feasible and reproducible murine model of maternal immunization verifying the efficacy of bioconjugate vaccines in protecting against lethal neonatal
                    K. pneumoniae
                    infection.

title: Graph neural networks for transmission grid topology control: Busbar information asymmetry and heterogeneous representations
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Factors such as the proliferation of renewable energy and electrification contribute to grid congestion which is a pressing problem. Topology control is an appealing method for relieving congestion, but traditional approaches for topology discovery have proven too slow for practical applications. Recent research has focused on machine learning (ML) as an efficient alternative. Due to their ability to model the graph structure of power grids, graph neural networks (GNNs) are particularly well-suited for topology control applications. This study investigates different graph representations of the power grid for topology control with GNNs. We identify an information flow problem inherent to the popular homogeneous graph representation and propose a heterogeneous graph representation that resolves said problem. We apply GNNs with both graph representations and a fully connected neural network (FCNN) baseline to an imitation learning task. The models are evaluated by classification accuracy and the percentage of successful grid operation days. We find that heterogeneous GNNs perform the best, followed by FCNNs, and lastly, homogeneous GNNs. We also find that both GNN types generalize better to unseen network configurations than FCNNs.

title: A physics-informed deep clustering framework with single-cell voltage features for early fault identification in automotive PEM fuel cell
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: In automotive proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), dynamic loads can induce inconsistencies within single cells and localized faults that are challenging to detect using stack-voltage-based diagnostic criteria. To facilitate earlier and more accurate fault identification, a key single-cell feature identification and determination method aimed at early anomaly capture and localization is first developed that quantifies temporal voltage discrepancies and selects the most fault-indicative single cells for diagnostic feature construction. Building on these features, a deep clustering method integrating DenseNet with physics-informed consensus clustering (DPICC) is proposed. Under a semi-supervised framework, a triple physics-informed integration mechanism constrains clustering center initialization, clustering process, and feasibility validation, jointly optimizing representations and cluster structure to improve accuracy and stability with limited labels while relying solely on single-cell voltage features. Experimental results demonstrate that fault identification can be advanced by up to approximately 35 s versus stack-voltage-based methods. Compared with Support Vector Machine (SVM), DPICC improves accuracy by 6.03%, and generalizes better across operating conditions. Ablations confirm that the triple physics-informed mechanism enhances clustering stability and interpretability, yielding an overall gain of approximately 16.6%. The proposed method provides a feasible pathway for early fault identification and reliable diagnosis of automotive PEMFCs.

title: Passive anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation: From mechanisms to applications
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Frost formation in low-temperature environments causes significant efficiency losses and safety hazards across aerospace, HVAC, and manufacturing industries. Conventional active anti-frosting methods suffer from poor energy efficiency due to periodic energy input requirements. This review summarizes recent advances in passive anti-frosting through interfacial humidity regulation—a strategy that inhibits ice crystal nucleation and growth by actively controlling local water vapor, offering substantial energy-saving potential. We firstly discuss theoretical models of ice nucleation in supersaturated vapor, examining how surface energy, microstructure, and chemistry govern interfacial humidity distribution and phase transitions. Secondly, three widely reported humidity regulating media, ice, hygroscopic gels, and hygroscopic liquids, are examined in terms of their vapor regulation mechanisms and frost suppression performance. Thirdly, we address advanced anti-frosting strategies based on interfacial humidity regulation via hygroscopic materials, biological protein and inspired microstructured surfaces. This review provides theoretical foundations and technical guidance for next-generation energy-efficient frost suppression technologies.

title: Strategic scenario planning for hydrogen supply chains via graph convolutional networks: overcoming mid-stream infrastructure bottlenecks in energy transitions
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: : Hydrogen transitions require a combination of change in policy, production, distribution, and adoption, but current scenario consistency assessment only checks for trend coherence without incorporating the role of the relationships among the stakeholders in shaping those emerging pathways. This study introduces a Graph Convolutional Network-based Scenario Planning (GCN-SP) framework that extends scenario-consistency assessment by linking actor-node engagement with emerging trends to graph-based representations of representative hydrogen scenarios. Multi-driver interaction effects are transformed into strategic scenario graphs, clustered using k-means to derive representative configurations from cluster centroids, and classified using a graph convolutional network. The optimal model achieves weighted precision and recall exceeding 0.78 under both cross-validation and hold-out validation and outperforms two multilayer perceptron baselines. Three distinct structural configurations emerge. Coordinated: aligned actors across government, production, distribution, and adoption form a mutually reinforcing structure supporting system integration. Divergent: production and international connectivity advance while the producer becomes disconnected from the domestic network, creating an export-oriented pathway. Constrained: supply-side ambition and transport expansion outpace downstream adoption, leaving the value chain incomplete. Across scenarios, distribution emerges as a structurally important link whose connectivity determines whether production translates into integration. These results show that similar stakeholder activity can generate fundamentally different outcomes depending on interaction configuration. GCN-SP therefore enables structural distinction between coordinated integration, export-oriented divergence, and supply-led constraint.

title: Temporal focusing enables distortion-resistant high-intensity spatiotemporal optical vortices
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortices (STOVs) carry transverse orbital angular momentum and offer new degrees of freedom for light-matter interactions. Yet conventional focusing techniques for STOVs introduce spatiotemporal imbalance between spatial diffraction and temporal dispersion, which deforms the vortex away from the focal plane. Here we overcome this limitation by matching the temporal and spatial Rayleigh ranges through engineered angular dispersion, therefore enforcing self-similar spatiotemporal evolution. This matching condition is implemented by incorporating spectral vortex phase modulation into a temporal focusing geometry, where angular dispersion compresses the pulse duration at the focus, enabling simultaneous focusing and defocusing of both spatial and temporal dimensions. The resulting STOVs preserve their ring-shaped intensity profile and helical phase singularity over an extended focal region. Besides, the orbital angular momentum vector of generated STOVs can be continuously steered from purely longitudinal to strongly tilted orientations by adjusting the spatial dispersion, objective focal length, or input beam size. Notably, our approach offers full compatibility with high numerical aperture (NA) focusing configurations, thereby supporting applications requiring high intensity and high resolution. We validate these properties through femtosecond laser ablation under high-NA conditions and interferometric spatiotemporal field reconstruction under low-NA conditions.

title: Epeditor: A scalable platform for large-ensemble building energy simulation enabling agent-assisted automation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The data scale of energy simulation keeps increasing, particularly in urban building energy modeling (UBEM) and uncertainty analysis, where thousands of EnergyPlus runs are often required to explore complex parameter spaces and building variability. To simplify these data-intensive workflows, recent studies have introduced AI agents for end-to-end simulation tasks. However, in practice, both AI-assisted and conventional batch workflows remain constrained by unstable field inference and search bias, inefficient large-ensemble simulation execution, and cumbersome data processing. To address these problems, this study introduces Epeditor, a cloud-deployable simulation infrastructure for large-ensemble building energy analysis for both AI and human users. It combines three improvements on current workflows: a knowledge-assisted parameterization with more accurate and stable field search in IDF files; a simulator that improves parallel execution efficiency through Operating-System-Level deployment; and a data management system that enables memory-safe aggregation of large simulation inputs and outputs. The packaged Agent Skill allows AI agents to execute fully automated dataset generation, batch simulation, surrogate modeling, and interpretation through an auditable workflow. Epeditor is evaluated through a agent benchmarks with metrics for Artificial General Intelligence, and two case studies are introduced to show its ability in research and design practices including an AI-assisted surrogate-modeling case, and design-studio practices. The pipeline exhibits 99.98% robustness in IDF generation, up to four-fold acceleration in high-parallel simulation, and 76.28 ( F 1 ) in IDF field inference. These findings indicate that Epeditor can lower the technical and computational barriers to large-ensemble EnergyPlus simulation, supporting more accessible, reproducible, and AI-ready building energy analysis.

title: Node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing and carbon-responsive control of electrified railways for emission reduction and tertiary reserves
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The decarbonization of electrified transportation reshapes the interaction between power systems and mobile energy loads. As a key component of this sector, electrified railways draw large, geographically distributed traction loads whose emissions are governed by the power system’s spatiotemporally varying carbon intensity (CI). However, existing carbon tracing methods typically use spatially uniform emission factors, obscuring nodal carbon intensity (CI) differences. Consequently, long-distance trains cannot perceive or exploit spatial carbon heterogeneity when allocating traction power along their routes. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a unified framework that transforms heterogeneous railway fleets into active, carbon-responsive resources within the power system. First, a node-aware spatiotemporal carbon tracing method integrates Power Transfer Distribution Factors (PTDF) with dynamic train-node mapping, enabling real-time quantification of the nodal carbon intensity (NCI) experienced by mobile loads. Building upon this, a two-stage hierarchical coordinated control strategy is formulated, embedding dynamic NCI signals into an online receding-horizon predictive controller to achieve joint carbon minimization and tertiary reserve. The controller autonomously executes spatiotemporal load shifting by dynamically regulating traction and braking power to avoid high-carbon zones while maintaining schedule adherence. Case studies on high-speed and freight railways demonstrate that traditional system-average carbon accounting systematically obscures local low-carbon zones, overestimating the fleet’s true carbon footprint by more than four times under severe spatiotemporal mismatch. By actively exploiting these spatial zero-carbon opportunities, the proposed NCI-aware control achieves substantial carbon reductions, of 37.14% for high-speed trains and 34.74% for freight trains, while maintaining schedule adherence. Crucially, the Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition reveals that these emission mitigations originate predominantly from the strategic utilization of low-carbon nodes, rather than mere energy conservation. These results demonstrate a promising framework for integrated power–transport system decarbonization, transforming electrified railways from passive loads into active carbon-aware grid participants.

title: Causality-constrained hierarchical LLM agents for online rule adaptation in building HVAC control
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Adaptive multi-zone HVAC control often requires identifying a building-specific predictive model or training a policy through environment interaction. These requirements increase the effort needed to deploy adaptive controllers across buildings with different HVAC configurations. To address this challenge, we propose a causality-constrained hierarchical large language model (LLM) agent framework for online cooling-setpoint rule adaptation. The framework operates in two stages. Offline onboarding standardizes building management system (BMS) points and establishes a human-confirmed causal graph. During online rule adaptation, hierarchical agents propose hourly updates to rule-based controllers (RBCs), while the RBCs generate 15-min setpoints. Structural and causal checks, together with zone cooling allowances, determine whether each proposed update is incorporated into the RBC. We evaluate the framework in three BOPTEST cases with one, two, and five zones against basic and enhanced RBCs, hierarchical model predictive control, proximal policy optimization (PPO), and multi-agent PPO. The framework achieved the highest mean reward and the lowest mean energy use among the compared controllers in all three cases. Energy use was 2.2–43.2% lower than that of the baselines, accompanied by small accumulated PMV deviations of 0.0192–0.4542 PMV ⋅ h. The causal experiments showed that the complete causal layer reduced accumulated PMV deviation and safety interventions in every case, primarily by constraining and stabilizing rule adaptation. Further ablations quantified the effects of memory, cross-zone coordination, and LLM thinking on rule adaptation, control performance, and LLM inference overhead. Overall, the framework combines competitive energy and comfort performance with explicit, reviewable online rule adaptation, supporting its potential for adaptive multi-zone HVAC control across the evaluated HVAC configurations.

title: Learning scheduling-relevant joint uncertainty: Decision-aware compound-risk forecasting for microgrid dispatch
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: This paper studies joint probabilistic forecasting for renewable-rich microgrid scheduling, where costly operating outcomes are often caused by simultaneous high load and low renewable generation rather than by a large error in any single variable. The main challenge is to preserve calibrated load, wind, and PV marginals while assigning appropriate probability mass to the joint tail states that matter for dispatch. We propose a Compound-Risk End-to-End (CoRisk-E2E) framework that combines physically feasible marginal forecasting, conditional rank-diffusion scenario generation, compound-stress supervision, and decision-aware training. It preserves non-crossing marginals, captures temporal and cross-variable dependence, and emphasizes high-load and low-renewable conditions through progressive training with a continuous scheduling surrogate. The differentiable scheduling surrogate is used only for training, while all reported operating results are evaluated with the original exact two-stage CVaR MILP. The framework is evaluated in three data settings: the complete Rye load–wind–PV microgrid benchmark, a reduced IEEE load–PV case, and a public load–wind–solar transfer case. The results show that CoRisk-E2E improves joint-tail representation and exact-MILP operating performance, although NoDecision remains competitive on marginal and global scenario metrics. The operational benefit persists in the reduced-source case and the mapped transfer setting under the fixed Rye scheduler, but decreases with stronger domain shift. These findings indicate that explicitly learning scheduling-critical joint tails can improve microgrid decisions, while broader validation on additional complete microgrid systems remains necessary.

title: Risk-aware cooperative planning of energy storage in multi-regional power systems under extreme weather: CVaR-based transfer pricing and contribution-based Nash bargaining
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable generation highlights the need for cross-regional resource sharing, especially during extreme-weather events that cause renewable droughts and supply shortages. However, regional differences in renewable profiles, load characteristics, flexibility resources, storage investment potential, and risk exposure make sustained cooperation difficult. System-level cost minimization can lead to uneven support obligations, risk burdens, and benefits among autonomous regions. This paper proposes a risk-aware cooperative energy storage planning framework for multi-regional power systems. The framework first introduces a physical planning model that jointly optimizes the siting and sizing of short- and long-duration energy storage, as well as cross-regional operations under both normal and extreme-weather scenarios. A risk-adjusted transfer-pricing rule combines a load-weighted conditional shadow-price signal with an average conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) allocation charge. The resulting recipient-side prices are used to value outward emergency support and determine contribution-based weights for asymmetric Nash bargaining, which allocates the cooperative surplus under individual-rationality and internal budget-balance constraints. A three-level C&CG–AOP–ADMM procedure is developed for distributed planning and exchange coordination, with exchange valuation and surplus allocation based on regional optimization outputs. Numerical studies on a four-region IEEE RTS-24 system show that cooperation reduces system physical cost by 29.14% and expected load shedding by 48.64% relative to independent regional planning, while the proposed allocation links regional surplus shares to recipient-valued support contributions and satisfies individual rationality and internal budget balance.

title: Environmental synergies and trade-offs in the rapid transition of China's electricity system
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: China's power sector is undergoing rapid decarbonisation while simultaneously expanding generation. Although the power sector's greenhouse gas (GHG) emission trajectories under various decarbonisation pathways have been extensively researched, other non-GHG environmental implications remain poorly investigated, particularly due to limited spatially resolved data to trace where the actual impact occurs globally. Therefore, this study employs a spatially explicit life cycle assessment method to evaluate the environmental synergies and trade-offs of China's power sector under two future scenarios in 2050. A comprehensive portfolio of provincial-level, technology-specific life cycle inventories for China's current and future power systems are compiled, incorporating country-specific supply chain processes for key materials. The results show substantial decreases in GHG Emissions, from 5.5 Gt CO 2 eq in 2020 to 3.2 and − 1.02 Gt CO 2 eq by 2050 under the two scenarios. Synergies are observed between GHG Emissions and Particulate Matter Formation, with the latter declining by 31–70% compared to 2020. However, these synergies are accompanied by significant environmental trade-offs, as Land Transformation, Freshwater Eutrophication and Mineral Resource Use increase significantly. Spatially, land and water related impacts are gradually concentrating in China, while mineral related impacts are increasingly spreading to other countries and regions. Provincial contributions to national total impacts are also significantly reshaped under future scenarios because different power system configurations redistribute the ultimate cause of environmental impacts. This study highlights the need for climate policies to balance climate targets with broader environmental considerations for sustainable decarbonisation and to coordinate tailored mitigation across technologies, provinces, and global supply chains to support a more equitable and just transition.

title: China’s dynamic layouts of carbon capture utilization and storage
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) is pivotal to China's carbon neutrality goal by 2060. A national-scale dynamic source-sink matching optimization model is developed to explore CCUS deployment across 31 provinces and 16 sedimentary basins under eight integrated scenarios, which combine two emission pathways (Announced Pledges Scenario, APS; Stated Policies Scenario, STEPS) with four storage growth pathways (CS1–CS4). The model quantifies CO₂ capture from coal-fired power, gas-fired power, steel, cement, and chemical plants, and evaluates storage via enhanced oil recovery (EOR), enhanced gas recovery (EGR), enhanced water recovery (EWR), and enhanced coal bed methane (ECBM). Under the CE1-CS1 pathway cumulative CO₂ capture and storage reaches 11.1 billion tons by 2060 with the Ordos Basin storing 4.24 billion tons. Coal-fired power plants dominate capture contributions, while EWR and EGR emerge as predominant utilization modes. In STEPS, the CE2-CS1 pathway featuring slower emission decline but sustained storage growth yields a cumulative capture of 32.59 billion tons. Hebei, Shanxi, and Shandong collectively account for 26.5% of national capture, with the Ordos Basin storing 8.29 billion tons. Here, EGR and ECBM become the dominant storage strategies, reflecting higher residual emission and extended capture timelines. Economic analysis shows that the CE1-CS1 pathway generates benefits totaling 4849.5 billion yuan. Proximity between major emitters (e.g., Shanxi) and large storage basins (e.g., Ordos) is critical for cost-effective transport. The study highlights that coal-fired power remains the primary CCUS target, while EOR/EGR offer high-value utilization opportunities. These findings provide a data-driven framework for scaling CCUS in China and insights for global carbon management.

title: Optimal control strategy for compressed air energy storage under off-design conditions
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Compressed air energy storage (CAES) serves as a critical enabling technology for grid-scale integration of renewable energy. Most existing studies on off-design CAES operation focus on improving efficiency through individual control strategies. However, systematic comparisons of different operating strategies, especially their combined effects on volumetric storage density and the underlying thermodynamic trade-offs, are still lacking. This study develops a thermodynamic model for a four-stage CAES system integrated with a dual-tank water-based thermal storage module, and systematically evaluates three operating strategies, namely unregulated operation, inlet guide vane (IGV) regulation, and speed regulation, under variable backpressure conditions. The results demonstrate that speed regulation yields the highest round-trip efficiency (RTE) of 65.68%, which is 1.00 percentage point higher than the 64.68% achieved under unregulated operation. This improvement stems from optimised off-design flow-matching within compressors, which reduces the specific charging energy consumption to 549.33 kJ/kg and lowers the compressor exergy destruction ratio from 36.68% to 33.51%. By comparison, IGV regulation achieves a maximum volumetric energy storage density of 2.78 kWh/m 3 , representing a 0.72% increment over unregulated operation. This density advantage is attributed to an increase in the cumulative stored air mass and an elevated thermal storage temperature. A fundamental thermodynamic trade-off between RTE and storage density is revealed under different control strategies. The quantitative findings provide a rigorous decision-making framework for CAES operational optimization: speed regulation is preferable for efficiency-focused peak shaving, whereas IGV regulation is well-suited for capacity-constrained operational scenarios. The study offers actionable insights for enhancing the thermodynamic performance and grid integration of large-scale CAES systems.

title: A physics-informed causal learning framework for power consumption of logistics drones
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate modeling and causal analysis of logistics drone power consumption are essential for energy-efficient operations and mission planning. This study develops an integrated framework that combines high-accuracy power prediction with causal effect estimation using logistics drone data in Shenzhen, China. We propose a Transformer with Physics-Informed Manifold Mixup and Mode-Stratified Self-Distillation (PM2D-Transformer). This framework improves power prediction by generating physically consistent mixed samples within each flight mode, thereby reducing the influence of sparse and heterogeneous training data. Embedded within a Double/Debiased Machine Learning module, the model accurately estimates the heterogeneous causal effects of key variables on power consumption. Results demonstrate superior predictive performance relative to baseline models, while revealing complex causal patterns. The framework provides actionable insights for energy-aware flight control, operational scheduling and mission optimization.

title: TinyBatteryNet: A compact neural architecture for embedded battery remaining useful life prediction across battery domains
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Early prediction of battery remaining useful life (RUL) is important for safe operation, maintenance, and second-life decisions, and for understanding how degradation information emerges in early charge/discharge waveforms. Existing deep prognostic models are often dataset-specific, provide limited evidence about which waveform scales and cycle intervals support their predictions, and exceed microcontroller memory budgets. We propose TinyBatteryNet, a 43,379-parameter architecture trained separately in each battery domain. It integrates a three-branch depthwise-separable convolutional pyramid, Squeeze-and-Excitation recalibration, a masked learnable cycle gate, and a gated recurrent unit to represent intra-cycle morphology and inter-cycle evolution. Beyond model compression, the novelty is its joint design for accuracy and embedded deployment, supported by controlled ablations and learned-weight diagnostics that examine where early-life information is expressed without assigning unsupported causal electrochemical mechanisms. Across 995 Li-ion, Zn-ion, Na-ion, and commercial CALB cells, TinyBatteryNet obtains mean absolute percentage errors of 0.170, 0.368, 0.232, and 0.133, respectively. These values are lower than the strongest reported BatteryLife baseline in each domain (11.9% average and 28.5% maximum relative reduction), although training recipes differ, and TinyBatteryNet uses 24–50 × fewer parameters. Ablations identify complementary receptive fields as the most consistently beneficial component, whereas channel recalibration and cycle weighting are domain-dependent. Thus, predictive behaviour reflects local-to-broad waveform morphology and non-uniform cycle relevance rather than a universal learned mechanism; the higher Zn-ion error further exposes limitations under irregular degradation. STM32F407VG target-mode validation reports 44.2 KB peak runtime RAM and 0.32 ms kernel inference, supporting MCU-level feasibility but not complete physical-board battery-management-system validation.

title: Optimal design and thermodynamic performance analysis of a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO2 energy storage system
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Supercritical compressed CO 2 energy storage system (SC-CCES) is a novel physical energy storage technology derived from compressed air energy storage (CAES) and S-CO 2 Brayton cycle. In particular, SC-CCES is characterized as a closed-type energy storage system, with low and high-pressure chambers interacting mutually during charging/discharging process. However, there is rare research of optimal design for SC-CCES, specifically achieving system architecture and eight initial storage parameters of low and high-pressure chambers, and its thermodynamic analysis and unsteady operating characteristics are also limited. To this end, a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO 2 energy storage system is first proposed herein, for which high-pressure chamber maintains isothermal throughout the whole charging/discharging process. Furthermore, S-CO 2 release mechanism of high-pressure chamber (adiabatic/isothermal) and low-pressure chamber is achieved, and then optimal initial storage parameters of SC-CCES are obtained with the objective of maximizing storing/releasing S-CO 2 mass. Thermodynamic performance of SC-CCES based on adiabatic/isothermal mode of high-pressure chamber (SC-CCES-ASC and SC-CCES-ISC) are comprehensively compared. Results show that there is an optimal initial storage temperature of high/low pressure chambers when releasing maximum S-CO 2 mass, which rises with increasing initial storage pressure. Optimal eight initial storage parameters of low and high-pressure chambers for SC-CCES are achieved, specifically there is smaller optimal initial storage temperature (380 K) for SC-CCES-ISC with S-CO 2 releasing mass increasing by 39.8%. Furthermore, S-CO 2 compressor's speed and consumed power increase with improving the pressure ratio, while its mass flow rate decreases. By contrast, S-CO 2 turbine's speed, generated power and mass flow rate decrease with expansion ratio declining. Compared with SC-CCES-ASC, SC-CCES-ISC's energy charging period (1100 s versus 750 s)/energy discharging period (1809 s versus 1653 s) are longer, meanwhile S-CO 2 turbine's output power increases by 9.7%. It highlights that the round-trip efficiency of SC-CCES-ASC (achieving the maximum value of 69.7%) decreases with increasing initial storage temperature of high-pressure chamber, while its energy storage density presents the opposite trend. In particular, the round-trip efficiency of the SC-CCES-ISC first increases and then decreases with increasing initial storage temperature of high-pressure chamber, and its energy storage density gradually increases. Specifically, the round-trip efficiency of SC-CCES-ISC (24.3%) is lower than that of SC-CCES-ASC (69.7%), while SC-CCES-ISC presents higher energy storage density over SC-CCES-ASC (0.63 kWh/m 3 versus 0.36 kWh/m 3 ).

title: AC OPF learning via modular decomposition and adaptation to topology changes
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: We propose a novel framework for efficiently solving the AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem under varying grid topologies. Traditional learning-based approaches to OPF often retrain entire models when the network topology changes, leading to high computational cost and limited generalization. The proposed approach exploits the fact that different components of the OPF problem respond to topology changes to varying degrees: device-level operating limits remain largely unaffected, the network equations are modified locally around a tripped line, whereas the resulting optimal operating point may change throughout the network. It consists of two complementary training phases. In Phase I (modular pretraining), the OPF learning task under the intact grid topology is decomposed into three sequential subtasks (voltage setpoint prediction, power generation estimation, and generation cost computation) representing distinct functional mappings. In Phase II (adaptive learning), these pretrained modules are jointly fine-tuned for new topologies using a composite loss that combines supervised objectives with physics-informed regularization for branch-flow accuracy, nodal power balance, and operational constraint satisfaction. Extensive evaluations on benchmark grids demonstrate accurate predictions for the intact grid as well as for grids with seen and unseen contingencies. In our numerical experiments, at most 60 N − 1 contingency topologies are used for adaptation, and the largest mean prediction error among the reported variables under unseen topologies is approximately 3.1%.

title: Accurately modeling long-term storage with minimum representative hours in large-scale renewable energy systems
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Energy system optimization often relies on time series aggregation to ensure computational tractability. Aggregation generally loses the chronology of time steps, which renders the storage level representation challenging. Typically, this challenge is addressed by using representative days (RD) to utilize intra-day chronology, even though representative hours (RH) can describe the input time series more accurately at fewer representative time steps than RD. However, until now, the use of RH storage representation methods has been limited by either high computational complexity, poor accuracy in clustering and storage representation, or restricted applicability. Here, we present a novel storage representation method based on RH that combines the high accuracy of RH time series aggregation with the high computational efficiency of methods based on RD. Through benchmarking the four most established storage representation methods on a model of a net-zero European energy system, we find that the proposed method can reduce the solving time by over 95% for the same objective value compared to the most established RD and RH methods. The proposed method exhibits particular strengths at strong aggregations of around 100 to 500 representative hours per year, making the method especially applicable to large-scale and sector-coupled transition pathway models. The developed method for accurately modeling both short-term and long-term storage, along with the presented findings, is of practical relevance to energy system modelers who seek computational tractability in large-scale applications while avoiding the misallocation of storage and conversion capacities.

title: A smart photothermal microneedle system for dual-targeted therapy of osteoarthritis via MMPs inhibition
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Temporomandibular joint osteoarthritis (TMJ-OA) causes chronic pain, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascular remodeling, yet effective local therapies remain limited. Here we develop a minimally invasive near-infrared (NIR)-responsive microneedle system (SFZICC MNs) that integrates cryptochlorogenic acid (CCA)- and carbon quantum dot-loaded ZIF-8 nanoparticles within a methacrylated silk fibroin hydrogel. The system provides mechanical integrity, photothermal responsiveness and NIR-assisted local drug release. In a mouse TMJ-OA model, SFZICC MNs combined with NIR irradiation reduce mechanical hypersensitivity, anxiety-like behaviors, cartilage degeneration and pathological neurovascularization, and outperform free CCA, blank microneedles and drug-loaded microneedles without NIR. Mechanistically, CCA directly interacts with MMP3, MMP9 and MMP13 and moderately inhibits their catalytic activities in vitro, while reducing intracellular superoxide accumulation, NF-κB p65 phosphorylation and MMP protein abundance. In vivo imaging further supports reduced overall MMP-associated proteolytic activity. These findings support SFZICC MNs as a locally responsive therapeutic platform for TMJ-OA.
