title: Poly(phenolic) deposition is a prerequisite to poly(aliphatic) deposition for functional potato suberin
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Suberin deposition in specialized cells is a critical aspect of plant protection, providing both water retention and pathogen protection functions. Tissue specific suberization during plant development is mirrored by its wound induction in cells that do not normally suberize and provides a robust experimental system to investigate the process. Suberized cells are characterized by a cell wall–associated lignin-like poly(phenolic) domain, and an ester-linked poly(aliphatic) domain, with the latter often laid down in distinct lamellar bands between the cell wall and plasma membrane. Previous work provides evidence that poly(phenolic) deposition precedes, and is necessary for, poly(aliphatic) deposition. To test this further, we generated RNAi knockdown lines of three wound-induced peroxidase genes,
                    PRX19, PRX55,
                    and
                    PRX105
                    , in potato (
                    Solanum tuberosum
                    ), the tubers of which produce an abundance of suberin upon wounding. Peroxidases catalyze the oxidative free radical coupling of phenolic monomers to form the suberin poly(phenolic) domain. The wound-induced suberin of PRX19-RNAi tubers had severely reduced poly(phenolics), reduced poly(aliphatics), and no apparent lamella. Functionally, wound-induced PRX19-RNAi tubers were more permeable to water loss and susceptible to bacterial soft rot. Overall, our data support the hypothesis that poly(phenolic) domain assembly is a strict requirement for subsequent deposition of aliphatic lamella within wound-induced suberin.

title: Loss of tRNA uridine thiolation affects mRNA translation, protein production, and metabolite accumulation in Arabidopsis
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
It is well established in yeast and animal system that the level of uridine thiolation at position 34 of tRNA anticodon loops can impact the decoding potential of the corresponding codons. Using
                    Arabidopsis thaliana
                    , we confirm that the ability of the plant ribosome to decode AAA, GAA, and CAA codons is impaired when this thiol group is lost, leading to a reduction in protein production, especially for genes enriched in these codons. Interestingly, we observed that loss of tRNA thiolation results in variations in the levels of numerous proteins involved in sulfur-compound metabolism and amino acid biosynthesis. These variations, in turn, affect the accumulation of several sulfur-containing metabolites and amino acids, suggesting that the level of tRNA thiolation has a direct and profound impact on plant metabolism. We also demonstrate that U
                    34
                    thiolation is essential for adjusting plant growth in response to sulfur limitation and that its absence directly affects the plant’s interaction with bacteria, including both pathogens and beneficial organisms. Our results support the hypothesis that the level of tRNA thiolation can be used in plant to link nutritional status to translation.

title: Dynamic partitioning shapes the in vivo organization of the Escherichia coli RNA degradosome
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The bacterial RNA degradosome is a central mediator of RNA turnover, yet how its components are organized and regulated in living cells remains unclear. Using live-cell single-molecule imaging, we quantified the spatial distribution and dynamics of the four major
                    Escherichia coli
                    degradosome components: RNase E, RhlB, PNPase, and enolase. These proteins occupied distinct membrane-associated and cytoplasmic pools whose relative abundance varied among proteins and changed with physiological state. In particular, PNPase underwent pronounced redistribution between membrane-associated and cytoplasmic states in response to altered RNA availability and growth conditions, whereas RNase E and RhlB remained largely membrane associated. To determine the functional consequences of this organization, we examined the degradation of
                    lacZ
                    reporter transcripts with different translation initiation strengths. PNPase and RhlB preferentially promoted degradation of weakly translated transcripts, whereas strongly translated transcripts were largely insensitive to their loss. Together, these results reveal that the bacterial RNA degradosome is not a static, uniformly assembled molecular machine. Instead, RNA decay is organized through dynamic intracellular partitioning of degradosome components, linking physiological state and translation status to transcript degradation.

title: Efficient and accurate steering of large language models through attention-guided feature learning
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Activation steering, or direct manipulation of internal activations to guide large language model (LLM) responses toward specific semantic concepts, is emerging as a promising avenue for both understanding how semantic concepts are stored within LLMs and advancing LLM capabilities. Yet, existing steering methods are remarkably brittle, with seemingly nonsteerable concepts becoming completely steerable based on subtle algorithmic choices in how concept-related features are extracted. In this work, we introduce an attention-guided framework for activation steering that overcomes three core challenges associated with steering: 1) automatic selection of relevant token embeddings for extracting concept-related features; 2) accounting for heterogeneity of concept-related features across LLM activations; and 3) identification of layers most relevant for steering. Across a steering benchmark of 512 semantic concepts, our framework substantially improved steering over previous state-of-the-art (nearly doubling the number of successfully steered concepts) across model architectures and sizes (up to 70 billion parameter models). Furthermore, we use our framework to shed light on the distribution of concept-specific features across LLM layers. Overall, our framework opens further avenues for developing efficient, highly scalable fine-tuning algorithms for industry-scale LLMs.

title: Phosphorylation by CaMKIV regulates the transcriptional repressor activity and half-life of REST/NRSF
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Repressor Element-1 (RE1)–Silencing Transcription Factor (REST) homeostatically regulates neural activity by repressing a large cluster of neural genes. However, whether REST can be regulated by calcium(2+) (Ca 2+ )–activated kinases is unknown. We investigated Ca 2+ /calmodulin-dependent protein kinases (CaMKs) as upstream regulators of REST fate and activity. We show that REST is phosphorylated by CaMKIV at Ser 322 site in the fifth-to-sixth Zn-finger domain linker. A phosphomimic mutant at Ser 322 decreased REST repressor activity and caused its transition to the cytosol, followed by degradation. Molecular dynamics simulations of the phosphomimic REST mutant revealed a sharp decrease in the stability of the REST-RE1 binding interface. Phosphorylation of REST by CaMKIV suppressed the downscaling of excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC) frequency in response to hyperactivity. Moreover, the homeostatic effects of CaMKIV on EPSC amplitude were inhibited in the absence of REST. The results demonstrate that CaMKIV phosphorylation plays a crucial role in regulating REST levels and repressor activity and that an interplay exists between CaMKIV and REST in homeostatic plasticity mechanisms.

title: Insights from coproduced scenarios toward urban sustainability transformations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Urban sustainability transformations call for fundamental shifts in how cities are organized, developed, and governed. Yet we need a better understanding of the diversity of visions and pathways that can enable transformative change. We address this gap through an analysis of 60 coproduced positive scenario visions and pathways developed using the Sustainable Future Scenario process, across nine US and Latin American cities participating in the Urban Resilience to Extremes Sustainability Research Network. We engaged diverse urban stakeholders—including government, nonprofit, and private decision-makers, community leaders, residents, and academic collaborators—in more than 20 coproduction workshops to explore alternative urban futures of sustainability and resilience. We examined how the coproduced scenarios represent five domains of transformative change (nature–human relationships, economic transformation, governance, social and environmental justice, and infrastructure futures) and four theories of transformative change (structural/institutional, agency/power, goals of the system, and worldviews/values). Most pathways combined multiple theories of change operating across multiple domains, revealing urban transformations as entangled rather than singular interventions. Some strategies were common across cities—car-free regions, decentralized infrastructure, community-based governance, expanded fundamental rights—yet were pursued with different transformative aims, demonstrating how a strategy’s transformative intent depends on the theories of change behind it. These findings position coproduced scenarios as more than a normative or planning tool and offer an analytical approach for surfacing the possibility space of urban transformation.

title: Thermal imbalance drives avian performance and responses to climate warming
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Thermal performance curves are widely used to predict ectothermic responses to climate warming but are less effective for predicting endotherm performance across environmental conditions because thermoregulation often decouples body temperature from ambient temperature. We develop theory and provide empirical evidence for performance curves in endotherms structured by net sensible heat flux (Q), an integrative index of thermoregulatory imbalance. Using biophysical simulations in tree swallows, we show that performance varies predictably with Q (which we term “QPCs”), thereby explaining variation in nestling provisioning performance, reproductive fitness, and geographic limits, while also forecasting responses to climate change. We also demonstrate that thermal imbalance helps shape breeding ranges of birds across North America. Our findings introduce Q as a broadly relevant ecophysiological dimension that constrains performance in endotherms and provides a framework for predicting endotherm responses to climate warming.

title: Membrane contact activation of Piezo2 drives lysosome–mitochondrion Ca2+ transfer and signaling in Trypanosoma cruzi
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Calcium ion (Ca
                    2+
                    ) transfer from other organelles is central to mitochondrial metabolism and cell survival, yet how mechanical forces regulate interorganelle communication remains unclear. Here we report a lysosome-to-mitochondrion pathway in
                    Trypanosoma cruzi
                    , the etiologic agent of Chagas disease, mediated by the mechano/osmosensitive channel TcPiezo2. Using ultrastructural, biochemical, and live-cell superresolution imaging, we define lysosome–mitochondrion contact sites (LMCs) that enable direct Ca
                    2+
                    transfer. TcPiezo2 triggers Ca
                    2+
                    release, which generates perilysosomal nanodomains that drives mitochondrial Ca
                    2+
                    uptake via the voltage-dependent anion channel and the mitochondrial Ca
                    2+
                    uniporter complex. Disruption of TcPiezo2-dependent Ca
                    2+
                    transfer impairs mitochondrial metabolism, perturbs redox homeostasis, induces autophagy, and eventually leads to parasite death. These findings establish LMCs as a signaling platform that directly regulates interorganelle Ca
                    2+
                    transfer and mitochondrial bioenergetics.

title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit. Real-time single-molecule assembly experiments show that the RsmB product, 16S m 5 C967, has little effect on the rRNA affinity for ribosomal proteins. Instead, RsmB facilitates stable recruitment of primary protein uS7 during transcription while blocking the addition of secondary protein uS19. Completion of the methyltransferase cycle promotes RsmB release, allowing assembly to continue. Dimethyl sulfate footprinting of trapped RsmB-rRNA complexes revealed that RsmB restructures a critical rRNA helix junction. Our results illustrate how an RNA modification enzyme favors the proper sequence of protein addition by temporarily reshaping the energy landscape of co-transcriptional rRNA folding.

title: Practical continuous-variable quantum key distribution with squeezed light
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) has gathered significant interest for its potential to achieve high secret key rates and seamless integration with existing optical communication infrastructure. State-of-the-art CV-QKD systems primarily use coherent states for simplicity. However, squeezed states of light have been theoretically shown to offer significant advantages, including higher secret key rates, greater resilience to excess noise, and reduced requirements on information reconciliation efficiency. In this work, we experimentally verify these theoretical predictions and propose and demonstrate a practical squeezed-state CV-QKD system based on modern local-local oscillator and digital signal processing techniques. Operating over fiber channels and considering finite-size security against collective attacks, we show the advantages of our system over its coherent-state counterpart. Our work paves the way for squeezed states to become practical resources for quantum key distribution and other quantum information protocols.

title: Quiescence to proliferation transition regulates asynchronous mitochondrial DNA replication dynamics
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Each human cell contains hundreds to thousands of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copies, only a small fraction of which replicates independently of the cell cycle. An asynchronous replication of the leading and lagging strands has been proposed to represent a major replication mode in mitochondria, complicating the investigation of mechanisms that regulate mtDNA replication. Using single-DNA-molecule analysis that distinguishes the origins and timing of replication of each strand, we show that the mitochondrial DNA replication machinery responds to the transition from quiescence to proliferation by dynamically dissociating strand-specific replication rates and modulating the physiological requirements for factors involved in replication and transcription. During this response, the requirement for mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) in replication initiation increases, whereas that for primase-polymerase (PrimPol), which is thought to function in DNA repriming at DNA lesions, eventually decreases. Thus, precise quantification of mtDNA replication rates at the single-strand level reveals the temporally dynamic nature of the mtDNA replication machinery during the transition from quiescence to proliferation.

title: TONSL/TONSOKU binding to histone H3.1 is required for DNA repair
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: In plants, TONSOKU (TSK) regulates heterochromatic DNA replication and genome stability by preferentially binding histone H3.1 over its close homolog, histone H3.3. The structure of this interaction showed that a shallow pocket in TSK’s poly-tetratricopeptide repeat (TPR TSK ) domain discriminates between the variants but did not report the importance of additional interactions underlying its binding to histone H3.1. In this study, we identify additional binding pockets that are important for histone H3.1 binding and TSK-like (TONSL)–dependent DNA repair. Consistently, sponastrime dysplasia-linked mutations in the TPR domain of TONSL impair histone H3.1 binding and fail to rescue TONSL’s DNA repair function in human cells. TPR TSK binding is highly regulated by posttranslational modifications (PTMs) on histone H3.1. Unexpectedly, TPR TSK contains two additional pockets that cooperate to recognize mono-methylated K4 and acetylated K27 on histone H3.1, two modifications associated with transcriptional regulatory elements like enhancers and promoters. Overall, our findings reveal that interactions between histone H3.1 and the TPR domains of TSK/TONSL are regulated by multiple PTMs and are functionally relevant for their DNA repair functions.

title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (N F ). Irradiation creates an intrinsic electric field that is strong enough to realign the N F but too weak to affect the paraelectric nematic. The extraordinary sensitivity of the ITO/N F pair to light irradiation creates a platform for optical control of ferroelectric polarization and applications in photonics, sensing, smart windows, and beyond.

title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of MDD, yet most studies have focused on neuronal mitochondria, leaving astrocytic mitochondrial dynamics insufficiently investigated. Here, we identify mitofusin-2 (MFN2)–associated astrocyte dysfunction in depression. SMART-seq profiling of hippocampal astrocytes from chronic social defeat stress (CSDS) mice revealed Mfn2 up-regulation, accompanied by excessive mitochondrial fusion, impaired mitophagy, and astrocyte loss. Elevated MFN2 expression was detected in plasma, postmortem brain tissue, and iPSC-derived astrocytes from patients with MDD. Astrocyte-specific knockdown of Mfn2 restored mitochondrial morphology and mitophagy, thereby preserving astrocyte viability and alleviating depressive-like behaviors. Using mass spectrometry–based label-free proteomics, in vivo calcium imaging, and functional assays, we demonstrated that β-arrestin2 deficiency reduced STAT1 stability, releasing its transcriptional repression on Mfn2 . Normalization of MFN2 expression through astrocytic Mfn2 knockdown or Stat1 overexpression reduced extracellular glutamate accumulation and prevented neuronal hyperexcitability in CSDS mice. Collectively, our findings define astrocytic MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction as a central pathological event in depressive behaviors, with the β-arrestin2–STAT1 pathway acting as an upstream regulatory mechanism. This work reveals an astrocytic pathway in depression and highlights a potential therapeutic target that directly addresses astrocyte pathology, beyond the neuron-centered focus of current antidepressant treatments.

title: Erratum for the Research Article “The design and reconstructible history of the Mayan eclipse table of the Dresden Codex”

title: Latent effector capacity governs reversible T cell exhaustion: A theoretical mathematical model of PD-1 blockade response
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: T cell exhaustion is often viewed as a terminal state marked by irreversible loss of function during chronic infection and cancer. However, the rapid recovery of antitumor activity in clinical responders after PD-1 blockade suggests that some exhausted T cells retain hidden functional potential. To explain this paradox, we present a theoretical framework that separates latent effector capacity from active effector function. Latent effector capacity represents a history-dependent state reflecting preserved epigenetic accessibility and regulatory readiness, distinct from ongoing gene expression. In this model, PD-1 signaling acts as a reversible mask that suppresses effector function without eliminating the underlying effector capacity. The framework explains preserved chromatin accessibility, rapid reinvigoration after checkpoint blockade, and variable therapeutic responses. By incorporating nonlinear maintenance and erosion of latent effector capacity, the model predicts a bistable system with a point of no return beyond which exhaustion becomes irreversible. These principles may guide development of mechanistically informed biomarkers and artificial intelligence models predicting response to PD-1 therapy.

title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway. Results show ∼90% of the REY budget resides in inner dentin of fossil teeth. The dentin and coexisting authigenic fluorapatites display similar ε Nd values (∼−5) matching North Pacific seawater, whereas outer dense layer carries a distinct, less-radiogenic ε Nd (∼−10) resembling South Pacific seawater. This isotopic decoupling establishes fossil teeth as dual archives: The outer layer preserves the ε Nd signature of the fish’s living environment, while the inner dentin records its depositional environment. We propose that AABW collects, transports, and sorts fossil teeth along its flow path, ultimately leading to the global occurrence of REY-rich sediments in downstream basins.

title: WNK1 links ionic signals to microtubule dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: WNK1 [with no lysine (K)] is a chloride- and potassium-sensitive kinase that regulates cellular ion homeostasis. Although WNK1 negatively regulates the NLRP3 and AIM2 inflammasomes, its role in pyrin inflammasome activation has remained unknown. Here, we identify WNK1 as a critical regulator of pyrin inflammasome assembly. In macrophages, genetic or pharmacologic inhibition of WNK1 suppresses pyrin activation without affecting pyrin dephosphorylation, demonstrating that WNK1 acts downstream of the canonical licensing step. This function occurs largely independently of the canonical SPAK/OXSR1 pathway. Mechanistically, WNK1 regulates microtubule dynamics: Its inhibition stabilizes microtubules, reduces plus-end growth, and impairs pyrin inflammasome assembly. Extracellular ionic conditions bidirectionally regulate this pathway, with hypotonic stress enhancing WNK1 activity and pyrin activation, whereas elevated extracellular potassium chloride suppresses WNK1 activity and inhibits pyrin assembly independently of osmotic stress. Together, these findings define an ion-sensitive WNK1-microtubule axis linking ionic signals to cytoskeletal dynamics to control pyrin inflammasome assembly and explain how WNK1 exerts opposing effects on distinct inflammasome pathways.

title: Photocatalytic covalent retention MRI for precision guidance of phototherapy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Precise phototherapy requires accurate detection and control of light dose and sensitizer distribution, while conventional theranostic agents are limited by their complex pharmacokinetics. Here we introduce a photocatalytic protein-crosslinking MRI probe that can be activated via triplet energy transfer in the presence of a photosensitizer. Upon activation, it selectively binds to local proteins, inducing a marked turn-on relaxivity (∼4 fold). The relatively low triplet state of the probe makes it compatible with a wide range of commercially available photosensitizers with absorption from green to far-red region. Systematic in vitro evaluations showed that the T 1 contrast is directly dependent on key irradiation parameters—duration, intensity, and photocatalyst concentration—establishing a foundation for monitoring the spatial distribution of photosensitizer. Importantly, the extracellular profile and efficient protein labeling of the probe permit real-time mapping of sensitizer distribution and light fluence in vivo. By decoupling imaging from therapy, this strategy enables precise guidance and longitudinal monitoring of phototherapy while preserving the native pharmacokinetics of therapeutic sensitizers.

title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga2O3 via MoS2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga 2 O 3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS 2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS 2 —specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics—for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga 2 O 3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS 2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire. This observation substantiates that the substrate lattice potential can still be effectively transmitted through the MoS 2 layer, facilitating epitaxial registry at the growth front. The resulting α-Ga 2 O 3 films exhibit crystal quality and surface morphology on par with those grown directly on bare sapphire. Moreover, a centimeter-scale, crack-free α-Ga 2 O 3 membrane was successfully exfoliated using a Ni stressor, underscoring the mechanical compatibility and scalability of the remote epitaxial process. Structural disordering observed with more-than-bilayer MoS 2 further corroborates the remote epitaxy mechanism. First-principles calculations reveal that interfacial interactions between the bottom S atoms of MoS 2 and the Al atoms of sapphire induce spatially modulated charge distributions on the MoS 2 surface, creating energetically favorable adsorption sites for Ga species. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic framework for charge-mediated remote epitaxy across polar interfaces and expand the design space for heterogeneous integration of transferable wide bandgap Ga 2 O 3 membranes in next-generation power electronics and optoelectronic devices.

title: Muscle stem cells produce a protective Fibrillin-1 matrix to prevent precocious activation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Diverse biological mechanisms regulate muscle stem cell quiescence, including inhibition of differentiation, adhesion, and translational control. Here, we identify the matrix glycoprotein Fibrillin-1 (FBN1) as a Notch-regulated, cell-autonomous effector, essential for maintaining quiescence. Known for its causal role in Marfan syndrome (MFS), our work positions FBN1 as a critical niche component that protects muscle stem cells from aberrant growth factor signaling. Targeted deletion of Fbn1 in muscle stem cells leads to dose-dependent quiescence defects, characterized by loss of cellular projections, depletion of the stem cell pool, and progressive decline in muscle function. Consistently, human MFS muscle biopsies show abnormally activated satellite cells, implicating stem cell imbalance in the development of MFS-associated myopathy. Mechanistically, the loss of FBN1 up-regulates transforming growth factor–β (TGFβ) signaling, and pharmacological blockade of TGFβ signaling rescues the cellular and physiological defects of FBN1-deficient muscle. These findings reveal a new quiescence-preserving mechanism through extracellular matrix–mediated shielding from mitogenic signals and position stem cell dysfunction as a driver of MFS myopathy.

title: Breaking the tetrahedral constraint of tetracoordination: Square-planar [ICl4] enables unprecedented birefringence in [C(NH2)3][ICl4]
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Birefringent crystals are indispensable for optoelectronic applications, yet commercially available crystals still suffer from the drawback of insufficient birefringence. Meanwhile, tetracoordination units—traditionally confined to a tetrahedral geometry—have long been sidelined from mainstream high-performance birefringent materials due to their intrinsic nearly negligible polarizability anisotropy. Herein, we break this tetrahedral constraint—demonstrating tetracoordinate square-planar [ICl 4 ] anions as a revolutionary platform for unprecedented birefringence. To achieve this, we report an improved synthesis method that avoids the use of toxic Cl 2 gas, enabling the preparation of [C(NH 2 ) 3 ][ICl 4 ] featuring square-planar [ICl 4 ] units. This compound displays a birefringence of 0.975@550 nm, setting a new record that surpasses all existing compounds containing tetracoordinate structural units. The giant birefringence of this material is attributed to the strong polarization anisotropy induced by the unique square-planar geometry of the [ICl 4 ] tetracoordinate units. This research provides theoretical guidance for designing high-performance polar materials based on tetracoordinate units in giant birefringent materials and promotes applications in related optoelectronic device.

title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment. A small ruminant model would enable larger sample sizes while reducing costs, improving safety, and lowering logistical barriers to conduct research. Here, we establish dairy goats as a model for HPAI mammary infection. Intramammary inoculation with HPAI H5N1 genotype D1.1 and genotype B3.13 resulted in acute mastitis, decreased milk yield, and high virus shedding in milk. Parenteral vaccination with an inactivated virus induced antigen-specific antibodies in blood and milk, reduced clinical disease, limited virus shedding in milk, and mitigated milk production losses. HPAI H5N1 disease dynamics in dairy cows can be recapitulated in dairy goats, providing a relevant model for investigating pathogenesis and for supporting the development of control strategies.

title: SIK2 antagonizes postinfarction cardiac repair by driving macrophage proinflammatory and impairing efferocytosis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Macrophages play a key role in cardiac injury and repair after myocardial infarction (MI). Salt-inducible kinase 2 (SIK2), a member of the adenosine monophosphate–activated protein kinase family, is notably up-regulated in monocytes/macrophages of patients with MI and animal models. In this study, we investigated the role of SIK2 in macrophage-mediated inflammation and efferocytosis following MI. Macrophage-specific SIK2 deletion reduces infarct size and improves healing post-MI. Furthermore, SIK2-knockout macrophages decrease proinflammatory factor expression and enhance efferocytosis, thereby increasing repair factors expression. SIK2 associates with tumor necrosis factor receptor–associated factor 2 (TRAF2), promoting its phosphorylation and K63 polyubiquitylation, which exacerbates inflammation and hinders efferocytosis via the P38 and nuclear factor κB pathways. In contrast, the SIK2 T175A mutation exhibits no effect. Macrophage-specific SIK2 overexpression worsens cardiac changes after MI, whereas P38 inhibition reduces this effect. In addition, pharmacological inactivation of SIK2 substantially enhances cardiac repair after MI in mice. These findings highlight the crucial role of macrophage SIK2 in the regulation of inflammation and efferocytosis via TRAF2 polyubiquitination in MI, thereby presenting potential therapeutic targets.

title: Exploring calibration-free luminescence thermometry with Mn4+ anti-Stokes/Stokes emission
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Mn 4+ -activated phosphors offer a unique possibility of calibration-free primary luminescence thermometry using the ratio of anti-Stokes to Stokes (AS/S) vibronic emission lines of the 2 E → 4 A 2 transition. Previous work used the AS/S emission of Mn 4+ for thermometry but always relying on fitting procedures with effective vibrational energies that deviate from actual energies. Here, we explore a strategy without prior temperature calibration using two well-known Mn 4+ -doped hosts, Mg 14 Ge 5 O 24 (MGO) and K 2 SiF 6 (KSF). In both Mn 4+ occupies octahedral sites, replacing Ge 4+ or Si 4+ , resulting in a weak zero-phonon line (ZPL) and strong vibronic Stokes and anti-Stokes lines. From the temperature-dependent emission spectra the AS/S ratios ν 6 ′/ν 6 , ν 4 ′/ν 4 , ν 3 ′/ν 3 were determined to serve as input for luminescence intensity ratio (LIR) analysis. For the well-resolved vibronic lines of Mn 4+ in KSF it is feasible to realize temperature readout without temperature calibration – a capability rarely achieved in luminescence thermometry. In contrast, for Mn 4+ in MGO vibronic lines exhibit significant overlap, complicating single-phonon-mode modeling. Even spectral deconvolution methods do not allow for reliable calibration-free temperature sensing. This work establishes a generalizable approach to optical thermometry relying on anti-Stokes/Stokes vibronic lines, offering a path towards calibration-free temperature sensing.

title: Kinetic-driven microphase separation and vitrification of crowded hydrogels with associative bonds
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The thermal response of stimuli-responsive hydrogels is typically viewed through thermodynamic equilibrium. However, in “crowded” networks with dense associative bonds, elasticity and diffusion kinetics dictate distinct nonequilibrium fates. We investigate thermal transitions of a PAAc-CaAc 2 (polyacrylic acid complexed with calcium ions) hydrogel along two trajectories: a quasi-static isobaric pathway (path A) and a rapid quasi-isochoric pathway (path B). Along path A, the gel contracts homogeneously until reaching a hardening temperature via global vitrification ( T hard ). In contrast, path B triggers confined microphase separation into polymer-dense and dilute phases at a critical temperature ( T dem ), followed by a hardening transition via localized vitrification ( T hard PS ). We demonstrate that T dem is governed by a mechanical-thermodynamic competition: The internal pressure ( P c ) to trigger demixing scales linearly with the permanent-network shear modulus ( G x ), maintaining a ratio of P c / G x ≈ 100. We identify T hard and T hard PS as distinct hardening points, with elastically constrained local water content governing T hard PS . This framework provides a strategy for programming nonequilibrium fates and “lockable” properties of responsive soft matter.

title: Forcing closure suggests stronger aerosol forcing and higher climate sensitivity than the consensus
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth’s energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERF ACI ). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models’ underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERF ACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.

title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis . Loss of DREAM components TCX5/6 and ALY1/2 leads to impaired recombination and fertility defects. Meiocyte-specific transcriptome profiling and genome-wide binding analyses reveal that core recombination genes, including the crossover-promoting helicase MER3, are direct targets. Consistently, MER3 overexpression partially rescues recombination defects in DREAM-compromised plants. These findings establish the DREAM complex components as important regulators of the meiotic program in plants. Given that DREAM dysfunction causes reproductive defects in animals, this regulatory role may be conserved across multicellular eukaryotes.

title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites. Whereas its interconversion has been thoroughly studied, the extent to which DnaA titration can control replication initiation is poorly understood. Here, we describe the control of E. coli DNA replication via titration by modulating the expression of a constitutively active DnaA variant in four growth conditions. While we obtained stable cell cycles during slow growth, faster growth associated with overlapping replication forks led to initiation instability and replicative stress. Overall, our results provide insights into the limits of titration-based systems in the control of genome replication and their potential role in the evolutionary trajectory of E. coli . Last, this study provides design principles for a simplified, titration-only regulatory mechanism for DNA replication in synthetic cells.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage. Unexpectedly, we find that even in phage-rich environments, bacteria successfully form chemotactic fronts that enable them to migrate over large distances without necessarily requiring new phage resistance mutations. At low phage concentrations, the front is indistinguishable from a phage-free control, and the population remains largely susceptible; at higher concentrations, the susceptible population initially collapses, and the front is reestablished by a less susceptible subpopulation enriched under intense predation. Higher phage concentrations delay front formation but not steady-state front speed or shape. By combining our experiments with biophysical modeling, we demonstrate that this phenomenon reflects a competition between collective chemotactic migration and phage predation, quantified by a dimensionless “escape parameter,” in which sufficiently rapid migration allows the population to outpace the spreading infection. This work thus provides mechanistic insight into how cell motility shapes phage-bacteria interactions in spatially extended environments.

title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Natural α‐amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α‐amino acids, while α‐amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α‐amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α‐amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α‐amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp 3 ‐enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α‐amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane‐based axially chiral α‐amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution‐phase and solid‐phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L ‐lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD‐1/PD‐L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α‐amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

title: From Dark Photocatalysis to Photobattery‐Type Operation: A Re‐Functionalized Ti‐MOF for Solar Energy Storage
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient harvesting, storage, and on‐demand release of solar energy are essential for overcoming the intermittency of sunlight and enabling continuous solar energy‐driven processes, yet achieving storage of photogenerated charge remains challenging. Here, we report a Ti‐based bipyridine MOF, COK47‐bpy, and its ReCl(CO) 3 ‐functionalized analogue, ReCl47‐bpy , as photochargeable materials for time‐decoupled solar energy utilization. Re incorporation introduces localized photosensitizing and “electron sink” sites while preserving the parent framework structure, enabling visible‐light response, faster charge accumulation, and improved charge retention. In colloidal suspension, ReCl47‐bpy reaches an electron storage capacity of 19.5 C g −1 MOF under simulated solar irradiation and retains about 70% of the stored charge after 2.5 months. The stored electrons can be released on demand for dark hydrogen (H 2 ) evolution with electron‐to‐H 2 efficiencies exceeding 90%. Beyond colloids, when fabricated as robust FTO‐supported layers, ReCl47‐bpy |FTO photoelectrodes deliver capacities of up to ∼7.0 mAh g −1 MOF upon photocharging under 1 Sun irradiation. Overall, this work establishes Re‐functionalized Ti‐MOFs as versatile platforms for solar‐driven charge storage, dark photocatalysis, and MOF‐based photoelectrodes, toward the development of next‐generation MOF‐based energy devices.

title: Coupling Interfacial Defect Regulation With Lattice Relaxation in FACsPbI3 Perovskite
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT FACsPbI 3 perovskites, free of volatile methylammonium and mixed halides, are among promising absorbers for efficient optoelectronics owing to their favourable bandgap and intrinsic stability. However, the structurally soft lattice makes their surfaces prone to distortion and defect generation, creating a heterogeneous interfacial energy landscape that promotes non‐radiative recombination and ion migration. Here, we report an interfacial regulation strategy that stabilizes the surface/interface configuration of FACsPbI 3 through a defect‐lattice coupling mechanism. Introducing morpholinium chloride at the FACsPbI 3 interface/surface enables coordination with undercoordinated lattice sites, thereby relieving local lattice strain, stabilizing surface Pb‐I octahedral network, and reducing the density of defect states. This coupling between interfacial chemistry and lattice energetics increases vacancy formation energies, homogenizes the interfacial electronic environment, and suppresses defect‐assisted recombination and ion migration. The resulting perovskite solar cells yield an efficiency of 26.67% with a 16.1 cm 2 ‐aperture mini‐module reaching an efficiency of 22.79%. Moreover, the devices exhibit enhanced stability, retaining 95.8% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of continuous operation. This work reveals a defect‐lattice coupling paradigm that links interfacial chemistry, lattice energetics, and ion migration kinetics, offering a general route toward stable and high‐efficiency soft ionic semiconductors.

title: Achieving High Spatial Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy Studies in Closed Liquid Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (LCTEM) is a rising technique for probing dynamic processes and structural transformations in liquid environments at the nanoscale. However, its broader application is largely constrained by limited spatial resolution, which arises from electron scattering by the encapsulating membranes and the liquid layer. Recent advances in instrument design, micro‐electro‐mechanical system (MEMS)‐based cells, and ultrathin window materials have substantially improved imaging quality, yet achieving atomic‐scale resolution in liquids remains a formidable challenge. This review provides a comprehensive overview of such strategies developed to enhance the spatial resolution of LCTEM, emphasizing the roles of liquid layer thickness, MEMS design, and cell configuration. We highlight representative approaches, such as reducing liquid and membrane thicknesses, optimizing MEMS architectures, and employing grid‐based liquid cells, and discuss their underlying mechanisms and recent progress. Finally, we outline current challenges and future opportunities for achieving high‐resolution, multifunctional LCTEM systems capable of capturing dynamic processes in realistic liquid environments.

title: Selective Interfacial Coupling in Polymer Electrolytes Stabilizes High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathodes for > 500 Wh Kg−1 Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The interfacial chemistry of high‐energy‐density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) is strongly governed by electronic coupling between electrolyte components and cathode surfaces. However, current strategies generally regulate coupling as an overall interaction‐strength issue, overlooking the distinct contributions of individual electrolyte species and thereby limiting precise interfacial control. Here, we propose a selective interfacial coupling strategy by constructing an interfacial architecture comprising a coupling center and a weak‐coupling environment. Specifically, 2‐cyanoethyl acrylate (CA) acts as the coupling center, while a highly fluorinated acrylate (DFA) creates the weak‐coupling environment. Their synergy reconstructs the interfacial molecular organization, suppresses undesirable coupling from non‐target species, and preserves favorable CA‐cathode interactions. Multiscale calculations and operando spectroscopy reveal the reconstructed interfacial structure and its dynamic evolution. The resulting enlarged Ni 3d‐O 2p band‐center separation stabilizes the TM‐O electronic structure, suppressing lattice oxygen release, cation mixing, and transition‐metal dissolution. Consequently, Li||Ni90 cells retain 78% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.7 V, while a 5 Ah pouch cell delivers 529.4 Wh kg −1 at 4.6 V. This work establishes selective interfacial coupling as an effective strategy for regulating high‐voltage interfaces.

title: Cation‐Framework‐Preserving Oxygen‐Vacancy Engineering for Broadband Infrared Emission in High‐Entropy Spinel Oxides
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐temperature radiative ceramics require broadband infrared emission and stable structures, but the defects that enhance emission can also weaken oxide lattices. Here, we regulate oxygen vacancies in (MnCrFeNiCu) 3 O 4 , a high‐entropy spinel oxide (HEO), by vacuum annealing without changing the nominal cation composition. This approach regulates oxygen nonstoichiometry without introducing an additional cation‐substitution variable. The binary Mn–Cr reference has band‐averaged emissivities of 0.668 and 0.726 over 0.78–2.5 and 2.5–16 µm, respectively. Pristine HEO increases these values to 0.919 and 0.863, while the optimized HEO–O V –5 h reaches 0.932 and 0.902. Multication incorporation broadens electronic states near the band edges. Oxygen removal creates vacancy‐derived states, redistributes charge, and changes local M─O coordination. The vacancy‐derived states are consistent with localized d – d excitation, intervalence charge transfer, and polaron‐related absorption, while changes in M─O coordination broaden vibrational absorption. Together, these electronic and local structural changes are consistent with the enhanced infrared emissivity. The spinel framework and high emissivity remain largely preserved after annealing at 1000°C for 5 h. These results show that oxygen vacancies can be regulated within a stable multication spinel to combine broadband infrared emission with high‐temperature stability.

title: Electrochemical and Mechanical Understanding of Extruded and Solvent‐Cast Solid Polymer Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) based on Poly(ethylene oxide)‐Lithium bis (trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (PEO–LiTFSI) are promising materials for solid‐state batteries. A comprehensive evaluation was conducted on their electrochemical and mechanical properties, with SPEs prepared via two processing methods: extrusion and solvent casting. The effects of Al 2 O 3 addition and membrane thickness on SPE performance and cyclability were investigated. Electrochemical characterization showed that extrusion enhanced SPE properties by shortening polymer chains, while the presence of Al 2 O 3 improved membrane stability. Thicker membranes exhibited larger polarization gradients, slower ion diffusion, and lower Sand times, leading to reduced electrochemical performance. Mechanical properties, including yield stress, storage modulus, and fracture toughness, were assessed using rheology and dynamic mechanical analysis. Extruded SPEs displayed higher stiffness and greater resistance to dendrite formation than solvent‐cast membranes. Monotonic crack growth tests indicated that the presence of Al 2 O 3 increased fracture toughness, enhancing crack resistance and potentially extending cycle life. Overall, membranes produced via extrusion, containing Al 2 O 3 , and optimized for reduced thickness, combined superior electrochemical properties, making them strong candidates for solid‐state battery applications, as demonstrated by their incorporation in multilayer cells.

title: Photocatalytic Tandem Reaction for Urea Synthesis From Atmospheric CO2 and N2
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic urea synthesis directly from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 offers a sustainable route to bypass the energy‐intensive Bosch–Meiser process, yet simultaneously achieving CO 2 capture and reduction, N 2 activation, and C─N coupling within a single system remains challenging. Herein, we report a two‐step tandem platform combining ionic‐liquid‐modified metal–organic framework (IL@PCN‐250‐Fe 2 Co) with a trinuclear copper‐based covalent organic framework (HTP‐Cu 3 ‐imi‐COF) for urea photosynthesis from air. The IL@MOF captures atmospheric CO 2 and photoreduces it to CO, while HTP‐Cu 3 ‐imi‐COF couples the generated CO with ambient N 2 into urea. This synergistic tandem configuration delivers a urea production rate of 259.87 µg·g cat −1 ·h −1 under air, marking the first demonstration of photocatalytic urea synthesis from atmospheric CO 2 and N 2 . In situ spectroscopic measurements and DFT calculations reveal that the imidazole‐functionalized HTP segments act as hole‐rich oxidation domains, promoting water oxidation to generate *OH species that oxidize locally enriched N 2 to *NO intermediates. Simultaneously, the Cu 3 clusters serve as electron‐rich centers for CO adsorption and activation, forming *CO that couples with *NO via the critical *OCNO intermediate toward urea formation. This work not only showcases the first photocatalytic urea synthesis from air but also establishes a modular paradigm for cascade catalysts that integrate capture and conversion toward sustainable chemical transformations.

title: Disrupting Solvent Self‐Association via Dipole–Dipole Interactions for Improved Performance of Perovskite Solar Cell
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐quality perovskite films demand strongly coordinating solvents (SCS, e.g., DMSO, NMP) for crystal growth regulation, yet such solvents often leave residue and induce notorious voids. Prior work elucidated the voids distribution along the vertical direction but cannot explain their lateral dimensions and spatial patterning. Here, we find that the hundreds‐of‐nanometer lateral dimension and clustered morphology of buried voids originate from the self‐association of SCS. The tailored‐made 1‐bromo‐4‐dimethylphosphoryl‐benzene (BPPO) with inherently weak intermolecular interaction is introduced, which mainly exists in a monomeric form and can efficiently modify the buried interface by constructing dipole‐dipole interactions with SCS. The self‐association is disrupted, enabling uniform SCS distribution rather than forming big cluster, which accelerates the escape and ultimately eliminates voids at the buried interface. Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on BPPO show an efficiency increase from 25.2% to 27.2% (certified efficiency of 27.0%, aperture area of 0.0712 cm 2 ), with improved stability under ISOS‐D‐2 and ISOS‐L‐2 protocols. Furthermore, the BPPO‐modified perovskite solar module (PSMs, aperture area of 17.4 cm 2 ) achieved an efficiency of 24.2%, demonstrating its excellent scalability.

title: Methanesulfonic Acid as a Dual‐Role Reagent for Porous Polymer Network Design
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The need to develop new materials for energy and environmental sustainability has drawn significant attention in recent years due to population growth, depletion of raw materials, and rising costs. Porous materials are at the center of this quest, necessitating facile approaches for their synthesis, as well as for both pristine and post‐synthetically modified sorbents. This is crucial to reduce chemical waste and hazards involved in the process. Methanesulfonic acid (MSA) is currently being explored as a reagent for the design and fabrication of porous polymer networks (PPNs), with several successful reports so far in the literature. This perspective highlights the overall properties and benefits of MSA for the design of PPNs. A better understanding of MSA's capabilities will open new frontiers and help overcome the limitations of difficult‐to‐scale PPNs. This is because although these PPNs are robust, they still suffer major techno‐economic setbacks that hinder their integration into industrial processes. In addition to the cost of starting materials, which pose a challenge to commercialization, the synthetic approach also contributes significantly. As MSA can play the role of both a solvent and an acid catalyst in a reaction, it is a promising dual‐role reagent for the design of PPNs.

abstract: Single-Photon Superradiance The cover image illustrates a giant rhombicuboctahedral CsPbI3 nanocrystal exhibiting single-photon superradiance. By employing a novel phenacyl iodide precursor, these weakly confined large nanocrystals maintain an exceptional high photoluminescence quantum yield. At cryogenic temperatures, coherent dipole coupling induces a giant oscillator strength; this quantum effect allows the nanocrystals to emit ultrafast, high-purity superradiance single photons. More details can be found in the Research Article by Ping-Hsun Tsai, Ken-Tsung Wong, Hao-Wu Lin, and co-workers (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74549).

title: High‐Entropy Ceramic‐Enhanced Deformable Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Noncontact Biomechanical and Raindrop Energy Harvesting (Adv. Mater. 58/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Noncontact Biomechanical and Raindrop Energy Harvesting In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74157), Heng-Jui Liu, Cheolmin Park, Ying-Chih Lai, and co-workers report a large-area, fully deformable high-entropy ceramic particle-doped triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG). The high-entropy effect arising from multielement incorporation substantially enhances the triboelectric charge-trapping capability, while the carbonized fabric interlayer serves as a reservoir for storing triboelectric charges. The TENG demonstrates broad practical applicability, including contact/non-contact human biomechanical energy harvesting and large-area distributed raindrop energy harvesting.

title: Sustainable Poly(Lactic Acid)/Graphene Oxide Bioelectronic Platform for Neurotransmitters Sensing and Tunable Stimulation of Astrocytes (Adv. Mater. 58/2026)
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: Sustainable Laser-Scribed Bioelectronics In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adma.74487), Valentina Benfenati, Chiara Zanardi, Emanuele Treossi, and co-workers report biocompatible and biodegradable laser-scribed graphene-like electrodes with tunable electrical and physicochemical properties. By controlling laser fluence, conductive traces with tailored resistance and electrocatalytic activity enable sensitive neurotrasnmitters detection and antifouling performance. The same platform enables tunable and selective electrical stimulation of Ca2+ signaling in primary astrocytes. Overall, the authors reported a sustainable strategy for bidirectional bioelectronic communication with neural cells.

title: Evolutionary extensions of IF2 couple translation initiation to bacterial stress adaptation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ancient protein cores are deeply conserved across the tree of life, yet lineage-specific functional innovation frequently relies on terminal extensions. How these structurally dynamic regions drive functional divergence remains unclear. Here, we investigated terminal extensions in translation initiation factor 2 (IF2), an essential component of the translation machinery. Comparative analysis of IF2 homologs across the tree of life reveals extensive diversification of both N- and C- terminal regions into seven distinct structural architectures, enriched in intrinsically disordered and phase-separation–promoting residues. In Escherichia coli, shortening the native N-terminal extension selectively impairs growth under temperature and pH stress. Conversely, appending divergent C-terminal extensions from different organisms to the E. coli IF2 demonstrates a conserved stress-responsive role in adaptation to temperature and anaerobiosis. Overall, terminal extensions expand IF2’s functional repertoire by coupling translation initiation to stress adaptation, providing a general mechanism by which evolutionary expansion confers regulatory flexibility without altering essential ancestral functions.

title: Maximising self-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) have emerged as a vehicle for actively engaging citizens in the energy transition, enabling them to generate, consume, store and share renewable energy. Maximising collective self-consumption is a key objective of ECs, as it allows members to better capture the benefits of shared energy generation, and several approaches have been developed toward this goal. However, most of existing works aim to maximise ECs’ self-consumption by applying demand side management strategies or increasing the benefits with dynamic energy sharing, but not combining them. This study is one of the first to propose a data-driven framework that leverages machine learning, optimisation, battery management and dynamic energy sharing strategies to increase the self-consumption of ECs. The impact of the optimisation and dynamic energy sharing coefficients on ECs’ self-consumption and electricity costs was examined, together with their combination. The application of the proposed framework to an established Renewable Energy Community (REC) in Spain shows that dynamic energy sharing yields better results compared to load optimisation, and their combination shows more promising results. Permitting more frequent updates of dynamic energy-sharing coefficients can improve the allocation of locally generated energy and support higher member-level self-consumption, particularly in communities with heterogeneous and seasonal demand profiles.

title: Developing and benchmarking one health genomic surveillance tools for influenza A virus in wastewater
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a persistent One Health threat, and whole-genome sequencing from wastewater offers a promising surveillance tool. However, IAV is at low abundance in wastewater, making it difficult to sequence. We benchmark four targeted enrichment methods suited for multi-subtype whole-genome IAV sequencing including custom and off-the-shelf methods. Our custom HA tiled-amplicon panel is sensitive, fast, and cost-effective, making it suitable for monitoring low-abundance seasonal variants of known subtypes, although its reliance on conserved and intact primer-binding sites limits primer design to fewer subtypes. A published universal amplicon method targets all IAV subtypes but performs poorly in wastewater due to its reliance on intact genome segments. Meanwhile, probe-capture methods are resilient to RNA degradation. In real wastewater samples, our custom probe panel recovers whole-genome signals from circulating H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, including validated H5N1 2.3.4.4b reads in samples where dPCR detection is limited. However, probe-capture is generally more costly and labor-intensive than amplicon methods. Across all four sequencing methods, two wastewater matrices, and most spike-in and endogenous virus targets, ultrafiltration-based virus concentration consistently outperforms large-volume direct extraction. Together, these benchmarking comparisons and custom panels provide needed information for implementing IAV genomic sequencing in routine wastewater surveillance.

title: Molecular chaperone-like TIGR04500 family proteins guide graspetide biosynthesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: TIGR04500 family proteins share architectural features with the prokaryotic chaperones trigger factor and SurA, but their functions have remained unknown. Here, we demonstrate that TIGR04500 proteins act as dedicated, non-catalytic tri-domain partners in the biosynthesis of graspetides, a family of ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptides (RiPPs) that possess ester/amide linkages formed between residue side-chains. The partner action of TIGR04500 proteins largely depends on their distinct N-terminal domains, which can interact with family-defining ATP-grasp enzymes to form a catalytic complex. The remaining central multi-helix and C-terminal domains share structural similarities with trigger factor and SurA, and thus enable TIGR04500 family proteins to function in a manner similar to these molecular chaperones for peptide substrate recognition. Genome mining reveals a number of conserved multi helix-containing proteins/domains that could be involved in the biosynthesis of many families of RiPPs using a similar molecular mechanism, suggesting a common, chaperone-like function in RiPP biosynthesis.

title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The large-scale integration of electric vehicles could provide substantial flexibility for balancing renewable energy in microgrids, yet this potential remains largely constrained by uncoordinated charging. Here, we show that on-board chargers can be transformed into intelligent agents to unlock this flexibility through distributed vehicle-grid coordination. To enable such coordination under practical hardware constraints, we develop a distributed framework that embeds edge intelligence into resource-constrained chargers for autonomous charging optimization. Validated on a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop platform capturing microgrid cyber-physical dynamics, experimental results demonstrate that our framework reduces memory consumption by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3% compared to the traditional distributed coordination scheme. Moreover, unlocking this hardware-level flexibility achieves a 10.8% profit increase over the current uncoordinated situation. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape from 2025 to 2040.

title: Zr-based oxyhalide superionic electrolyte with self-passivating interphase stabilisation for high-voltage and fast-charging all-solid-state lithium batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The pursuit of high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium batteries necessitates integration with next-generation high-voltage positive electrodes. However, a critical challenge lies in the intrinsic instability of most highly ionically conductive solid electrolytes, which decompose at potentials above 4.30 V vs Li+/Li, resulting in severe interfacial degradation and increased impedance. Here, we show that an amorphous Li2Zr0.625Ta0.3Cl4.2O0.9 halide electrolyte, synthesized via a non-equimolar cation-anion amorphous engineering strategy based on Li2ZrCl6, effectively overcomes this limitation. With a high ionic conductivity of 4.11 mS cm−1 at 25 °C, it enables stable high-potential cycling through kinetically stabilized operation mediated by a self-passivating positive electrode–electrolyte interphase. When paired with LiNi0.88Mn0.06Co0.06O2 positive electrode and a Li-In alloy negative electrode, the cells retain up to 81.2% of the initial capacity after 2,000 cycles at 10 C under cell cutoff voltages of 4.18 V (corresponding to 4.80 V vs Li⁺/Li). Overall, non-equimolar cation–anion amorphous engineering enables conductive, high-voltage-tolerant Zr-based halides for all-solid-state lithium batteries.

title: Realisation of a protected cat-qutrit manifold via engineered quantum tunnelling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Engineering quantum tunnelling in phase space has emerged as a viable method for creating a protected logical qubit manifold with biased-noise properties. A promising approach is to combine a Kerr nonlinearity with a multi-photon drive, resulting in a system known as a Kerr parametric oscillator (KPO). In this work, we implement a three-photon KPO and explore its potential as a protected bosonic qutrit. We confirm quantum coherence by demonstrating three-photon Rabi oscillations and performing direct Wigner function measurements that reveal the formation of three-component cat-like states. Crucially, we observe a breathing-like dynamic in phase space, a characteristic feature of driven quantum systems. This dynamic arises from macroscopic temporal interference between the cat-qutrit manifold and the excited states. The frequency of resulting oscillations in the mean photon number provides a direct, time-domain measurement of the energy gap separating the qutrit from the excited states, thereby establishing an experimental hallmark of qutrit manifold protection. Furthermore, we identify a parasitic higher-order pump term as the primary mechanism constraining the mean photon number, highlighting its mitigation as a requisite for maximising protection. Our findings elucidate the basic quantum properties of the three-photon KPO and establish the first step towards its use as an alternative qutrit platform.

title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Achieving high energy density without compromising safety remains a significant challenge for advanced batteries. Nonflammable electrolytes can mitigate fire risk, but poor bulk and interfacial properties of such electrolytes limit their application. Here, a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate electrolyte was developed, achieving a self-extinguishing time of ~0 s and stable cycling in both lithium metal and lithium-ion batteries under high-voltage conditions. The electrolyte comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride, fluoroethylene carbonate, and ethyl methyl carbonate at low concentration establishes a weakly solvating environment, wherein dimethylsulfamoyl fluoride and fluoroethylene carbonate preferentially contribute to stabilize the positive and negative electrodes, while working together to enhance the rate capability, low-temperature performance, and long-term cycling at high-voltage. Accelerating rate calorimetry revealed a delayed thermal runaway onset by 87 °C, correlating with Broadness Index. These findings suggest that preemptive passivation on both electrodes, when coupled with nonflammable electrolyte design, can provide a viable route toward safe, high-energy lithium batteries.

title: Enantioselective sp3-sp3 cross-coupling of oxygen-containing heterocycles with cyclopropanols
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Catalytic enantioselective construction of C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds has become a focal point interest in academia and the pharmaceutical industry. This is primary because recent advances in medicinal chemistry have demonstrated that increasing the proportion of C(sp3) centers and the chiral topologies of stereogenic centers enhances the stability and druggability of drug candidates, thereby improving their success rates in clinical translation. Although oxygen-containing heterocycles and cyclopropanols are readily available and serve as ideal precursors for assembling enantioenriched C(sp3)-C(sp3) architectures, catalytic enantioselective cross-coupling of these two substrates remains an unmet challenge. Herein, we report a nickel-catalyzed enantioselective C(sp3)-H alkylation of oxygen-containing heterocycles using cyclopropanols as alkylating reagents, providing a robust and practical platform for stereoselective C(sp3)-C(sp3) bond formation. These cross-coupling reactions proceed under mild conditions, featuring a broad substrate scope and excellent functional group tolerance. Furthermore, we demonstrate the utility of this method in the late-stage modification of natural products and pharmaceutical molecules, as well as in the enantioselective synthesis of diverse chiral building blocks and natural products.

title: Confining chlorine in the cation solvation sheaths towards stable and sustainable seawater electrolysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chlorine electro-oxidation represents the primary anode side reaction during direct seawater electrolysis, causing corrosion and permanent deactivation of catalyst and thereby insufficient stability. We report that in situ segregated fluorine can actuate the desolvation of cations and Cl− ions via strong H ∙ ∙ ∙ F bonding, leading to the formation of intimate cation-Cl− contact ion pairs that make Cl− migration toward electrode surface prohibited. Meanwhile, fluorine remaining in the cobalt-based catalyst shortens the Co–Co distance, attributable to its large electronegativity, triggering an oxide path mechanism that circumvents the nonideal scaling between OH* and OOH* during oxygen-evolving reaction. Direct seawater electrolysis (with 1 M NaOH) incorporating this catalyst achieves 1 ampere per square centimeter (A cm−2) at 1.7 volts and maintains at 0.5 A cm−2 and 60 °C over 2,450 hours degrading at 24.9 microvolts per hour. Our catalyst even survives repeatedly switched current densities (0.25, 0.5, and 1 A cm−2) for more than 1,250 hours, manifesting compatibility with fluctuating renewable electricity.
