title: Ten protein panel predicts ALS from plasma with high accuracy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Predictive biomarkers are increasingly used to guide clinical trial design, diagnosis, and management of patients with neurodegenerative diseases. We profiled plasma from 632 ALS patients and 160 healthy controls using the NULISA CNS and Inflammation Panels and applied eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) with nested cross-validation and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify disease-associated proteins. A 12-protein candidate panel was refined using SHAP feature importance and absolute quantification, then evaluated in an independent validation cohort (144 ALS, 37 controls). We identified a final 10-protein panel (NEFL, FOLR1, pTau-181, TREM1, VEGFA, NEFH, CALCA, NRGN, LAMP3, and PTX3) that achieved high classification performance (balanced accuracy 98.3%; AUC 0.992). Model performance was driven by plasma proteomic signatures rather than clinical variables and was not dependent on neurofilament light chain alone. Representing over 750 ALS cases, this study supports development of a clinically deployable blood-based ALS screening tool.

title: dITP shifts the assembly equilibrium of Kongming to activate NAD+ hydrolysis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The Kongming (Kom) system, consisting of KomA, KomB, and KomC, protects bacteria from phage infection. KomA collaborates with a phage enzyme to generate deoxyinosine 5′-triphosphate (dITP), which activates the KomBC complex to hydrolyze NAD⁺ and trigger cell death. Recent studies propose that dITP activates KomBC through a simple conformational change. Our findings instead reveal a more dynamic mechanism. Without dITP, KomBC complexes exist in equilibrium between tightly packed oligomers and loosely packed filaments, both inactive. Tight packing accumulates unfavorable electrostatic interactions without positioning catalytic residues for NAD⁺ hydrolysis, whereas loose packing relieves these interactions but leaves catalytic residues misaligned. dITP binding at KomB stabilizes tightly packed KomC cores in the filament while aligning catalytic residues. Therefore, a small-molecule signal activates signaling by shifting the assembly equilibrium of higher-order protein complexes toward a catalytically competent state.

title: Closed Pores as Internal Stress‐Regulation Units for Practical Silicon–Carbon Anodes
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon–carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation‐induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress‐regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon–carbon anodes. Heteroatom‐doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion‐induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li + insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen–doped silicon–carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g − 1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g −1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine–learning–guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed‐pore design. This work establishes closed‐pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low‐expansion silicon–carbon anodes.

title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (GC) are standard first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here we report BicureX (ChiCTR2300073023), a single-centre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of cadonilimab, an anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, plus GC for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTC. Patients received up to eight combination cycles followed by cadonilimab maintenance. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1); secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Sixty-one patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 23.5 months, ORR was 55.7% (34/61; 95% confidence interval, 42.4–68.5%), meeting the prespecified Simon two-stage efficacy criterion. DCR was 85.2%, median DoR 6.1 months, PFS 8.0 months, and OS 15.6 months. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 68.9% and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in 18.0%; no death was adjudicated as treatment-related. Proteomics identified a post-hoc exploratory three-protein response-associated signal without significance after false discovery rate correction. These findings support further randomized evaluation.

title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp 3 )‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS‐based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high‐performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long‐range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self‐assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.

title: Organocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution for the Stereoconvergent Synthesis of N–N Axially Chiral Compounds
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) serves as a fundamental approach in asymmetric synthesis which enables the efficient conversion of racemic starting materials into a single stereoisomer, yet its extension to racemic diastereomers remains a formidable challenge, and reported DKR processes have largely been restricted to substrates bearing a single stereogenic element. Herein, we report an organocatalytic DKR with catalyst‐accelerated racemization and epimerization for the asymmetric construction of significant N–N axially chiral compounds through the merger of a reversible Pudovik addition with an irreversible, stereoselective phospha ‐Brook rearrangement. Under bioinspired peptide‐phosphonium salt catalysis, a wide range of N–N axially chiral products were obtained in good yields and high enantioselectivities. Scale‐up synthesis and product derivatization further underscore the synthetic utility of this protocol. Mechanistic studies support a DKR process involving reversible racemization and epimerization through prochiral intermediates, identify the phospha ‐Brook rearrangement as the stereodetermining step, and reveal key roles of hydrogen‐bonding and ion‐pairing interactions in catalyst‐controlled stereochemical induction. This work establishes a new paradigm for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral molecules.

title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21% Organic Solar Cells
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic‐acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic‐acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular‐assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion‐derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self‐association and improves solution‐state dispersion. At the interfacial‐anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge‐assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface‐potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8‐BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm 2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

title: Hyperbranched Epoxy Topology Enables Covalent Interphases and Penetration‐Locking Thermoset Networks
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent trade‐off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide‐containing dual‐role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual‐phase “penetration‐locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross‐link density. At the fiber‐matrix interface, thiol‐terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol‐ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost‐effective T300‐based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800‐based composites, while T800‐based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.

title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration‐induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high‐entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O‐doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mg Pt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates CO ads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

title: A genetic platform to deconvolve efficacy and toxicity reveals the on-target effects of CDK11 inhibition in vivo
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The cyclin-dependent kinase CDK11 is an understudied kinase that has been the subject of conflicting reports regarding its function in cancer. Here, we combine genetic and pharmacological approaches to demonstrate that CDK11 is a critical regulator of cancer cell survival that is required for RNA splicing and the expression of homologous recombination genes. Inhibition of CDK11 disrupts genome stability, promotes the retention of intronic sequences in mature mRNAs, and induces synthetic lethality with PARP inhibitors. Through integrative analysis of functional genomics datasets, we identify heterozygous deletions of chromosome 1p36 - which encompasses CDK11 and its activating cyclin CCNL2 - as a recurrent and predictive biomarker of sensitivity to CDK11 inhibition. To assess the therapeutic potential of CDK11, we establish a genetically-engineered mouse model that allows us to differentiate between the on-target and off-target effects of CDK11 inhibitors in vivo. Using this platform, we demonstrate that MEL-495R, an orally bioavailable CDK11 inhibitor, induces widespread on-target toxicity, revealing a narrow therapeutic index. Experiments with a chemically distinct CDK11 inhibitor similarly reveal minimal anti-cancer activity at tolerable doses. Together, these findings define CDK11 as a core cancer dependency, uncover a chromosomal deletion that sensitizes tumors to CDK11 inhibition, demonstrate that on-target toxicity limits the efficacy of CDK11-targeting therapies, and provide a generalizable strategy for deconvolving drug efficacy and toxicity in vivo for novel oncology targets.

title: Decoupled Biomass Electrooxidation Over E‐Waste‐Derived Au Enables Low‐Voltage H 2 and Scalable FDCA Production
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low‐potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value‐added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion‐template–assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH) 2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride‐coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural to 5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low‐voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow‐electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm −2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low‐potential aldehyde oxidation from high‐potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low‐voltage hydrogen production with high‐value biomass conversion.

title: Laminated structure design accommodates thermal expansion mismatch for mechanically and thermally dual-stable thermoelectric contacts
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The quality of the barrier layer (BL) directly determines the long-term stability of thermoelectric (TE) modules. Conventional BLs struggle to simultaneously achieve thermal expansion matching with TE materials and robust diffusion-blocking capability. Here we show a bimetallic multilayer BL strategy that ensures thermal expansion matching while constructing a controllable interfacial stress field to inhibit element diffusion. Taking skutterudite (SKD) as an example, we construct a BL with alternating Nb and Cu layers, in which Nb serves as the primary diffusion barrier, while Cu tailors the effective thermal expansion behavior and regulates the stress field at the SKD/Nb interface via Nb/Cu back stress, thereby achieving mechanical stability and a strong diffusion-blocking effect. After aging at 823 K for 60 days, the SKD/Nb-Cu interface remains intact and maintains a low contact resistivity ( 2Te3- and GeTe-based TE systems, demonstrating its universality.

title: Vitamin C‐Induced Photo‐Redox Threshold Enables High‐Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter‐scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell–matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible‐light‐activated Ru(II)bpy 3 2+ /sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near‐immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L‐ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo‐redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high‐fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post‐printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post‐printing and cell‐laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell‐instructive 3D microenvironments.

title: Two-stage random forest framework for offshore platform identification to analyze spatial patterns and activity levels
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Offshore oil and gas platforms constitute critical infrastructure for national energy resource development, with their spatial density and operational activity exerting direct influence on national energy production capacity and the stability of maritime energy corridors. This study develops a multi-source remote sensing framework for identifying and analysing global offshore oil and gas platforms, integrating Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, and VIIRS nighttime light imagery. A two-stage random forest approach is used for platform identification, supporting the construction of a global long-term platform dataset and subsequent spatial and temporal analyses. Utilizing monthly VIIRS nighttime light time series from 2017 to 2024, platform activity patterns are characterized through a radiometric contrast approach, revealing temporal variations and distinct seasonal characteristics across major producing countries. Furthermore, a framework for analysing the global spatial patterns of offshore oil and gas platforms was developed. Using the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) as the basic unit of analysis, the framework employs indicators including platform density, average nearest-neighbor distance, nearest-neighbor index, and local clustering intensity to quantitatively characterize their spatial distribution and clustering characteristics, revealing regional differences and spatial heterogeneity in offshore oil and gas development. The multi-source remote sensing framework and quantitative analyses developed in this study provide a consistent basis for characterising the global spatial and temporal patterns of offshore oil and gas platforms, and may support further research on offshore energy development, marine spatial planning, and related resource management.

title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long‐Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n ‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10‐DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high‐LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.

title: Closed-loop photoreactor design enabled by machine learning and digital twins
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Designing efficient photoreactors remains challenging due to the complex interplay of reflection, scattering, and absorption. Here, we introduce a closed-loop workflow integrating ray-tracing digital twins with multi-objective Bayesian optimization to design photoreactors with high photon capture and uniform irradiation. A digital 3D reactor model is calibrated using measured emission characteristics, reflectivity data, and geometrical properties and validated against potassium ferrioxalate actinometry. The validated model explores reflector shape and vial positioning, identifying geometries that maximize incident photon flux while maintaining homogeneity across 16 vials. Experimental validation using a photocatalytic Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling shows that reaction yields track simulated photon flux. The optimized reactor is further applied to quantum-yield screening, enabling mechanistic insights across diverse conditions in a single experiment. This work establishes an experimentally validated virtual co-design framework in which machine learning and digital twins accelerate photoreactor development and support quantitative understanding of photochemical processes.

title: Projected intensification of soil salinization in global drylands under future aridity increase
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Soil salinization threatens agricultural production, water management, and ecosystem health. Yet, how increasing aridity will reshape 21st-century soil salinity patterns across drylands, particularly in croplands, remains unclear. Here, we compile a relatively comprehensive global soil salinity dataset from the past two decades, projecting future dryland soil salinity dynamics using climate-driven machine learning models with multiple covariates, including dynamic dryland extent and human influences. Our results show an 8% expansion of global drylands saline soils under increasing aridity by 2100 (SSP5-8.5) relative to 2004–2023. Southwestern US, Mexico, southern Europe, central South America, eastern and southern Africa are highest-risk hotspots. We further show dryland croplands face serious salinization, especially irrigated systems, where half of these newly salinized areas project more than 4.9% (maize), 17.2% (dryland rice), 3.3% (sorghum), and 21.2% (wheat) potential production losses. Our findings inform long-term adaptation strategies to mitigate emerging salinization risks and sustain water and food security.

title: Controlling the shell growth mechanism and interfacial oxidation of InAs/ZnSe quantum dots for shortwave infrared emission
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr−1 m−2, alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

title: Dynamics-aware scheduling of renewable electrolyzer plants: A physics-informed reinforcement learning approach
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Producing hydrogen via renewable electrolyzer plants (REPs) is crucial for reducing carbon emissions in industrial sectors. Meanwhile, with renewable energy generation and electrolyzer units integrated at a common grid connection, these plants provide high-quality resources for regulating power grid operations. Nonetheless, fully utilizing this potential relies on the profitable operation of REPs across joint energy and frequency containment reserve markets in conjunction with the application of data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) scheduling approaches to counteract the stochasticity in renewable generation and the volatility of markets. However, current scheduling frameworks often neglect detailed internal thermal-electrical dynamics and discrete operational states, which result in sub-optimal or physically infeasible policies. The present work addresses this issue by proposing a comprehensive imitation-enhanced RL (IE-RL) scheduling framework. First, the framework incorporates a physics-informed neural network surrogate model to capture transient electrolyzer dynamics accurately. Then, the operational environment is decoupled into continuous subspaces based on whether the electrolyzer unit is in the on state or in the standby state, and dedicated expert policies are pre-trained for each operational environment. Finally, the IE-RL agent is trained to imitate the expert policy matching the current active operational state accurately. The results of numerical computations demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances joint-market profitability while maintaining high physical fidelity with a significantly accelerated training process.

title: Unique features of EIGHT fold—Proteins with the most complex 8 3 knotted topology
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Herein, we present three crystal structures of the most complex knotted protein to date, an 8 3 knot with eight crossings, which belongs to a clasp knot family. The fold of this protein is also unique, and we call it the EIGHT fold (Extraordinarily Intricate Globular Helical Tangled fold). The 8 3 knot is found only in a certain group of bacteria, where it is strictly conserved, despite sequence identities as low as 10%. The 8 3 structure shows a high level of internal symmetry, with structurally analogous halves. It is possible that the EIGHT fold evolved from a single unknotted “half” that duplicated and formed a complex protein. Based on an in vitro study of three selected 8 3 proteins, we estimated their thermal and thermodynamic stability, and showed that they follow a two-state unfolding model under equilibrium conditions and their refolding occurs to a compact, nonnative state. Unfolding kinetics of 8 3 knotted proteins reveal a complex, multiphase process spanning milliseconds to days. Six kinetic phases were resolved using stopped-flow fluorescence and far-ultraviolet absorbance circular dichroism spectroscopy, highlighting both rapid early events and slower rearrangements in secondary and tertiary structures. Finally, with a structure-based model, we showed that proteins with an 8 3 knot can self-tie through a 6 1 knotted intermediate state. They can also self-untie, albeit via an additional intermediate knot such as 4 1 . Nevertheless, these proteins do not seem to fit with current folding theories known to date and require the development of a new approach.

title: Toward cooler cities by larger homogeneous functional clusters
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Urban heat island (UHI) intensifies heat-related risks and environmental degradation in cities worldwide, yet existing mitigation strategies have largely overlooked how the spatial scale of homogeneous functional building clusters influences local climate. This scale may matter because buildings with similar functions often share similar morphology, activity schedules, and anthropogenic heat-release patterns, allowing their spatial contiguity to shape ventilation and heat accumulation. Here, we introduce the Urban Homogeneous Scale (UHS)—an indicator that measures the spatial scale of contiguous, functionally similar building clusters—and analyze 233,844 observations across 101 global cities to assess its potential for mitigating surface UHI. We find that larger UHS is associated with lower surface UHI: every 100-meter increase in UHS corresponds to 4.5% decrease in daytime UHI. This daytime cooling effect is particularly more pronounced in inland, humid, and high-income regions. In low-income regions, larger building area and higher building volume more strongly weaken UHS cooling capacity than in wealthier regions, revealing a socioeconomic inequality in UHS’s mitigation benefits. Our findings identify the spatial scale of building clusters as a essential dimension of urban form associated with urban heat burden, and suggest that considering UHS alongside targeted controls on built environmental characteristics may inform future heat-mitigation planning.

title: Historical trends show more declining than increasing species among European pollinators
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Anthropogenic global change presents a growing threat to insect pollinators. Yet, long-term, continental-scale assessments of their population trends remain limited. Here, we leveraged a curated database of over four million occurrence records, covering 88% of extant bee and hoverfly species in Europe, to assess persistence, richness, and occupancy trends over the past century. Species persistence at the European level was relatively high, with modern records available for 87% of bee and 89% of hoverfly species. Regional richness changes were modest, with declines in the Atlantic and Continental regions for both pollinator groups. Recent increases were observed in the Alpine region for bees, but species richness remained largely stable elsewhere. At the species level, however, a more concerning picture emerged: Most bee species and about half of hoverfly species declined in occupancy. Species traits explained little variation in these trends, although there was a weak tendency for cold-adapted bees to show steeper declines than warm-adapted ones. Genera showing some of the steepest declines include parasitic or dietary specialists, though neither of these traits significantly predicted occupancy trends. Overall, we highlight clear warning signs of species population declines, but with potential recovery opportunities if we take urgent actions to reverse those trends.

title: mechanoLight: A genetically encoded fluorescent biosensor for visualizing 5-HT2AR mechanotransduction in live cells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) are pivotal sensors of the mechanical environment, yet how they sense and transduce physical stimuli into biochemical signals within live cells remains largely elusive. Here we introduce mechanoLight, a genetically encoded red fluorescent biosensor designed to report the mechanical activation of the 5-hydroxytryptamine 2A receptor (5-HT2AR). By incorporating a circularly permuted mApple (cp-mApple) into the third intracellular loop of 5-HT2AR with the optimized linker (m-linker), mechanoLight selectively detects conformational changes of 5-HT2AR in response to fluid shear stress while exhibiting minimal sensitivity to 5-HT. In sharp contrast, psychLight2, the previously developed green 5-HT2AR biosensor, primarily detects ligand-induced 5-HT2AR activation, suggesting that mechanoLight and psychLight2 capture distinct conformational modes of 5-HT2AR activation. Integrated analysis of linker-swapping experiments, structural modeling, and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the flexibility of the m-linker underlies the mechanosensitivity of mechanoLight. We further extend this strategy to other mechanosensitive GPCRs, enabling visualization of their mechanoreactivity in live cells. The mechanoLight signal reflects the mechanosensitivity of 5-HT2AR, as shear stress-induced 5-HT2AR activation triggers Gα q -dependent signaling pathways, including phospholipase C (PLC) activation, intracellular Ca 2+ mobilization, and ERK phosphorylation. Mutational analysis further identifies N-terminal glycosylation and helix 8 as structural determinants of 5-HT2AR mechanotransduction. Together, our findings establish 5-HT2AR as a mechanotransducer and introduce mechanoLight as a powerful tool for deciphering the molecular principles of GPCR mechanotransduction in live cells.

title: Identification and characterization of neoplastic cells in keratin-positive giant cell–rich tumors
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Keratin-positive giant cell–rich tumor (KPGCT) is a newly described bone and soft tissue tumor. The tumor is characterized by scattered keratin-positive cells and the presence of HMGA2::NCOR2 fusions. It is not known if the HMGA2::NCOR2 fusion is located in the keratin-positive cells, and little is known about how KPGCT develops. KPGCT shares some histologic features with tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT), a soft tissue tumor with CSF1 rearrangements. Single-nuclei RNA sequencing and Xenium spatial transcriptomics were used to elucidate the most likely mechanisms driving KPGCT and compare KPGCT to TGCT. We identified a population of cells coexpressing keratin, HMGA2 , and CSF1 as the likely neoplastic cells; these cells constitute the minority of the cells in the tumor. These cells express no synovial markers, confirming KPGCT as a distinct entity, separate from TGCT. The bulk of the tumor consists of CSF1R -expressing macrophages and multinucleated giant cells (MNGCs), suggesting an important role for CSF1–CSF1R signaling. In addition, we find that the likely neoplastic cell population shows activation of the hippo signaling pathway, a possible central pathway in KPGCT tumorigenesis. The CSF1–CSF1R axis likely stimulates the migration and proliferation of macrophages, which form the majority of cells in the tumor, as well as their differentiation into MNGCs. These results provide a rationale for the use of CSF1R inhibitors, which have already shown efficacy in TGCT, as a therapy for KPGCT.

title: Leveraging existing grid infrastructure for rapid US renewable and storage deployment
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Rapid electricity demand growth, grid connection delays, and supply chain constraints create a serious risk of supply shortages and rising electricity costs in the next few years. This paper studies the strategy of adding colocated renewables and storage at existing power plants to take advantage of spare grid capacity. Using satellite imagery, we assess solar and wind potential near 3,890 U.S. fossil and renewable plants. By 2030, we find that existing fossil plants could host up to 597 GW of economically viable solar and wind without exceeding the existing interconnection capacity of each site. Existing renewable plants could host an additional 260 GW of firm capacity—comprising storage paired with added solar and wind capacity. These additions could accelerate clean energy deployment and enhance reliability and affordability, but realizing this potential is contingent upon regulatory reforms and coordinating the operational constraints of colocated resources.

title: Scientists disrupt less but more persistently with career aging
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Disruption describes the extent to which a scientific work overturns the prior knowledge on which it builds and leads to a new line of research. A scientist’s tendency to produce disruptive work has been found recently to decline over the career. However, the disruption index captures only how strongly a paper overturns prior work and ignores whether that disruption is later accepted or overturned by subsequent research. The persistent disruption (PD) framework adds this second perspective, identifying work that disrupts prior research and is then consolidated rather than displaced by later work. We examine how PD evolves over the career and find the opposite pattern: The probability of producing a persistent disruptive paper increases with career age. Senior scientists disrupt prior work less often compared to young, but once they do, the disruption tends to persist rather than being quickly superseded. Our results suggest that this reversal feature is due to the experience and we corroborate it across several dimensions of recognition. We also show that, at a fixed level of disruptiveness, the more senior the scientist is, it attracts more citations, social-media attention, and research grants. Nobel laureates also show delayed persistent disruptions. They exhibit high disruptive ability early in their careers, yet their prize-winning work appears years later. This lag further indicates that experience is needed to turn disruptive ability into the field’s most celebrated contributions.

title: Calibration, accuracy, and domain variation across one million collective forecasts from prediction platforms
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Using approximately one million resolved contracts and questions across four collective forecasting platforms, twelve domains, and time horizons ranging from hours to years, we evaluate the calibration and accuracy of collective forecasts in real-world settings. We found that forecast probabilities were overall highly calibrated: events assigned a probability of p % occurred approximately p % of the time. This broad pattern was evident across platforms and many domains, although fine-grained analyses revealed systematic tendencies toward over- or underestimation in highly consequential areas. While this does not mean that forecasting platforms provide certainty about individual events, our findings suggest that large-scale aggregation of judgments contains meaningful information about real-world uncertainty; when examined in aggregate, the predictions generated by the platforms provided informative estimates of event likelihood.

title: Catalytic reactive-hydrogen membranes for rapid capture and hydrodefluorination of six PFAS of regulatory concern
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) persist in aquatic environments due to their ultrastable C–F bonds and poor susceptibility to conventional treatment. Here, we report an H 2 -based catalytic-film membrane that enables PFAS destruction in ambient conditions by generating highly reactive surface (H ads * ) and subsurface hydrogen (H sub * ), the latter stored as β-phase palladium hydride (β-PdHx). Solid-state analyses evidenced β-PdHx formation and related lattice expansion with elevated H 2 chemical potential, revealing a structural mechanism that links hydrogen storage to catalytic defluorination. Mechanistically, the two hydrogen species play complementary roles: H ads * -rich Pd 0 surface enabled PFAS capture through parallel adsorption to maximize interfacial contact with active H, whereas sustained H sub * supplied the energetic driving force for stepwise hydrodefluorination consistent with sequential C–F scission. As a result, across six PFAS of regulatory concern—PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFHxS, PFBS, and GenX—the catalytic membrane converted all contaminants toward fully defluorinated products. Long-chain PFAS were removed and defluorinated more rapidly than short-chain analogs, while GenX showed greater recalcitrance due to its ether linkage, weaker adsorption, and higher average C–F bond dissociation energy; nonetheless, GenX still exhibited removal and defluorination, with the production of 2-propoxypropanoic acid. The system also enabled continuous coremoval of all six PFAS in ambient conditions, with up to 96% removal and 83% defluorination over 58 d. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for how active hydrogen is generated, stored, and deployed in catalytic membranes, and identify engineered H 2 -catalytic membranes as a promising low-energy technology for destructive PFAS treatment.

title: Loss factor-based tandem power generation unit for ionic osmotic energy conversion
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Ionic osmotic energy conversion harnesses salinity-gradient energy through selective ion transport in charged nanochannels. While existing studies primarily focus on high-performance single-unit materials, large-scale applications require integration of multiple units to enhance power output. However, strong nonlinear coupling among ion transport, charge accumulation, and interfacial processes prevents simple linear scaling of individual unit performance, with key parameters and their coupling mechanisms at the system level remaining poorly understood. In this study, a loss factor ( Lf ) is proposed to quantify power loss in tandem power generation units (T–PGU). Based on an equivalent circuit model, a quantitative relationship between Lf and the electrical signal ratios of individual units in T–PGU is established. System parameters are further classified into shared operating and channel-specific categories for investigating power output and energy loss under varying conditions through experiments and simulations. Results reveal a trade-off between maximum output power ( P max ) and Lf with concentration variations. Increasing temperature enhances P max with minimal impact on Lf , while KCl electrolytes significantly improve performance, reducing Lf to 4 × 10 −4 compared to NaCl and LiCl. Additionally, tuning nanochannels with lower current enables simultaneous improvement in power output and reduction in Lf . Based on these findings, an optimization strategy involving temperature elevation, electrolyte substitution, and surface charge matching with pH regulation is proposed and validated, achieving 283% increase in P max and 92.5% reduction in Lf . This work provides a theoretical and experimental foundation for system-level optimization and scalable design of ionic osmotic power generation.

title: Molecular Preorganization Unlocks Reversible Solid‐State Photoconversion in Dianthrylnaphthalene‐Based Molecular Solar Thermal Systems
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems capable of harnessing sunlight, storing it as chemical energy in the form of a photoisomer, and releasing it as thermal energy on demand represent a promising strategy for renewable solar energy utilization both in liquid‐based devices and the solid state. However, the implementation of MOST materials in the solid state is limited by restricted molecular motion in the condensed phase, which hampers the geometrical requirements for photoisomerization, as well as by inner filter effects which can prevent quantitative photoconversion or necessitate long irradiation times. To address these challenges, three dianthrylnaphthalenes were designed to pre‐organize two anthracene moieties in a face‐to‐face geometry favorable for intramolecular photodimerization. This molecular design increased the forward photoisomerization quantum yield compared to ortho ‐dianthrylbenzenes, reaching 32%, while enabling solid‐state switching. In particular, the acenaphthene‐linked derivative underwent quantitative conversion to its higher‐energy photoisomer in both thin films and bulk crystalline powders. Electron diffraction analysis revealed elongated newly formed C─C bonds in the photoisomer, with refined lengths of 1.81(2) and 1.63(2) Å, exceeding the generally observed length of a C sp3 ─C sp3 bond. These results demonstrate how molecular preorganization can overcome limitations of anthracene‐based MOST systems and expand their potential for solid‐state solar energy storage applications.

title: Neuromodulatory control of cortical function: Cell-type-specific regulation of neuronal information transfer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Neuromodulatory systems such as dopamine and acetylcholine enable cortical circuits to rapidly shift between behavioral states, yet it remains unclear how receptor-specific signaling reshapes what single neurons compute. Here, we combined whole-cell recordings from excitatory and inhibitory neurons in layer 2/3 of mouse somatosensory cortex with information-theoretic analyses under frozen-noise stimulation. We quantified stimulus-to-spike information transfer and profiled each neuron across four functional domains: passive membrane biophysics, action potential dynamics, intrinsic adaptation currents, and input feature selectivity captured by spike-triggered averages. Activation of D1, D2, or M1 receptors revealed three main findings. First, neuromodulators altered fractional information and firing output in a cell-type- and receptor-specific manner, demonstrating selective regulation of encoding. Second, unsupervised clustering based on functional attribute sets showed that receptor activation reorganizes baseline functional grouping, consistent with a dynamic computational phenotype. Third, multiset correlation and factor analysis revealed that neuromodulation systematically reorganizes covariance among functional domains. In excitatory neurons, dopaminergic activation decreased coordination between input feature selectivity and other functional properties while strengthening coordination among response-based features such as spike dynamics and adaptation. Inhibitory neurons, by contrast, generally exhibited increased coordination across domains. In unison, these findings identify neuromodulation as a reconfiguration signal that reshapes not only individual cellular properties, but also the statistical architecture linking them across the recorded cohort, thereby revealing a higher-dimensional mode of single-neuron regulatory control in the cortex.

title: Transforming electrified railway into mechanical energy storage for electricity system decarbonization
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Decarbonizing electricity requires vast energy storage capacity worldwide, but constructing dedicated storage assets creates substantial capital, material and embodied carbon burdens. Electrified railways already exchange energy with electricity systems through traction and regenerative braking, but their inherent potential as mechanical energy storage remains unexploited. Here we show that modulation of train operations can transform electrified railways into Electrified Rail-Based Energy Storage. By analyzing 326,034 inter-stop train operations, we estimate its global potential at 190 gigawatts in 2025 and 315–579 gigawatts by 2050. Capacity expansion models for China, Europe and India indicate that it can reduce investment in conventional storage by 11.9–20.0%, corresponding to an extrapolated global value of US$14.9–35.1 billion annually. Without increasing total system cost, electricity systems with this flexible resource could further reduce operational CO2 emissions by 94.3–258.9 million tonnes per year. Electrified railways can therefore complement conventional storage technologies for electricity system decarbonization.

title: Degradation-aware optimization of SOFC operating strategies under off-design balance-of-plant dynamics
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems face significant performance and cost challenges due to stack degradation and the resulting off-design operation of balance-of-plant (BoP) components. This study presents an optimization framework for SOFC operation that explicitly accounts for stack degradation and off-design BoP dynamics. A 10-cell hydrogen-fueled SOFC stack was fabricated and tested under varied flow and humidity conditions to obtain polarization data, which were used to calibrate the system model with an R 2 of 94.7–99.2%. The calibrated model, coupled with surrogate-based optimization, enables time-segmented scheduling of current density and fuel utilization with periodic setpoint updates over a 20-year techno-economic assessment based on levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), electrical efficiency, and lifetime electricity output. The results show that, under the assumptions of the representative case study, the optimized schedules can reduce LCOE by up to 16%, increase lifetime electrical efficiency by more than 10 percentage points, and increase cumulative electricity output by nearly 20%. In addition, the sensitivity of the optimal schedules to the adjustment interval reveals practical trade-offs between economic performance and computational cost. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to identify improved long-term SOFC operating strategies under degradation and off-design constraints, while the absolute economic values remain case-dependent.

title: Infoergy equation: A case study on vehicle energy management technology
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: “Infoergy” is not a typo, but rather the energization of information, which is an abbreviation for “information-energy”. Vehicle energy-saving is progressively evolving toward intelligent energy management systems that integrate information interaction; however, there remains a lack of quantitative description of the coupling relationship between information quantity and energy consumption. This hinders the full utilization of information to uncover energy-saving potential in energy management decisions and prevents an objective assessment of information's contribution to enhancing system energy efficiency. Therefore, this study proposes for the first time an information-energy equation that describes the intrinsic connection between information and energy in vehicle energy management technology. Aiming at the comprehensive information representation of multi-source time-varying information within the context of vehicle energy management, this equation defines vehicle velocity as the observable random variable of working condition information to quantify its uncertainty. An energy-saving potential evaluation system is then established. Then, by utilizing information metrics and energy-saving indicators to construct a nonlinear mapping model, it reveals the impact of working condition complexity on energy consumption from the perspective of information. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed infoergy equation exhibits excellent fitting accuracy and generalization capability. It effectively reproduces energy consumption trends and possesses good physical interpretability. At the application level, compared to other methods, the new paradigm of information-energy coupling mechanisms demonstrates better energy-saving effects. It provides a novel theoretical foundation and precise quantitative tools for unlocking energy-saving potential in intelligent energy management, laying the groundwork for deep energy savings in intelligent transportation systems.

title: Nano-kinetic implant surface mediates osteo-antibacterial synergy through electromagnetic-mechanical coupling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics.

title: Near-infrared-responsive thia-hexaphyrin-based covalent organic frameworks for cancer phototherapy
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COF) have emerged as promising phototherapeutic platforms for tumor therapy, where the columnar π-arrayed metal-free photosensitizers serve as both a cooperative light-harvesting antenna and a semiconducting scaffold for efficient charge-carrier separation and transport. However, the phototherapeutic agents based on COFs are usually activated with ultraviolet and visible light, resulting in the limitation of deep-tissue phototherapy. Herein, we develop near-infrared-responsive COFs through elaborate design and synthesis of a thia-hexaphyrin building block, which feature well-aligned conjugation skeletons for the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and photothermal effect upon 808 nm laser irradiation, outperforming conventional porphyrin-based COFs. This porous framework exhibits high phototherapeutic efficacy, leading to the tumor suppression for 4T1 tumors and CT26 tumors in female mouse model by inducing immunogenic cell death through phototherapy and triggering systemic anti-tumor immune responses.

title: Rapid assessment of chemical complementarity of ligands for protein design
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Driven by deep-learning methods, computational protein design can now rapidly generate de novo structures, opening new frontiers for creating proteins that bind small molecules tightly and specifically, although achieving predictable and tunable binding remains challenging. Here we address this with a rapid physics-based computational method to generate isosteric and chemically complementary binding pockets for small-molecule targets in de novo designed proteins. We test this experimentally by constructing and characterizing binding proteins for several synthetic and natural chromophores. By evaluating only single-digit numbers of designs, the pipeline delivers stable proteins with pre-organised binding sites in apo structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography, which bind the targets with micromolar affinities or better. To illustrate the scope and applications of this approach, we incorporate selective and coupled chromophore-binding sites in a two-domain de novo protein enabling controlled energy transfer between the two sites, and we develop a small de novo binding protein that can be used in live mammalian cells to visualise sub-cellular structures.

title: The 2023 North Atlantic marine heatwave could have evolved into a far more extreme event
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: In 2023, the North Atlantic Ocean experienced a marine heatwave of unprecedented intensity and duration, raising the question of whether substantially more severe outcomes were physically plausible under comparable present-day preconditioning, and which processes could produce them. Here, we apply ensemble boosting to a coupled Earth system model to generate physically consistent alternative evolutions of a 2023-like event. The boosted ensemble produced marine heatwaves lasting up to 579 days, reaching maximum intensities of 4.5 °C above climatology and cumulative intensities of 717 °C·days, compared with 240 days, 2.9 °C and 224 °C·days in observations. Detailed analyses of the longest and most intense events highlight contrasting roles for persistent Euro-Atlantic high pressure, reduced turbulent heat loss, enhanced shortwave radiation and upper-ocean heat redistribution. Finally, we place these present-day storylines in the context of future warming, showing that events comparable to the observed 2023 event become increasingly common as global warming progresses.

title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. Almost half of this loss is moderated by the presence of ice mélange, which influences glacial calving and melt rates. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. Here we present an explanation of ice mélange seasonality and collapse using a coupled ice mélange-ocean model that incorporates both high-resolution ocean circulation and dynamic granular mélange flow. In multi-year simulations, we reproduce observed seasonal variability of ice mélange and characterize the mechanism of collapse. We parameterize the threshold for ice mélange collapse and compare this to observations from five fjords across Greenland. Our results show that perennial ice mélange, currently present at the majority of the largest glaciers in Greenland, may suddenly collapse when subjected to increased submarine melt, which would drive greater calving, glacier mass loss, and sea level rise.

title: Two-stage joint planning enabled reliability enhancement of offshore wind farm collection system
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Floating offshore wind farms are characterized by long offshore distances and poor transportation accessibility, which result in higher failure loss cost under fault conditions in existing radial networks. Therefore, it is urgent to propose a more reliable ring topology planning scheme for the collection system. To solve the problem, a two-stage joint planning method (TJPM) is proposed for floating offshore wind farm collection system to enhance the operational reliability and reduce the full life cycle cost. In the first stage, the offshore substation location is optimized by the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), which performs an adaptive search by continuously and dynamically adjusting its probability distribution parameters. The optimal offshore substation location obtained in the first stage can be jointed as the constraints of the relationship optimization between wind turbines (WTs) and offshore substation areas in the second stage. In the second stage, the relationship is optimized based on a Tabu search algorithm, which is customized by integrating neighborhood operations such as reallocation and swapping on key WTs. The continuous Hopfield neural network is used for cable topology planning by linearizing the full life cycle cost of floating offshore wind farms, thereby improving the computational speed in the whole topology process of the collection system. Case studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed joint planning method for floating offshore wind farms in operational reliability and economic performance.

title: Understory diversity is positively associated with overstory carbon sequestration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Forests are a major terrestrial carbon sink, and higher overstory diversity is often associated with greater carbon accrual in trees and soils. Yet the contribution of the understory vegetation, the most species-rich forest stratum, to tree and soil carbon accumulation remains largely unknown. Here, we analyzed Canada’s National Forest Inventory database to explore whether understory diversity (richness and evenness of shrubs, herbs, and bryophytes) is associated with carbon accumulation in overstory trees and soils across environmental gradients of air temperature, climate moisture, and nitrogen deposition. We found that herb and bryophyte species richness were positively associated with decadal tree carbon accumulation, with the strongest effects at warmer, drier, and nitrogen-limited sites. In contrast, understory diversity showed no consistent association with soil carbon accumulation. On a decadal scale, increasing herb and bryophyte species richness from their minimum to median values corresponded to 15% and 6% increases in tree carbon accumulation, respectively. These results provide large-scale observational evidence that diversity in lower vegetation layers is positively associated with overstory carbon sequestration and reveal strong environmental modulation of these multistratal biodiversity–ecosystem functioning relationships. These findings suggest that species-rich herb and bryophyte communities should be considered in strategies for sustaining forest carbon sinks, especially under warmer, drier conditions and nutrient limitation.

title: Geography of groundwater use and depletion in internationally shared aquifers
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Transboundary aquifers (TBAs) underlie 35% of global groundwater-irrigated cropland, yet few are covered by formal cooperative arrangements. Whether this limited cooperation is consequential depends in part on where groundwater is used within shared aquifers, because pumping far from international borders may generate little cross-border impact. Combining ∼ 116,000 well observations with global irrigation data across all 426 known TBAs, we assess how groundwater use and depletion differ from comparable domestic systems and how they are distributed relative to international borders. While we find no evidence of greater average depletion in TBAs, depletion is more strongly concentrated toward international borders in shared aquifers and varies substantially across systems. Irrigation is also more intensive and concentrated toward borders in shared aquifers, although much of this pattern is attenuated after accounting for border rivers. Groundwater-supplied irrigation remains more border-proximate after accounting for these rivers. A dyad-level typology distinguishes shared systems according to where groundwater demand is concentrated, linking their potential for cross-border interaction to different management options. These findings suggest that transboundary groundwater governance should be organized around the geography of groundwater use and potential cross-border interactions rather than treating shared aquifers as uniform governance units.

title: Immense but not immutable: A sudden and sustained decline in deep-pelagic life in a large oceanic ecosystem
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The deep-pelagic habitat of the Gulf of Mexico comprises 90.4% of its volume and houses an exceptionally diverse deep-pelagic animal community that provides numerous ecosystem services, including carbon cycling and prey provisioning for oceanic predators. Here, we report sudden, severe, and persistent declines in the abundance of deep-pelagic fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods that have persisted for over a decade. Over a 3.5-y period, animal abundances declined by 60 to 85%, taxon depending. Particularly hard-hit were ecologically foundational taxa such as euphausiids and lanternfishes. The magnitude of population-level decline that occurred during this 3.5-y period was greater than any observed over a 60-y period in the California Current system, the only comparable dataset, making this the fastest and most severe faunal decline reported for Earth’s largest ecosystem type. These declines were detected both via direct sampling and acoustic sensing, providing independent corroboration. Genomic analyses indicate reductions in genetic diversity among dominant taxa, both a corroboration and a consequence of the decline. Furthermore, resource managers report that these trends parallel those of managed or protected Gulf species that are dependent on deep-pelagic prey, including endangered species (e.g., beaked whales, Rice’s whale). No naturally occurring factors (e.g., temperature, oxygen, food supply) correlated with the observed declines, suggesting an anthropogenic proximate cause. That the declines began shortly after the Deepwater Horizon oil spill points to that event as the most parsimonious explanation. These findings suggest that despite its immense size the deep-pelagic biome is vulnerable to human-induced disturbance and possesses limited resilience to facilitate recovery.

title: Modeling the global potential of smart farming innovations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Smart farming innovations can improve agricultural productivity, resilience, and environmental sustainability, yet their real-world impact hinges on their diffusion dynamics, which in turn depend on their economic viability. We present here a global assessment of the profitability of smart farming innovation across croplands at a spatial resolution of ~5 km from the farmers’ and the societal perspectives. We cover application mapping for precision agriculture, automated application of inputs, autonomous weeding machines, GPS steering assistance systems, and autonomous irrigation systems. For this, we compiled a globally comprehensive dataset of smart farming innovation adoption locations (N = 4,422) based on a combination of a survey (N = 2,677) and a meta-analysis (N = 1,745) and combined them with remotely sensed and statistical data to train an ensemble of five geospatial machine learning models (generalized linear models, random forests, support vector machines, maximum entropy, and boosted regression trees), which show the global distribution of the different innovations’ profitability and its overlap with major environmental issues the innovations can help to mitigate. Simulations of future socioeconomic pathways combined with assumptions about future agri-environmental policies reveal that, especially in middle-income countries, the potential of smart farming will grow over time.

title: A Bering Sea marine heatwave triggers unprecedented crab hybridization, challenging fisheries management
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Marine heatwaves are increasingly recognized for their capacity to generate ecological surprises, yet the pathways that propagate these unexpected responses are often poorly understood. Here, we document an unanticipated ecological response 7 y after a Bering Sea marine heatwave, in which formerly rare snow crab ( Chionoecetes opilio ) × Tanner crab ( C. bairdi ) hybrid abundance increased 13.4-fold, and the proportion of commercial-sized hybrid males increased 13.1-fold, relative to historical averages. Using causal modeling, we show that the hybrid crab surge was mediated by a heatwave-induced collapse of snow crab rather than direct thermal effects on hybrid survival or increased spatial overlap between mature snow and Tanner crab. Our results reveal an indirect cascading pathway through which an extreme climate event triggered unexpected ecological consequences and unforeseen challenges for fisheries management in the Bering Sea. The dramatic increase in abundance of harvestable hybrid crab, coupled with their exclusion from existing management frameworks, highlights the vulnerability of inflexible management systems to unanticipated ecosystem responses.
