title: Synergistic Proton Transport Regulation and Interfacial Anion Adsorption Engineering in ZIF‐8‐Derived PtCu Electrocatalysts for High‐Performance Light and Heavy‐Duty PEM Fuel Cells
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering catalyst‐ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT‐PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8‐derived 3D‐hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D‐hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton‐conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half‐cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin‐type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec − 1 , delivering 0.75 A mg Pt −1 at 0.90 V IR‐free under H 2 ‐O 2 operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm − 2 at 0.70 V under light‐ and heavy‐duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress‐test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst‐ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high‐performance LT‐PEMFC.

title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self‐Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few‐Layer Nanosheets Grown From High‐Curvature Micro‐Interface for Fuel Cell
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low‐resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro‐interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few‐layer iCOF nanosheets at high‐curvature micro‐interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation‐driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere‐like morphologies in previously reported micro‐interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil‐in‐water microemulsion interface using weakly surface‐active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As‐prepared iCOF few‐layer nanosheets (1.3–1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM (3.2–15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF‐based membranes.

title: Electric Double Layer‐Driven Surface Reconstruction Enables Cooperative Zn(002)/(101) Growth for High‐Utilization Zinc Anodes
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc batteries are limited by the mismatch between dynamic interfacial chemistry and anisotropic Zn crystallization. Here, imidazolidinyl urea (IDU) is used to couple electric double layer (EDL) reconstruction with Zn surface reorganization. IDU preferentially enriches at the Zn/electrolyte interface, displaces interfacial water, and interacts strongly with Zn(100). In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, quartz crystal microbalance, and neutron reflectivity reveal transient removal and reconstruction of surface Zn rather than simple molecular adsorption. The reconstructed interface suppresses Zn(100) and promotes cooperative Zn(002)/(101) evolution, enabling compact deposition with favorable kinetics. Meanwhile, the water‐deficient EDL and hybrid organic‐inorganic interphase inhibit parasitic reactions and stabilize the interfacial environment. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 6000 h at 4 mA cm −2 and 2 mAh cm −2 , while Zn||Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 3000 cycles. Stable operation is further maintained at −10°C and under high Zn utilization. Zn||CVO full cells retain 75% capacity after 650 cycles at an N/P ratio of 2.9, and a 21 mAh pouch cell preserves 84% capacity after 400 cycles. This work links EDL reconstruction with crystallographic evolution to enable highly reversible and practically relevant Zn metal anodes.

title: Lightweight and Robust Bamboo Fiber Composite for Efficient Infrared Stealth
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the continuous advancement in modern infrared detection technologies, efficient infrared stealth materials with features of lightweight and high mechanical strength are urgently desired in many fields. In this study, natural bamboo fibers were employed as a renewable substrate and were processed into lightweight and robust infrared stealth bamboo fibrous (HsIs-Bamboo) via oxidative defibration, ionic cross-linking, vacuum-assisted loading, and hot pressing. The fabricated bamboo fibrous composite enables uniform dispersion of functional particles, resulting in low infrared emissivity (65–73% in 8–14 μm), lightweight (0.80 g cm–3), and high mechanical strength (specific tensile strength of 385.9 MPa cm3 g–1). The composite also exhibits low-cost, efficient flame retardancy, and superior infrared shielding performance with a 10.6 °C decrease in the infrared thermal imaging test. This novel infrared stealth material from natural bamboo offers a promising solution for the stealth protection of critical facilities and holds substantial application potential as a highly robust infrared stealth material in weight-sensitive circumstances.

title: Tailoring Crystal Facets Enables Scalable Synthesis of Highly Dispersed Single Crystal NCM90
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high‐valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi 0.90 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (SC‐NCM90) in low‐cost. The surface substitution of Ni 2+/3+ by W 6+ /Mo 6+ facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo‐doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li + ‐migration and endowing the Mo 6+ ‐doped SC‐NCM90 with the capacity of 111.0 mAh g −1 at 5C, achieving the desired fast charging for SC‐NCM90. W‐doping facilitates the growth of both (003) and (104) planes, benefiting the particle segregation, as (003) plane inhibits ionic fusion. W‐ and Mo‐doped SC‐NCM90 deliver markedly improved cycling life and safety performance than polycrystalline NCM90. This work establishes the strategy of high‐valence elemental surface doping as a dual‐functional paradigm that simultaneously manipulates crystal facet evolution for suppressing particle agglomeration and fortifies transition metal (TM)─O bonding for stabilizing interface, producing highly dispersed SC‐NCM90 with faster charging capability and durability.

title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX2, previously reported as having inverted S1-T1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX2 show anti-Kasha S0←S2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S0→S1, linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S0→S2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S0←S1 emission, whereas exciting S0→S1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S2 and S1 is very weak, S2-TN intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S1↔T1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T1→S1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale.

title: Thermal Transport in Atomic Layer Deposition-Grown Beryllium Oxide Thin Films and Implications on Device Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thin film beryllium oxide (BeO) is an emerging material that can potentially be used as a high thermal conductivity gate dielectric and/or passivation layer for high power electronic devices. This study presents the measurement of the thermal conductivity and thermal boundary conductance associated with plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD)-grown polycrystalline BeO films on Si substrates with thicknesses ranging from 25 to 250 nm. The measured out-of-plane thermal conductivities of the 250, 113, 53, and 26 nm-thick BeO films are 13.45 ± 1.45, 8.7 ± 1.35, 7.2 ± 2.1, and 5 ± 2.2 W m–1 K–1, respectively, representing an order-of-magnitude improvement over conventional dielectric materials such as SiN and SiO2. The measured thermal boundary conductance across the BeO/Si interface is ∼200 MW m–2 K–1 at room temperature, which approaches the intrinsic interface limit and suggests that interfacial heat transport is predominantly governed by elastic phonon transmission. The growth of a ∼200 nm-thick polycrystalline diamond film on an AlGaN/GaN-on-Si epitaxial wafer using a 5 nm-thick BeO diamond-seeding is demonstrated, where the structural integrity of the underlying AlGaN/GaN heterostructure is fully preserved. Thermal simulations of AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) integrated with a top-side polycrystalline diamond heat spreader predict that replacing the conventional SiO2 passivation and nucleation layers with BeO helps reduce the channel temperature rise by an additional 5.2%.

title: Dual Anion‐Involved Interfacial Chemistry Enables Ultra‐Stable PEO‐Based Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries by Suppressing NMP‐Induced Side Reactions
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The incorporation of solvent N‐methylpyrrolidone (NMP) into polyethylene oxide (PEO) weakens EO‐Li + interaction and boosts Li + transport via strong Li + affinity, but free NMP inevitably reacts with Li metal, undermining interface stability. Herein, we report a dual‐anion coordination strategy that repurposes the residual NMP from a “side‐reaction source” into a “functional component”. LiDFOB and LiNO 3 are introduced as dual‐salt additives into an NMP‐containing PEO/LiTFSI system. Leveraging the preferential coordination of DFOB– and NO 3 – with Li + , an anion‐enriched solvation sheath is constructed, which strengthens the Li + ‐NMP interactions. The modified coordination environment facilitates the preferential formation of a kinetically stable, anion‐derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively mitigating interfacial side reactions between the NMP and Li metal. As a result, the obtained electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.69 × 10 −4 S cm −1 and stable cycling over 1200 h at room temperature. The assembled Li/LFP cell exhibits a high capacity retention of 93% after 2000 cycles. Even at room temperate and 0°C, the assembled Li/LFP cell maintains stable and efficient cycling. This work establishes a universal solvent structure tailoring strategy to regulate reactive solvent molecules, opening a fresh avenue for high‐performance PEO‐based solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl‐shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li 4 pocket that traps Cl − , Br − , and I − in strongly flattened to ideal planar tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral [Li 4 X] 3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a charge‐attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf) 2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na 15 Sn 4 ), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn 2+ ‐Na + coordination excludes PF 6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf − and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na + desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg −1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO 2 /Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO 2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO 2 →WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO 2 ), as directly evidenced by in situ x‐ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H 2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO 2 –WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO 2 . Consequently, WO x /TiO 2 /Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H 2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO 2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO 2 /Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO 2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter DT‐BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The DT‐BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQE max values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%‐based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR‐TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

title: High-Mobility a-InZnO Thin-Film Transistors Incorporating an Oxygen-Related Defect Control Layer for Improved Illumination Stability and Environmental Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The introduction of an appropriate passivation layer is considered a viable strategy for improving the long-term stability and electrical performance of thin-film transistors (TFTs). In this study, an additional layer deposition strategy involving the deposition of a single-layer oxygen-related defect control layer on amorphous indium zinc oxide (a-IZO) thin-film transistors is developed. This approach improves the electrical characteristics and negative-bias illumination stress (NBIS) stability of the channel layer. The oxygen-related defect control layer is a hafnium oxynitride (HfON) layer. It functions as an insulating material with a relatively high dielectric constant, high film density, and low surface energy, serving as a protective barrier against environmental degradation such as exposure to ambient air and moisture. In addition, it contributes to the improvement of NBIS-induced stability by passivating the defect sites in a-IZO during the activation annealing process. Furthermore, the number of carriers in the channel layer increased because of the formation of oxygen vacancies in the a-IZO front channel through the oxygen adsorption of the oxygen-related defect control layer, resulting in the fabrication of thin films with better electrical properties. This resulted in field-effect mobility improving from 37.53 to 66.43 cm2/(V s), the on/off current ratio was enhanced from 1.93 × 109 to 5.77 × 1011, and the threshold voltage shift under NBIS at green light (532 nm) flux density of 1 mW/cm2 for 10,000 s decreased from 15.25 to 2.64 V.

title: Boosting Carrier Mobility and Restoring Ambipolarity in 2D TMD Transistors via Nano-spherical Probe Cleaning
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), particularly MoS2 and WSe2, are ideal candidates for constructing next-generation high-performance electronics due to their atomic thickness and excellent electrical tunability. However, interface contaminants and bubbles inevitably introduced during device fabrication remain a critical challenge, acting as scattering centers that severely limit carrier mobility and induce device instability. This study demonstrates an in situ mechanical contact strategy using a nano-spherical probe to precisely remove interface residues in MoS2/hBN and WSe2/hBN van der Waals heterostructures. Experimental results indicate that this method significantly reduces interface roughness from ∼11.5 to ∼1.35 nm. The cleaned MoS2 field-effect transistors (FETs) exhibited a significant increase in effective electron mobility from ∼8.5 to 79.2 cm2/V·s, an improvement of approximately one order of magnitude in the on/off ratio, and a significant suppression of charge-trapping-induced hysteresis. For WSe2 devices, the technique successfully restored intrinsic symmetric ambipolar transport characteristics, enhancing both electron and hole drive currents. Furthermore, a 90-day monitoring period in a non-vacuum environment revealed the different degradation mechanisms of interface adsorbates on n-type and p-type carrier transport. This work not only confirms the universality of nanomechanical cleaning technology in enhancing the intrinsic performance of 2D material heterostructure devices but also deeply elucidates the structure–property relationship regarding long-term stability, providing guidance for the interface engineering of high-performance 2D electronics.

title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core–shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)–Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs–Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs–Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·–, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs–Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs–Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs–Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs–Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

title: In Situ Tracking of Se Vacancy-Promoted Surface Reconstruction of NiCoSe2 into NiCoOOH during Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding the dynamic surface reconstruction of precatalyst materials during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a forefront area of research for designing and studying effective electrocatalysts. Here, we report the deliberate engineering of Se vacancies in NiCoSe2 via a facile NaBH4 reduction strategy and systematically investigate how anion vacancies govern surface reconstruction behavior under alkaline OER conditions. The presence of Se vacancies is confirmed via EPR spectroscopy and ICP-MS analysis. Cyclic voltammetry and in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy during the electrochemical activation process reveal that the vacancy-enriched NiCoSe2–x undergoes faster and more extensive structural reconstruction than pristine NiCoSe2. Quasi in situ ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy track the dynamic evolution of NiCoOOH during anodic polarization, providing direct spectroscopic evidence for the Se vacancy-promoted NiCoOOH active phase generation with abundant Ni–O–Co synergy. Evaluation of electrochemical surface area and turnover frequency establishes that the generation of abundant Ni–O–Co synergy in NiCoSe2–x simultaneously increases the density of accessible active sites and enhances the intrinsic activity per site. Consequently, the NiCoSe2–x precatalyst delivers significantly improved OER performance relative to bare NiCoSe2, along with high Faradaic selectivity and long-term stability. Post-stability characterizations confirm bulk structural and morphological reconstruction driven by Se vacancies and thus highlight the complete utilization of the available catalytic sites. This work provides a fundamental mechanistic framework linking anion vacancy engineering, surface reconstruction kinetics/mechanism tracking, and intrinsic OER activity enhancement in bimetallic chalcogenide precatalysts, offering rationalized design principles for next-generation earth-abundant OER catalysts.

title: Three-Dimensional Crosslinked CNT/SiO x -F Network Encapsulated by Pitch-Derived Carbon as a High-Stable Anode for Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Intrinsic low conductivity and huge volume expansion severely limit the cycling stability of SiOx anodes. Herein, a 3D crosslinked CNT/SiOx-F@C composite is synthesized via bifunctional fluorosilane crosslinkers and conformal pitch carbon coating. Fluorosilane acts as both a silicon source and a crosslinker to build interconnected, conductive CNT frameworks, while the outer pitch carbon optimizes the pore structure and induces flexible, LixPOyF6-rich SEI layers. Kinetic tests reveal dominant capacitive charge storage and a Li+ diffusion coefficient one-order-of-magnitude higher than that of control electrodes. The half-cell delivers a stable reversible capacity of 672.6 mA h g–1 over 200 cycles at 0.2 A g–1 and retains 86.5% capacity after 600 cycles at 1 A g–1. Pre-lithiation elevates the initial Coulombic efficiency from 47.4 to 84.2%, while the electrode achieves an areal capacity approaching 4 mA h cm–2, far exceeding that of commercial graphite. This dual-carbon synergistic strategy provides a facile route to optimizing silicon oxide anodes.

title: Hydrogel Microneedle-Enabled In Situ Monitoring of Leaf Nitric Oxide for Evaluating NO Nanoprodrug-Mediated Salt Stress Alleviation in Maize
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chemical signals in living plants are spatially confined, rapidly consumed, and strongly dependent on the delivery history of exogenous regulators, creating a need for bioelectronic interfaces that can interrogate molecular dynamics directly within intact tissues. Here, we integrate a nitric oxide (NO) nanoprodrug with a conductive hydrogel microneedle platform to connect controlled molecular delivery, in planta electrochemical readout, and downstream biological responses in living maize. The working electrode comprises a poly(vinyl alcohol)/aramid nanofiber (PVA/ANF) hydrogel containing FeMo-N/C and an MXene conductive network. The hydrated microneedle architecture provides tissue-conformal contact and analyte transport, FeMo-N/C enhances the NO-associated electrochemical response, and MXene improves interfacial charge transfer. The resulting platform responds to NO from 1 nM to 100 μM with a detection limit of 0.3 nM and discriminates NO from representative electroactive plant interferents. Chitosan nanoparticles containing S-nitroso-mercaptosuccinic acid were used to moderate NO release, and the microneedle interface resolved treatment-dependent leaf signals over 7 days under salt stress. Signal attenuation by the NO scavenger cPTIO supported the NO-related origin of the electrochemical response. The time-resolved readout was accompanied by improved growth, reduced lipid peroxidation, changes in osmotic and antioxidant responses, and altered expression of stress-responsive genes. This delivery–bioelectronics–analysis framework provides a materials-based strategy for evaluating reactive nanoprodrugs and interrogating transient chemical signaling in living plants.

title: Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET Plastic Waste
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800–5050 nm and width: 780–970 nm). This unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by the spent catalyst’s analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic recycling industry.

title: Interfacial Regulation via Organic-Inorganic Interpenetrating Networks for Enhanced Protection in Waterborne Polyurethane Nanocomposites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The abundance of hydrophilic groups and the linear polymer chain structure in waterborne polyurethane (WPU) lead to insufficient water resistance and corrosion protection. These inherent characteristics make it challenging for WPU to be applied in the marine protection field, where high comprehensive performance of coatings is demanded. Herein, a WPU nanocomposite was designed incorporating hydroxyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane and bifunctionalized nano-silica (modified with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane and propyltrimethoxysilane) during prepolymerization. This strategy established an organic–inorganic interpenetrating cross-linked network through covalent bonding and intermolecular interactions. The silica nanoparticles act as interfacial bridges between polymer segments, mitigating phase separation and agglomeration caused by polarity mismatch, thereby enhancing coating compactness and improving stress transfer. Performance tests demonstrate that the properties of the coating have been comprehensively enhanced. The coating exhibits an elongation at break of 254.64% while maintaining a tensile strength of 21.17 MPa. Additionally, the water absorption rate of the coating decreases to approximately 5%, the electrochemical protection efficiency reaches 99.9920%, and no obvious corrosion phenomenon is observed after a 7 day salt spray corrosion test. Additionally, the coating shows excellent drag-reduction performance, with a drag-reduction rate of 6.56% under turbulent flow. By integrating interfacial design with nanocomposite architecture, this work develops a robust WPU coating system suitable for marine engineering applications, and employs molecular dynamics simulations to reveal the microscopic mechanism by which amino and n-propyl silane dual modification inhibits the aggregation of silica nanoparticles as well as the interfacial interaction mechanism, thereby highlighting the role of colloidal and nanomaterial strategies in advancing functional protective coatings.

title: Wettability-Gradient Interphase for Reconciling Water Shielding with Zincate Transport in Alkaline Zn–Ni Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial interfacial layers on Zn anodes are a promising route for stabilizing alkaline Zn–Ni batteries, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by a trade-off between suppressing water-induced parasitic reactions and maintaining rapid Zn-containing species transport. Herein, a hydrophobic–hydrophilic gradient composite layer is developed on a Zn substrate through sequential perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) modification followed by crosslinked polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) coating. This gradient interphase couples a buried hydrophobic PFOTS layer with an outer hydrophilic PVA layer, thereby balancing water shielding, electrolyte affinity, mechanical compliance, and Zn-containing species transport at the Zn/electrolyte interface. As a result, the symmetric cell based on PFOTS/PVA-modified Zn (ZP) delivers stable cycling for 1200 h at 1 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2. When coupled with a Ni(OH)2-based cathode, the resulting alkaline Zn–Ni full cell exhibits an output voltage of ≈1.77 V, retains 93.2% of its capacity after resting for 48 h, sustains stable operation for more than 1100 h at 1 C, and maintains durable cycling over 1500 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates that wettability-gradient interfacial engineering can reconcile water regulation, Zn-containing species transport, and mechanical compliance for durable alkaline Zn anodes.

title: ROS-Responsive Hydrogel for Spatiotemporal Cascade Regulation of Ferroptosis and Fibrosis for Myocardial Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Myocardial infarction (MI)-induced cardiac injury is mainly divided into two phases: the acute necrotic phase and the repair phase. Given the distinct therapeutic requirements of each phase—salvaging dying cardiomyocytes and reducing infarct size in the acute phase, while achieving controlled fibrosis to promote effective ventricular remodeling in the repair phase—we designed an ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivery system (Met/Anti-34a@Gel) loaded with metformin (Met) and Anti-34a liposomes (Anti-34a Lip) to achieve precise regulation of both the acute and repair phases of MI. In the highly oxidative stress microenvironment following MI, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases Met and Anti-34a Lip in a stage-specific manner. Met improves mitochondrial function, inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, thereby effectively salvaging cardiomyocytes in the acute phase. Anti-34a Lip modulates the differentiation behavior of cardiac fibroblasts, suppressing excessive fibrosis and promoting favorable ventricular remodeling in the repair phase. Echocardiography revealed that Met/Anti-34a@Gel preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) at 72 h post-MI, reduced serum MDA levels in the acute phase, and maintained EF at approximately 60.92 ± 8.37% with a lower collagen I/III ratio at 4 weeks, collectively demonstrating both acute cardioprotection and long-term anti-fibrotic remodeling. In this combined therapeutic strategy, the early mitochondrial protection and anti-ferroptosis effects establish a favorable tissue and functional foundation for subsequent precision anti-fibrotic therapy, while the later anti-fibrotic treatment further consolidates the early protective effects. The two actions synergistically form a positive feedback loop, ultimately achieving sustained long-term cardiac functional improvement.

title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron–phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron–phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

title: From gas generation to intelligent management: a gas-signal-driven framework for thermal runaway early warning in lithium-ion batteries
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Thermal runaway (TR) in lithium-ion batteries poses a critical challenge to the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems. Conventional battery management systems (BMSs), which primarily rely on voltage and temperature signals, frequently exhibit delayed response and limited capability for early-stage fault detection. Gas signals, generated at the early stages of TR, provide rich physicochemical information on internal reactions and offer unique potential for timely warning and fault diagnosis. This review presents a gas-signal-driven early warning framework that systematically integrates mechanism understanding, signal sensing, and intelligent decision-making. The framework is designed to upgrade current BMS architectures without major hardware redesign. Specifically, this review (i) deconstructs multi-stage gas generation mechanisms, characteristic gas fingerprints across different battery chemistries, and their spatiotemporal evolution; (ii) critically evaluates state-of-the-art gas sensing technologies and their applicability to practical battery systems; and (iii) synthesizes intelligent early warning architectures, with an emphasis on multi-sensor fusion and AI-based methods to enhance detection reliability, extend warning lead time, and enable predictive safety interventions. In addition, key engineering challenges-including trace gas detection under realistic conditions, environmental interference, long-term sensor stability, and constraints for edge deployment-are systematically discussed. Future directions toward cloud-edge collaboration are also outlined. Beyond early warning, this infrastructure also holds promise for full-lifecycle management, including state estimation and maintenance scheduling.

title: Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial–immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB–Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

title: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metabolic dysregulation under nutrient stress disrupts bone homeostasis. Although acetate metabolism is linked to diabetes and alcoholism, its role in the skeletal complications of these conditions remains unknown. Here we identify acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (ACSS1) as a key stress responder that mediates mitonuclear communication in bone marrow skeletal stem cells. ACSS1-driven rewiring of acetate metabolism impairs cellular metabolic flexibility, mitochondrial function, and osteogenesis. Mechanistically, nutrient excess from glucose, alcohol or acetate upregulates ACSS1 via a mitochondrial ROS activated integrated stress response-CEBPB pathway. Maladaptive ACSS1 accumulation enforces excessive acetyl-CoA production from either exogenous or glucose/ethanol-derived endogenous acetate, promoting mitochondrial protein hyperacetylation specifically inactivating ME2 via lysine 94 acetylation. This ACSS1-triggered ME2 inactivation disturbs the malate-aspartate shuttle, leading to a self-perpetuating cycle of redox imbalance and oxidative stress that exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and osteogenic impairment. Importantly, genetic deletion of Acss1 or AAV-delivered non-acetylatable ME2 mutant in osteoprogenitor cells restores mitochondrial resilience, osteogenic capacity, and bone formation, protecting against osteoporosis or osteonecrosis in male mouse models of type 2 diabetes and chronic alcohol consumption. These results unveil an essential role for ACSS1 in controlling metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis, identifying ACSS1 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic stress-related bone disorders.

title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery.

title: Constructing reliable clean energy facility network under ambiguous distribution information
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: In the context of the transition from clean energy to sustainable development, as an emerging low-carbon energy carrier, hydrogen is of crucial importance. The planning of a hydrogenation facility network (HFN) with a reliable hydrogen supply has thus become an important research topic in the field of hydrogen energy provision. This study investigates the planning of the HFN from the perspectives of economic cost and network reliability, under conditions of uncertain hydrogen supply capacity. To address the challenges posed by uncertainty, the renewable energy-powered hydrogen production process is categorized into multiple scenarios. We formulate an ambiguity set using the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and establish ambiguous chance constraints, thereby proposing a novel bi-objective distributionally robust HFN optimization model (DR-HFN). Based on the decision-maker’s preferences in practice, an economic-oriented optimization model and a reliability-oriented optimization model are developed, respectively. Subsequently, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) representation is derived from the proposed model to ensure computational tractability. A customized branch-and-cut (BC) algorithm is further designed to enhance the model’s solvability and scalability. Finally, a practical case study conducted in Guangdong Province, China demonstrates that our proposed method can withstand uncertainties in hydrogen supply capacity with a probability of 90%. Moreover, the comparison with the sample average approximation (SAA) method shows that our method only generates a robustness cost of about 0.087% when addressing distributional uncertainty. This further demonstrates that our method is capable of generating high-quality decision solutions while also exhibiting strong robustness and applicability.

title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has a rising incidence. The majority are diagnosed at an early stage, albeit with a minority exhibiting aggressive tendencies. Given its generally indolent nature, controversy persists regarding the management of early-stage PTCs, particularly surgical intervention and long-term surveillance strategies. Here, we conduct a large-scale proteomic characterization of early-stage PTC based on tumor samples from 797 patients. Proteomic profiling unveils clinically relevant modules and identifies six subtypes, capturing the spectrum of heterogeneity from indolent to progressive disease states. Notably, subtypes associated with higher progression risk display enhanced signatures of ribogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Furthermore, integrating machine learning with protein co-expression network analysis, we identify predictive markers of PTC progression risk such as GPX3 and TMSB4X. Integration of clinical and proteomic data provides a valuable resource for a deeper understanding of early-stage PTC biology and may inform personalized management strategies for patients with indolent or progressive disease.

title: State-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries from random local charging fragments: A reliability-aware local-global fusion framework
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Accurate battery health estimation from incomplete and irregular charging records remains challenging because local fragments differ not only in length but also in diagnostic quality. This study interprets random local charging fragments as reliability-varying partial health observations and develops RLCF-Net, which fuses local Q V response, masked voltage-location context, and scalar operating conditions. A training-only multi-evidence procedure selects a coverage-stable mother voltage interval, while category-level empirical reliability is defined as the inverse calibration RMSE for each span-region category and used for prediction-level aggregation. The framework is evaluated on two laboratory datasets comprising 121 NCA/NCM cells and a field dataset from 20 commercial EVs. On the main NCA dataset, validation-derived category reliability transferred strongly to held-out cells (Spearman 0.936; Pearson 0.983). Random single-fragment estimation achieved a cycle-level RMSE of 0.0082, whereas cross-fitted selection identified the 0.15 V + 0.20 V Val-K2 protocol with an RMSE of 0.003918. Across all nine K2 protocols, reliability weighting reduced RMSE in every case and remained statistically significant in seven protocols after Holm correction. Entity-level analyses further showed that Val-K2 improved all 14 held-out NCA cells relative to K1 (paired Wilcoxon p = 0.000122), RLCF-Net outperformed the strongest unified baseline in 11 of 14 cells ( p = 0.0419), and NCM reliability weighting reduced physical-cell macro RMSE from 0.002807 to 0.002258 ( p = 0.0322). The independently retrained NCM pipeline achieved a pooled Val-K2 RMSE of 0.002613. In the EV one-event evaluation, reliability-weighted K2 achieved RMSEs of 1.590 and 1.541 pp., with availabilities of 65.15% and 43.49%, respectively. Strict event-disjoint label-independence and common-all-protocol EV audits preserved the directional K2 benefit, although exact inference was limited by the four held-out vehicles. Single-thread CPU latency was 5.105 ms for K1 and 10.058 ms for K2. These results support reliability-aware aggregation for incomplete charging observations while identifying operating-condition-dependent reliability, limited fleet size, label-free adaptation, and automotive-MCU validation as remaining boundaries.

title: A systematic review of cross-sectoral life cycle assessments of carbon capture, utilization, and storage systems
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The institutional scale-up of Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) architectures constitutes a critical mandate to fulfil global net-zero targets. Ensuring that carbon mitigation complies with the EU Taxonomy “Do No Significant Harm” principle demands a rigorous life cycle assessment (LCA) framework. This study delivers a comprehensive, PRISMA-driven systematic review and systematic quantitative evidence synthesis based on a multi-database search across Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection. The finalized corpus comprises 97 peer-reviewed articles (14 reviews, 83 primary research studies) categorized across five thematic clusters. The methodological inventory uncovers severe analytical fragmentation; functional units and system boundaries remain divided between mass balances and energy outputs, limiting cross-industry standardization. The empirical evidence synthesis demonstrates that whilst integrated CCUS interventions deliver deep direct carbon reductions (GWP mitigation ranging from 43% to 95% relative to study-specific baselines), concurrent thermal and electrical energy penalties frequently trigger environmental burden-shifting under particular energy and process conditions. Amine-based capture and high-temperature loops can force intense trade-offs, driving absolute increases from 15% to over 50% across terrestrial Acidification and aquatic Eutrophication Potentials. Conversely, advanced pressurized chemical looping and slag mineralization optimize process efficiencies, enabling highly negative LCA results down to −745 kg CO2 eq/ton; however, these values predominantly reflect net-avoided emissions via product displacement rather than permanent geological carbon removal. Finally, a systems-level conceptual framework highlights that the ultimate scalability of integrated CCUS chains is captive to macro-system dependencies, requiring thorough grid decarbonization and optimized dense-phase pipeline transport.

title: Is more aggregated better? Balancing power generation, employment accessibility, and climate mitigation in photovoltaic deployment
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) deployment, together with its growing concentration in large renewable-energy bases, has intensified the need to reassess PV land-use value. However, whether greater spatial aggregation consistently improves power, employment, and climate outcomes remains unclear. Here, we integrated multi-source geospatial data from 30,023 PV plants across China to build a site-to-region framework. This framework links PV aggregation to power-generation potential, population-based local accessibility, and net climate-mitigation benefit, and summarizes their joint performance as total composite benefit (TCB). We found a climate-specific non-linear pattern: TCB peaked at high aggregation in humid and sub-humid regions (76.7% and 62.1%, respectively), but declined monotonically with further aggregation in arid regions. Across regions, aggregation delivered larger gains in power-generation potential than in local accessibility or climate mitigation, and this imbalance became stronger as aggregation increased. Current deployment often falls outside the empirically identified high-benefit aggregation ranges, including 64.0% of PV capacity (42.9 GW) in arid high-demand areas and 87.1% (89.17 GW) in sub-humid flat terrains. These findings show that more concentrated PV deployment is not necessarily associated with greater land-use value. Our framework provides empirical benchmarks for evaluating PV aggregation and informing more balanced PV deployment across power-generation potential, local employment accessibility, and climate outcomes.

title: Effects of climatic control on microenvironmental responses in desert PV systems: A comparative analysis with machine learning interpretation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Microenvironmental responses to desert photovoltaic (PV) systems have been increasingly reported, yet how these responses vary across contrasting arid climate backgrounds remains insufficiently understood under comparable engineering settings. In this study, cross-climate field observations, Δ-response modeling, and SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) interpretation were combined to examine PV-induced environmental change at the Wuwei and Hami sites in northwestern China. Instead of reproducing absolute local states, the models estimated PV-induced deviations from the reference (REF) position, ΔY(position) = Y(position) − Y(REF), for the below-panel (BL) and interrow (IT) positions. The Wuwei site exhibited coupled hydrothermal regulation, with enhanced shallow soil-water retention after rainfall, whereas the Hami site exhibited predominantly thermal regulation because its moisture-retention pathway was largely inactive under extremely low precipitation, coarse soil, and strong evaporative demand. Soil-temperature perturbations were consistently predictable (best-model R 2 = 0.93–0.99), whereas air-temperature perturbations showed moderate skill (R 2 = 0.41–0.65) and relative-humidity perturbations were strongly site dependent (Hami: 0.14–0.19; Wuwei: 0.47–0.97). Grouped SHAP analysis distinguished the predictor groups associated with air-temperature, soil-thermal, and soil-moisture responses. Sparse interaction networks further elucidated the joint roles of these predictor groups in shaping model responses across climates and distinguished relatively stable thermal structures from climate-sensitive hydrothermal linkages. It is hoped that these analyses will contribute to the development of climate-adaptive, site-specific environmental monitoring strategies for desert PV plants.
