title: Electrostatic Contributions of the Extended Environment and Local Catalytic Effects in Bipolar Membranes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Catalyst layers are widely used to accelerate water dissociation in bipolar membranes (BPMs), yet their role in defining junction electrostatics and reversible reaction kinetics remains unclear. Here, we probe the electrochemical response of catalyst-containing BPM junctions using open-circuit voltage measurements, polarization analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. We show that catalyst nanoparticles influence both the recovery of the membrane potential and the voltage losses associated with water dissociation and formation at the catalyst layer. These changes reflect coupled effects of catalyst surface chemistry, junction electrostatics, and proton-transfer kinetics. Notably, catalysts that recover the membrane potential do not necessarily reduce overvoltage under applied bias, highlighting that membrane-potential recovery alone is insufficient to predict BPM performance. By combining improvements in membrane-potential recovery and reaction kinetics, catalyst–ionomer interface engineering reduces water-formation losses by up to 65% and increases peak power density for energy storage by more than an order of magnitude.

title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH 2 OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. Metallic bismuth (Bi) is intrinsically active for this reaction, yet undergoes severe structural degradation under continuous electrolysis—a failure mode we identify as electrochemical spongification, wherein the compact Bi framework cathodically relaxes into an electrically disconnected porous network. Herein, we report an “asymmetric electrochemical breathing” strategy that effectively decouples long‐term catalytic durability from structural failure. Using pulsed potentials between −1.36 and +1.24 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl nanosheets serve as a dynamic template, delivering a high Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% and a yield rate of 4.29 mmol h −1 cm −2 , among the highest reported for NH 2 OH electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical insights reveal that BiOCl rapidly reduces in situ to dense metallic Bi to drive efficient nitrate reduction. Crucially, a brief anodic pulse reconstructs the framework before irreversible degradation occurs, enabling continuous structural rejuvenation for over 380 h. This dynamic reconstruction strategy successfully suppresses the Faradaic efficiency decay rate by two orders of magnitude, establishing a robust paradigm for stabilizing highly active yet metastable electrocatalysts.

title: Ni 3 (HITP) 2 @PTFE Molecular Fence Enables Selective C 2 Coupling in Methane Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis (CEC) enables methane activation under ambient conditions; however, the poorly understood interfacial active sites and uncontrolled evolution of reactive radical intermediates cause methane conversion to remain dominated by C 1 oxygenation rather than selective C─C coupling. Herein, we assemble the established Ni 3 (HITP) 2 framework (HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) on PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) to construct a molecular fence interface integrating Ni–N 4 sites with spatial confinement for selective C 2 coupling. During CEC, contact electrification at the PTFE–water interface supports radical generation for methane conversion, while the coupled Ni–N 4 sites further facilitate O 2 activation and modulate reactive species utilization. Simultaneously, the porous Ni 3 (HITP) 2 outer layer shows enhanced CH 4 uptake near the charged interface and is proposed to favor C─C coupling by promoting local methane enrichment and retention of methane‐derived intermediates. As a result, methane conversion is redirected from C 1 oxygenation toward selective C 2 coupling under ambient conditions, delivering a C 2 yield of 0.58 mmol g −1 h −1 with 82.4% selectivity. In situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations support a mechanistic model in which interfacial Ni–N 4 sites and the porous framework jointly influence reactive‐species utilization and methane‐derived intermediate reactions, favoring pathway‐selective methane CEC.

title: Biomimetic Molybdenum Chemistry Spanning all Four Molybdopterin Enzyme Families: From Stoichiometric Oxygen Atom Transfer to Catalytic C─H Oxidation
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Molybdopterin enzymes catalyze a diverse array of redox transformations, ranging from oxyanion reduction to C─H hydroxylation, through Mo VI /Mo IV cycling at active sites with conserved dithiolene‐coordinated structures. Synthetic models of these active sites have struggled to replicate this versatility in part due to comproportionation to inactive Mo V dimers, and catalytic turnover remains scarce. Here we report that a [N 2 S 2 ] 2− ‐supported Mo IV ═O complex abstracts oxygen atoms from substrates representative of three molybdopterin enzyme families: Me 2 SO, Me 3 NO, ClO 4 − , NO 3 − , and SeO 4 2− (DMSO reductases); methionine sulfoxide (sulfite oxidases); and benzamidoxime and N ‐hydroxyphthalimide (mARCs). In the cases of ClO 4 − and NO 3 − , oxygen atom transfer (OAT) requires Lewis acid activation by B(C 6 F 5 ) 3 . The corresponding Mo VI (O) 2 redox partner oxidizes formate via hydride abstraction, akin to formate dehydrogenases. The same complex has previously been shown to promote C─H hydroxylation of substrates inspired by the XO family, thus demonstrating reactivity that spans all four molybdopterin families. Coupling OAT and hydride transfer half‐reactions enables catalytic turnover, as demonstrated here for both benzimidazoline C─H hydroxylation and formate decarboxylation using DMSO as terminal oxidant, thus demonstrating the first examples of catalytic C─H oxidation by a molybdopterin‐inspired synthetic platform.

title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.

title: Breaking the π‐Conjugation‐Dependence: Enhanced Birefringence and SHG Response in Densely Packed Deep‐UV Phosphates
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Optimizing birefringence and SHG in deep‐UV NLO crystals based on tetrahedral oxyanions remains challenging as extending π‐conjugation often sacrifices UV transparency. In this study, we propose a synergic design strategy that correlates π‐conjugation degree, packing density, and optical performance, resulting in two formamidinium phosphate crystals, enabling two deep‐UV NLO crystals, [CH(NH 2 ) 2 ]H 2 PO 4 ( I ) and [CH(NH 2 ) 2 ] 2 HPO 4 ( II ), with simultaneously enhanced birefringence (0.10@550 nm of I and 0.15@550 nm of II ) and SHG responses (1.1 × KDP of I and 2.0 × KDP of II ). Notably, birefringence of compound II outperforms a number of guanidinium‐based and phosphate‐based NLO crystals, endowing it with exceptional comprehensive performance, as evidenced by its highest quality factor ( Q = 4.4 for II) . Due to the superior birefringence and SHG intensity, both I and II realize phase‐matching at fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm and 532 nm. Structure–property relationship studies reveal that formamidinium's small steric size facilitates dense packing of building blocks within lattice, thereby enhancing birefringence and SHG. This work elucidates the critical influence of π‐conjugation degree on packing density and overall performance (SHG intensity and birefringence). Based on these findings, a novel design pathway for deep‐UV materials might be proposed, linking π‐conjugation degree and packing density with SHG and birefringence.

title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu 3 ‐COF achieves up to 99% H 2 O 2 selectivity and a flow‐cell production rate of 39 420 mmol·g cat −1 ·h −1 , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

title: Electrosynthesis of p ‐Hydroxybenzoic Acid From Phenol and CO 2
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT P ‐hydroxybenzoic acid ( p ‐HBA), with wide applications in food preservatives, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystalline polyether, is currently synthesized via the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction using anhydrous phenolate (PhO − ) and carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). However, this reaction typically suffers from poor selectivity, and requires high temperature/pressure, strongly base, and metal/organic cations for selectivity control. Herein, we report a new method for the electrosynthesis of p ‐HBA from phenol (PhOH) and CO 2 by iodine mediation, achieving 61% yield and 90% selectivity without strong bases and metal cations under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Mechanism studies indicated that PhOH was first selectively iodinated by iodine cations (I + ) generated at the anode to form p ‐iodophenol (HOPh‐I). Subsequently, HOPh‐I and CO 2 were respectively activated on Ag catalyst with abundant grain boundaries (GB‐Ag) through single‐electron reduction, and then underwent radical coupling processes to produce p ‐HBA. Notably, this electrochemical method also successfully converted various oxygen‐containing and nitrogen‐containing aromatic compounds, including the typical structural units of lignin and its derivatives, into valuable carboxylic acids. This innovative electrochemical approach overcomes the inherent limitations of the traditional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, offering a promising strategy for the sustainable utilization of CO 2 and biomass resources.

title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
source: Advanced Energy Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N 4 . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N 4 configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O 2 and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Engineered Excited‐State Coupling Enables Efficient Exciton Harvesting in Binuclear Copper Iodide Cluster Scintillators
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low‐cost, high‐performance x‐ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu–I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin‐orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x‐ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation‐induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation‐state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu–I clusters with nearly identical x‐ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited‐state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water‐resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV −1 and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm −1 . Furthermore, tandem integration with a high‐Z scintillator enables selective density‐discriminating x‐ray imaging and micro‐computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high‐throughput development of promising metal‐cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.

title: Electronic Coupling and Dual‐Spillover Effect in Co/Co 7 Fe 3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Rational design of dual‐site catalysts to decouple complex multi‐electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO 3 − ) reduction reaction (NO 3 RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co 7 Fe 3 heterojunction with strong electronic coupling that drives NO 3 RR efficiently via an unconventional [4+4] tandem mechanism. In this [4+4] pathway, the first 4‐electron step reduces NO 3 − to the *HNOH intermediate at the Fe sites. The second 4‐electron process involves the migration of *HNOH to adjacent Co sites, followed by a 4‐electron hydrogenation step. Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well‐defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co 7 Fe 3 with markedly boosted electrocatalytic activity for NO 3 RR through synergistic dual‐spillover effects, and enabling it to achieve a near‐unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.16% ± 0.3% and a remarkable NH 3 yield rate of 36.07 ± 0.52 mg h −1 cm −2 at −0.48 V versus RHE. Additionally, a rechargeable Zn‐nitrate battery featuring this material as the cathode delivers a peak power density of 18.15 mW cm −2 with excellent cycling stability. This study provides a novel paradigm for designing efficient tandem electrocatalysts.

title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs 4 PbBr 6 and CsPbBr 3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high‐performance perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next‐generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs 4 PbBr 6 phase often accompanies CsPbBr 3 crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive‐mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3‐carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3‐CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr 3 formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs 4 PbBr 6 and CsPbBr 3 phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr 3 phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs 4 PbBr 6 phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.

title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3′−5′ exonuclease activity, generating free 3′ overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid–electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase is a key performance regulator in Li-metal batteries, which are regarded as an important technology for future energy storage. Understanding this crucial interphase through non-destructive analysis is essential to advance the performance and lifespan of Li-metal batteries. We introduce angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for the depth-profile analysis of the solid electrolyte interphase in Li-metal batteries. Importantly, we show that this characterization technique displays a distinct advantage in preserving the solid electrolyte interphase's integrity compared to traditional sputtering-based depth-profiling. Our findings add to the understanding of compositional differences in the solid electrolyte interphase before the onset of Li electrodeposition and after Li plating. Moreover, we find significant variations in the thickness and distribution of solid electrolyte interphase species across different classes of electrolytes, which strongly influence the solid electrolyte interphase's protective properties and, by extension, Li-metal battery performance. This study benchmarks the application of angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in revealing detailed, depth-resolved chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase in a non-destructive approach.

title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a global pathogen, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its virulence and antimicrobial resistance are poorly understood. Here, we characterize 370 transcription factors (TFs) and their binding profiles in a clinical isolate CR-HvKP4, and construct a global gene regulatory network. Using topological analysis, we identify and validate key virulence and antibiotic resistance regulators. Temporal transcriptomic profiling reveals a highly streamlined regulatory efficiency, where over 88% of TFs maintain steady-state expression across growth phases, with middle-layer TFs exhibiting preferential high-level expression to process regulatory signals. Additionally, our pan-genome study across 2059 KP strains reveals high conservation of TFs and distinct geographic patterns within sequence types. Finally, we develop a predictive model that accurately maps transcriptional regulation across independent KP strains. Collectively, we identify 25 key TFs and four TFs regulons at two growth stages, highlighting VmrR (RS15210), whose deletion significantly attenuated virulence in the lungs of female mice.

title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

title: Molecular drivers of cotranslational protein assembly in bacteria
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Protein complexes are pivotal to all major cellular processes. Translation-coupled complex assembly is ubiquitous in eukaryotes, but its molecular basis and prevalence in bacteria remain poorly understood. Here, we combine ribosome profiling and single-molecule optical tweezers to establish principles governing cotranslational assembly of four structurally diverse complexes in Escherichia coli . We reveal how heterotetramers form cotranslationally via hierarchical assembly pathways, with initial heterodimer formation priming the assembly of higher-order oligomers through a topology-dependent organization of homomeric and heteromeric interfaces. Co-post assembly, defined as interaction between nascent and fully synthesized subunits, initiates when dimerization domains are completely exposed at the ribosome. The assembly order is predominantly unidirectional and matches the operon gene order, with upstream-encoded subunits being synthesized first, and then engaging downstream nascent partner subunits. The co-post assembly efficiency depends both on the native operon structure and the ribosome-associated chaperone trigger factor, which binds emerging oligomerization domains and whose dissociation marks the onset of partner subunit engagement. The handover from chaperone engagement to cotranslational assembly is mediated by nascent chain folding. Finally, we show that co-post assembly provides a fitness advantage. Together, these findings reveal how genome organization and chaperone-assisted folding coordinate cotranslational assembly to promote efficient complex biogenesis and cellular fitness in bacteria.

title: HAP40 functions as a proteostasis regulator by controlling huntingtin interactions and its release into the extracellular space
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Huntingtin-associated protein 40 (HAP40) forms a stable protein complex with huntingtin (HTT). Its cellular function and how HAP40 loss influences mutant HTT (mHTT) abundance and pathobiology are currently unclear. Here, using diverse cellular models and omics methods, we demonstrate that HAP40 is an obligate interaction partner of HTT and through its binding controls HTT interactions and the abundance of HTT-associated proteins, indicating that it functions as a HTT interaction regulatory unit. Also, loss of HAP40 in mHTT-expressing striatal cells impairs autophagic protein degradation and triggers transcriptional activation of the CLEAR network, demonstrating that it functions as a proteostasis regulator that acts on quality control pathways. Finally, mHTT-expressing cells lacking HAP40 showed increased secretion of a ~205 kDa mHTT fragment through an endoplasmic reticulum (ER)/Golgi-associated route, indicating that striatal cells reduce intracellular mHTT-induced proteotoxicity through activation of secretory pathways. Together, these results establish HAP40 as a critical proteostasis regulator that through controlling HTT interactions maintains cellular homeostasis.

title: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: The search for high-performance lubricants is of broad relevance to biomedical applications, including artificial joints, regenerative scaffolds, and osteoarthritis therapies. Here we introduce glycerosomes—phosphatidylcholine (PC)-based vesicles containing glycerol—as a promising boundary lubricant. Using a surface force balance, we show that glycerosomes achieve a friction coefficient as low as 10 − 5 under a high compression pressure of 15.6 MPa, representing a 20-fold reduction compared to conventional PC liposomes. This level of lubrication surpasses any previously reported boundary lubricant system at such pressures in aqueous media. Mechanistically, glycerosomes exhibit substantially lower adhesion energy than PC liposomes, and theoretical simulations reveal enhanced vesicle stability and flexibility. Our findings establish glycerosomes as a superior hydration lubrication platform, with promising implications for both biomedical implants and industrial applications requiring robust lubricity.

title: Cold start of proton exchange membrane fuel cells in high-altitude cold regions: coupled heat-water-oxygen mechanisms, system constraints, and engineering validation
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Cold start remains a major barrier to the reliable deployment of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs) in subfreezing environments. High-altitude cold regions impose a compound operating boundary in which low temperature, reduced ambient pressure and oxygen partial pressure, dry air, cold-soak history, compressor demand, coolant thermal inertia, and limited auxiliary energy act simultaneously. This critical review integrates previously separated evidence on generic cold start, high-altitude operation, residual-water control, air supply, heating, and liquid-cooled thermal management. The literature is classified according to whether a study directly tests the coupled high-altitude/subfreezing boundary, tests only one constituent boundary, provides validated simulations or architecture-specific evidence, or supports an engineering synthesis. The combined evidence indicates that reduced oxygen availability may constrain the admissible heat-generating current before water production becomes the sole limiting factor, while minimum cell voltage and coolant response emerge as key stack-scale variables. On this basis, the review proposes an altitude-aware sequence linking purge, loading, air supply, heating, and coolant operation and defines success through thermal, electrochemical, system-energy, and durability criteria. Because direct full-size liquid-cooled validation under simultaneous reduced pressure and subfreezing temperature remains scarce, the immediate priorities are compound-environment experiments, platform-specific weakest-cell safety boundaries, and experimentally verified air-current-coolant switching with unified net-energy accounting.

title: Electrode crosstalk in rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries: species transport, interfacial reactions and coupled full-cell failure
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Rechargeable aqueous zinc batteries fail through reactions that couple the two electrodes as well as through local degradation. Dissolved cathode products, soluble redox intermediates and electrolyte gradients can cross the separator, alter the receiving interface and redistribute active material, zinc and water. This Review defines electrode crosstalk by a source, a transmitted species or perturbation, and a consequential interaction at the opposite electrode. It distinguishes direct chemical transfer from electrolyte-mediated coupling while allowing both pathways to operate in the same cell. Manganese, vanadium, Prussian blue analogue, halogen, selenium and organic cathodes are compared through their carrier chemistry and zinc-side reactions. Liquid, gel and solid electrolytes are examined in terms of their conducting phase, species partitioning and interfacial contact. A six-level evidence hierarchy separates source generation, crossover, arrival, receiver reaction and causal intervention. Consistent definitions of permeability, molar dose and reaction-associated charge loss connect these measurements with cell capacity without conflating ionic charge and reaction stoichiometry. Quantitative examples show how imported species and interfacial regulation affect corrosion, hydrogen evolution and zinc deposition. Mitigation is assessed against resistance, recoverable inventory and cell-level energy, including the possibility of relocating failure. Comparisons of lean-electrolyte and pouch cells identify the operating conditions under which crosstalk becomes consequential. The outlook develops a route for combining spatially resolved measurements, reaction–transport models and data-driven screening to design mutually compatible electrode environments.

title: A hierarchical framework and Bayesian game model for multi-load aggregator strategic interaction under incomplete information
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: High renewable penetration intensifies power fluctuations in distribution networks, making load aggregators (LAs) essential providers of flexibility. However, in practice, multiple LAs operate within the same area, with their decisions coupled through dynamic interactions in power flows and profits. Commercial privacy further creates information barriers, forcing LAs to decide under incomplete information and uncertain outcomes. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the modeling of multi-LA strategic interactions. A hierarchical information-decision-execution framework is formulated, in which a Bayesian game model is used to describe the physical and economic interdependencies among LAs, with equilibrium solutions defining the optimal strategies. Furthermore, a Productive Mixed-Attention Transformer (PMA-Transformer) is developed to enable the DSO to accurately estimate each LA's regulation capacity and resource composition, providing reliable type estimates for dynamic prior construction in the game. Finally, a constraint-aware vSoC balancing and priority-based allocation strategy (CSB-PAS) is proposed for node-level power allocation, improving computational efficiency while respecting user comfort and device constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed approach effectively meets the regulation target and enhances voltage quality. Compared with the complete information game approach, it also improves the total utility by 5.06%.

title: Coordinated supply scheduling of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering power and transportation networks
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Converting offshore wind energy into hydrogen is a promising approach to improving renewable energy utilization. Coordinated offshore and onshore operation can further enhance hydrogen supply flexibility. Despite this potential, most existing studies model offshore hydrogen production and onshore demand delivery separately. This paper therefore proposes a coordinated supply scheduling model of offshore and onshore hydrogen considering both power and hydrogen transportation networks. The model coordinates power system operation with maritime and onshore hydrogen transportation scheduling under network constraints, capturing the spatiotemporal interactions among offshore production, port buffering, onshore production, truck routing, storage operation, and hydrogen refueling demand satisfaction. A time-window mapping method is developed to couple continuous time transportation events with discrete time power and hydrogen scheduling constraints. To handle renewable generation uncertainty, the proposed model is extended into a two-stage stochastic formulation. An accelerated progressive hedging algorithm (PHA) with adaptive penalty updating and stable binary variable fixing is developed to improve the efficiency of solving problems with multiple scenarios. Case studies on modified IEEE 24-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. The proposed accelerated PHA substantially reduces solution time while maintaining negligible deviations in the objective value.

title: Coordinated secondary frequency regulation of thermal power units and feeder loads under high renewable penetration: Joint economy-performance optimization and distribution network PCC power tracking
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: Large-scale integration of high-penetration renewables aggravates net-load fluctuations and brings uncertainties to secondary frequency-regulation demands. Limited by adjustable capacity, ramping capability and operational costs, conventional thermal generating units cannot independently provide frequency-regulation support balancing economic and dynamic performance. Different from existing user-side frequency-regulation schemes relying on end-user authorization, massive communication terminals, aggregator coordination and dedicated compensation-settlement mechanisms, this work exploits voltage-power coupling of feeder loads and grid-controllable voltage-regulation devices to incorporate feeder clusters into the active-power frequency-regulation resource pool. Three core challenges are addressed: quantification of feeder safe adjustable capacity, coordinated command allocation among heterogeneous resources, and sustained Point of Common Coupling (PCC) power tracking over regulation cycles. First, the Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) coefficient of feeder loads is identified via grid-side voltage-driven exogenous excitation. Combined with a Z -bus-based linearized power-flow model, feeder safe adjustable capacity is evaluated subject to full-node voltage constraints. Second, considering discrepancies in cost, tracking accuracy and response speed between continuously-regulated thermal units and feeder clusters, a joint economy-performance command-decomposition model is built. The trade-off solution is obtained using the ε-constraint method, Pareto filtering, TOPSIS evaluation and knee-point identification. Finally, a real-time tracking strategy with disturbance observation and sensitivity-weighted allocation is proposed to mitigate PCC deviations induced by second-scale source-load fluctuations. Simulations verify that the proposed method reduces frequency-regulation costs, improves response accuracy and speed, and enhances PCC tracking and system frequency-support capability while guaranteeing feeder node-voltage security.

title: Data-driven design of hybrid energy systems: Insights from a high-resolution nationwide geospatial assessment
source: ScienceDirect Publication: Applied Energy
abstract: In the United States, roughly 95% of hydrogen is produced via steam methane reforming (SMR) and natural gas is becoming increasingly valuable for other applications such as power generation and export. This study evaluates pathways to diversify supply and lower hydrogen costs through a high-resolution, physics-based, open-source assessment of off-grid hybrid energy systems for electrolytic hydrogen. We resolve plant design, nonlinear electrolyzer performance and degradation, and hydrogen storage across 58,225 sites, executing approximately 173 million simulations that sweep 198 wind-solar-battery configurations, five hydrogen storage options and three electrolyzer CapEx scenarios, to produce geographically resolved design guidance. Key findings: (1) Hybrid and hybrid-battery plants minimize levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) at nearly all sites, with optimal designs consistently oversizing generation relative to electrolyzer capacity. (2) Declining electrolyzer costs simplify plant designs by eliminating batteries, this change in plant design leads to lower capacity factors and shorter stack lives. (3) Electrolyzer cost reductions yield larger LCOH reductions without storage than with buried pipe. (4) Optimal storage adds approximately $0.64/kg on average; buried pipe is never the least-cost option but is widely considered deployable today. Together, these results show that off-grid hybrid energy systems can become increasingly competitive with SMR as electrolyzer CapEx costs fall and indicate where that competitiveness emerges first. Future work should assess advanced dispatch to limit degradation and LCOH, optimize for fixed delivery profiles, and expand to additional electrolyzer types and dispatchable generators to map broader hybridization benefits.

title: The survival paradox of close-in planets orbiting red-clump giants
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Close-in planets orbiting core-helium-burning red-clump giants directly challenge tidal-engulfment theory, which predicts that planets within about 1 au of Sun-like stars should be engulfed during red-giant-branch (RGB) expansion. The existence of such survivors would imply missing physical processes in the late stages of stellar and planetary evolution. Yet only one such “forbidden” planet had been identified to date. Here we report three systems—24 Boo b, HD 12648 b, and TYC 4282-605-1 b—whose host stars are confirmed red-clump giants through asteroseismology, showing that each has already undergone dramatic expansion and contraction following helium ignition. Their planets now reside at orbital separations smaller than the maximum stellar radii attained during the RGB phase, implying that they should not have survived. Among them, 24 Boo b orbits at only 0.183 au with a 30-d period, making it the closest planet known around a red-clump giant. These findings demonstrate that this paradox is not an isolated anomaly but signals the emergence of a class of evolved planetary systems. Their survival defies current models of stellar–planetary coevolution and points to unexplored physics shaping planetary architectures around post-RGB stars.

title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action.

title: m 7 G modification in mRNA cooperates with QKI to promote homologous recombination repair
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: DNA double strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired through distinct pathways, with homologous recombination (HR) favored when DNA ends undergo extensive resection. Although cytoplasmic N7-methylguanosine (m7G)-modified RNA increases after UV-induced single-strand breaks, its role in DSB repair (including HR) remains unclear. Here, we show that m7G-modified RNA accumulates at DSB sites, where it recruits the m7G reader protein Quaking (QKI)5, to selectively promote HR. Mechanistically, QKI5 directly interacts with MRE11 and enhances its DNA binding affinity, thereby facilitating DNA end resection. Depletion of QKI5 impairs recruitment of the MRE11–RAD50–NBS1 complex to DSBs and reduces HR repair efficiency. Moreover, elevated QKI5 expression is associated with resistance to radiotherapy in both mouse models and clinical cohorts. Together, these findings identify the m7G RNA–QKI5–MRE11 axis as a regulator of HR pathway choice and suggest QKI5 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer treatment.

title: System-level reorganization of gene networks underlies the nurse-to-forager transition in honeybees
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
abstract: Division of labor in social insects is enabled by coordinated changes in physiology, neural signaling, and gene regulation, yet it remains unclear to what extent behavioral maturation reflects incremental changes in individual genes and/or a reorganization of transcriptomic regulation at the system level. Here, we analyze the nurse-to-forager transition in worker honeybees ( Apis mellifera ) from a network perspective, treating the transcriptome as a gene–gene correlation system whose global organization reflects collective regulatory states. Using fat body gene expression data across five developmental time points that span an interval of behavioral transition, we construct signed gene–gene correlation networks and quantify their macro- and mesostate properties. We then descend to the level of the gene and construct microstate gene lists of interacting genes. Behavioral maturation of worker honeybees is accompanied by coordinated, nonmonotonic changes in global network structure rather than simple global shifts in interaction strength across the network. Early stages exhibit broadly positive, globally synchronized correlations, whereas later stages show increased modular segregation and the emergence of antagonistic gene–gene relationships. Despite this differentiation, networks remain fully connected with high global efficiency, consistent with a flexible small-world–like organization. Positive correlations primarily support global integration, while negative correlations act as localized, boundary-enforcing constraints. Negative correlations form a structured pattern of antagonism that is sparse and module-specific, occurring primarily between functional gene modules rather than within them. Network layouts and module analyses reveal two polarized, attractor-like regulatory states, a structure recapitulated in a vitellogenin-centered subnetwork and consistent with prior experimental perturbation studies.

title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

title: O-antigen loss modulates meropenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae through metabolic and redox reprogramming
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Carbapenems are last line β lactam antibiotics for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet the adaptive routes by which Enterobacterales survive carbapenem stress remain incompletely understood. Here we show that prolonged subinhibitory meropenem exposure promotes O antigen loss in Klebsiella pneumoniae, predominantly via insertion sequence-mediated disruption of O-antigen biosynthesis genes, thereby enhancing carbapenem resistance. O-antigen deficiency is accompanied by envelope-associated redox remodeling and reprogramming of central metabolism, mitigating meropenem-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and oxidative killing. This adaptation also conferred collateral sensitivity to aminoglycosides, associated with increased outer-membrane electronegativity and altered porin expression that may promote aminoglycoside uptake. Analysis of public genomes further revealed O-antigen locus disruptions in subsets of K. pneumoniae and Escherichia coli isolates. Together, our findings establish O-antigen deficiency as a surface-remodeling adaptation that enhances carbapenem resistance through coordinated metabolic and redox reprogramming, while exposing an aminoglycoside vulnerability that warrants further evaluation.

title: XIST drives X-chromosome inactivation and safeguards female extraembryonic cells in humans
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. The inactive X chromosome displays an atypical chromatin state, lacking DNA methylation and canonical heterochromatin marks. We demonstrate that extraembryonic differentiation and XCI are temporally linked. Using loss of function approaches, we found that XIST is required for XCI establishment in humans. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data (N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.
